meta.blurb_uz: Bennetlar oilasida beshta qiz bor, onasining yagona orzusi — ularni boy kuyovlarga berish. Aqlli va o'tkir tilli Elizabet Bennet mag'rur janob Darsi bilan birinchi uchrashuvdayoq bir-birini yoqtirmay qoladi. Ammo noto'g'ri birinchi taassurotlar, yolg'on va g'urur ortida haqiqiy his-tuyg'ular yashiringan bo'lib chiqadi.
meta.why_uz: Ingliz adabiyotining eng sevimli romanlaridan biri. Dialoglarga boy, kinoya va hazilga to'la. Asl matn — XIX asr boshidagi adabiy ingliz tili: B2–C1 darajadagi o'quvchi uchun lug'at va so'z tarjimasi bilan juda foydali mashq. 61 qisqa bob, har biri 5–15 daqiqa.
meta.author_uz: Jeyn Ostin (1775–1817) — ingliz yozuvchisi. Uning romanlari o'z davridagi o'rta zodagonlar hayoti, nikoh, pul va ijtimoiy mavqe haqida, nozik kinoya bilan yozilgan. «G'urur va xurofot» 1813-yilda chiqqan va bugungacha eng ko'p o'qiladigan kitoblardan biri.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq matn. Roman ingliz tilida yozilgan va jamoat mulki (Project Gutenberg #1342). Matn o'zgartirilmagan; faqat juda uzun xatboshilar o'qish qulay bo'lishi uchun bo'lingan. O'zbekcha parallel tarjima — WordDrop tarjimasi (bosqichma-bosqich qo'shilmoqda); hali tarjima qilinmagan boblarda «Tarjima» tugmasi avtomatik tarjimani ko'rsatadi.

characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet
characters.uz: Elizabet (Lizzi) — ikkinchi qiz, aqlli, hazilkash va mustaqil fikrli. Lekin birinchi taassurotga tez ishonadi.

characters.name: Mr. Darcy
characters.uz: Janob Darsi — juda boy, Pemberli mulki egasi. Mag'rur va sovuq ko'rinadi, aslida halol va saxiy.

characters.name: Jane Bennet
characters.uz: Jeyn — to'ng'ich qiz, juda chiroyli va mehribon, hammada faqat yaxshilik ko'radi.

characters.name: Mr. Bingley
characters.uz: Janob Bingley — boy, quvnoq va ochiq yigit; Jeynni sevib qoladi.

characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Bennet
characters.uz: Ota-ona: ota aqlli, lekin beparvo va kinoyachi; ona esa asabiy va faqat qizlarini erga berishni o'ylaydi.

characters.name: Mr. Wickham
characters.uz: Janob Uikhem — chiroyli ofitser, yoqimli, lekin yolg'onchi va qarzdor.

characters.name: Mr. Collins
characters.uz: Janob Kollinz — ruhoniy, mulk merosxo'ri; yaltoq va kulgili.

characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh
characters.uz: Ledi Ketrin — Darsining xolasi, mag'rur va hamma narsaga aralashadigan boy xonim.

characters.name: Charlotte Lucas
characters.uz: Sharlotta — Elizabetning amaliy dugonasi; sevgi emas, xavfsizlik uchun turmushga chiqadi.

characters.name: Lydia Bennet
characters.uz: Lidiya — eng kichik qiz, o'ylamas va sho'x; oilani sharmandalikka olib keladi.

themes.uz: G'urur — Darsining g'ururi uni boshqalardan uzoqlashtiradi, Elizabetning g'ururi esa uni xato hukmga olib boradi.
Xurofot — birinchi taassurotga asoslangan noto'g'ri fikr. Romanning dastlabki nomi «First Impressions» edi.
Nikoh va pul — o'sha davrda ayollar uchun nikoh ko'pincha yagona iqtisodiy himoya edi.
Ijtimoiy tabaqa — boylik va oila nasl-nasabi odamlarning munosabatini belgilaydi.
O'zini anglash — Elizabet: «Shu lahzagacha men o'zimni bilmagan ekanman».

chapters.title: A Single Man of Good Fortune
chapters.recap_uz: Netherfield Park mulkini boy yosh janob Bingley ijaraga oladi. Missis Bennet beshta qizidan biriga uni kuyov qilmoqchi va erini unga tashrif buyurishga undaydi; janob Bennet esa xotinini masxara qiladi.

paras.en: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
paras.uz: Hamma tomonidan tan olingan bir haqiqat bor: katta boylikka ega bo'ydoq erkakka, albatta, xotin kerak bo'ladi.

paras.en: However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters.
paras.uz: Bunday erkak biror mahallaga endi kelganida uning his-tuyg'ulari yoki qarashlari qanchalik noma'lum bo'lmasin, bu haqiqat atrofdagi oilalarning ongiga shunchalik mustahkam o'rnashganki, uni ularning u yoki bu qizining qonuniy mulki deb hisoblashadi.

paras.en: “My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?”
paras.uz: «Aziz janob Bennet, — dedi bir kuni xonimi unga, — Nezerfild Park nihoyat ijaraga berilganini eshitdingizmi?»

paras.en: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet eshitmaganini aytdi.

paras.en: “But it is,” returned she; “for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it.”
paras.uz: «Lekin berilgan, — dedi xotini, — chunki hozirgina missis Long shu yerda edi va menga hammasini aytib berdi».

paras.en: Mr. Bennet made no answer.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet javob bermadi.

paras.en: “Do you not want to know who has taken it?” cried his wife impatiently.
paras.uz: «Uni kim ijaraga olganini bilishni istamaysizmi?» — deb qichqirdi xotini sabrsizlanib.

paras.en: “You want to tell me, and I have no objection to hearing it.”
paras.uz: «Siz menga aytmoqchisiz, men esa eshitishga qarshi emasman».

paras.en: This was invitation enough.
paras.uz: Bu yetarli taklif edi.

paras.en: “Why, my dear, you must know, Mrs. Long says that Netherfield is taken by a young man of large fortune from the north of England; that he came down on Monday in a chaise and four to see the place, and was so much delighted with it, that he agreed with Mr. Morris immediately; that he is to take possession before Michaelmas, and some of his servants are to be in the house by the end of next week.”
paras.uz: «Bilsangiz, azizim, missis Longning aytishicha, Nezerfildni Angliya shimolidan kelgan katta boylikka ega yosh yigit ijaraga olibdi; u dushanba kuni to'rt otli aravada joyni ko'rgani kelibdi va undan shunchalik zavqlanibdiki, darhol janob Morris bilan kelishibdi; Mikail kunidan oldin ko'chib keladi, xizmatkorlaridan ba'zilari esa kelasi hafta oxirigacha uyda bo'ladi».

paras.en: “What is his name?”
paras.uz: «Ismi nima?»

paras.en: “Bingley.”
paras.uz: «Bingli».

paras.en: “Is he married or single?”
paras.uz: «Uylanganmi yoki bo'ydoqmi?»

paras.en: “Oh! Single, my dear, to be sure! A single man of large fortune; four or five thousand a year. What a fine thing for our girls!”
paras.uz: «Oh! Bo'ydoq, azizim, albatta! Katta boylikka ega bo'ydoq yigit — yiliga to'rt-besh ming funt. Qizlarimiz uchun qanday ajoyib!»

paras.en: “How so? How can it affect them?”
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib? Bu ularga qanday ta'sir qilishi mumkin?»

paras.en: “My dear Mr. Bennet,” replied his wife, “how can you be so tiresome! You must know that I am thinking of his marrying one of them.”
paras.uz: «Aziz janob Bennet, — dedi xotini, — buncha zerikarli bo'lmasangiz! Axir men uning qizlarimizdan biriga uylanishini o'ylayotganimni bilishingiz kerak».

paras.en: “Is that his design in settling here?”
paras.uz: «U bu yerga shu niyat bilan joylashyaptimi?»

paras.en: “Design! Nonsense, how can you talk so! But it is very likely that he may fall in love with one of them, and therefore you must visit him as soon as he comes.”
paras.uz: «Niyat! Bema'nilik, qanday qilib shunday gapirasiz! Lekin u ulardan biriga oshiq bo'lib qolishi juda mumkin, shuning uchun u kelishi bilanoq uning oldiga borishingiz kerak».

paras.en: “I see no occasion for that. You and the girls may go, or you may send them by themselves, which perhaps will be still better, for as you are as handsome as any of them, Mr. Bingley may like you the best of the party.”
paras.uz: «Men bunga hojat ko'rmayapman. Siz va qizlar borishingiz mumkin, yoki ularni o'zlarini yuboring — bu, balki, yanada yaxshiroq bo'lar, chunki siz ulardan birortasidan kam chiroyli emassiz, janob Bingli butun guruhdan sizni eng ko'p yoqtirib qolishi mumkin».

paras.en: “My dear, you flatter me. I certainly have had my share of beauty, but I do not pretend to be anything extraordinary now. When a woman has five grown-up daughters, she ought to give over thinking of her own beauty.”
paras.uz: «Azizim, siz menga xushomad qilyapsiz. To'g'ri, menda ham o'z vaqtida go'zallik bo'lgan, lekin hozir o'zimni g'ayrioddiy deb da'vo qilmayman. Ayolning beshta voyaga yetgan qizi bo'lsa, u o'z go'zalligi haqida o'ylashni bas qilishi kerak».

paras.en: “In such cases, a woman has not often much beauty to think of.”
paras.uz: «Bunday hollarda ayolda o'ylashga arziydigan go'zallik ko'pincha qolmaydi».

paras.en: “But, my dear, you must indeed go and see Mr. Bingley when he comes into the neighbourhood.”
paras.uz: «Lekin, azizim, janob Bingli mahallaga kelganda siz rostdan ham borib uni ko'rishingiz kerak».

paras.en: “It is more than I engage for, I assure you.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, bu men va'da qila oladigan narsadan ortiq».

paras.en: “But consider your daughters. Only think what an establishment it would be for one of them. Sir William and Lady Lucas are determined to go, merely on that account, for in general, you know, they visit no newcomers. Indeed you must go, for it will be impossible for us to visit him if you do not.”
paras.uz: «Lekin qizlaringizni o'ylang. Ulardan biri uchun bu qanday ta'minlangan turmush bo'lishini bir tasavvur qiling. Ser Uilyam va ledi Lukas faqat shu sababli borishga qaror qilishdi, chunki odatda, bilasiz, ular yangi kelganlarga tashrif buyurishmaydi. Rostdan ham borishingiz kerak, chunki agar siz bormasangiz, biz unga tashrif buyura olmaymiz».

paras.en: “You are over-scrupulous, surely. I dare say Mr. Bingley will be very glad to see you; and I will send a few lines by you to assure him of my hearty consent to his marrying whichever he chooses of the girls; though I must throw in a good word for my little Lizzy.”
paras.uz: «Siz haddan tashqari tortinchoqsiz. Ishonamanki, janob Bingli sizni ko'rganidan juda xursand bo'ladi; men esa siz orqali bir necha satr yozib yuboraman: qizlardan qaysi birini tanlasa ham, unga uylanishiga chin dildan roziman, deb. Garchi kichkina Lizzim haqida bir yaxshi so'z qo'shib qo'yishim kerak bo'lsa ham».

paras.en: “I desire you will do no such thing. Lizzy is not a bit better than the others; and I am sure she is not half so handsome as Jane, nor half so good-humoured as Lydia. But you are always giving her the preference.”
paras.uz: «Bunday qilmasligingizni istayman. Lizzi boshqalardan zarracha yaxshi emas; ishonchim komilki, u Jeyndek chiroyli ham, Lidiyadek xushchaqchaq ham emas. Lekin siz doim uni ustun qo'yasiz».

paras.en: “They have none of them much to recommend them,” replied he; “they are all silly and ignorant like other girls; but Lizzy has something more of quickness than her sisters.”
paras.uz: «Ularning hech birida maqtashga arziydigan ko'p narsa yo'q, — dedi u, — hammasi boshqa qizlardek ahmoq va bilimsiz; lekin Lizzi opa-singillaridan ko'ra ziyrakroq».

paras.en: “Mr. Bennet, how can you abuse your own children in such a way? You take delight in vexing me. You have no compassion for my poor nerves.”
paras.uz: «Janob Bennet, qanday qilib o'z bolalaringizni bunday haqorat qila olasiz? Siz meni asabimga tegishdan zavq olasiz. Bechora asablarimga zarracha rahmingiz yo'q».

paras.en: “You mistake me, my dear. I have a high respect for your nerves. They are my old friends. I have heard you mention them with consideration these last twenty years at least.”
paras.uz: «Meni noto'g'ri tushunyapsiz, azizim. Men asablaringizni juda hurmat qilaman. Ular mening eski do'stlarim. Kamida so'nggi yigirma yildan beri siz ularni hurmat bilan tilga olganingizni eshitib kelaman».

paras.en: “Ah, you do not know what I suffer.”
paras.uz: «Ah, siz mening nimalar chekayotganimni bilmaysiz».

paras.en: “But I hope you will get over it, and live to see many young men of four thousand a year come into the neighbourhood.”
paras.uz: «Lekin umid qilamanki, bundan o'tib ketasiz va yiliga to'rt ming funt daromadi bo'lgan ko'plab yigitlarning mahallaga kelishini ko'rish uchun yashaysiz».

paras.en: “It will be no use to us, if twenty such should come, since you will not visit them.”
paras.uz: «Bunday yigitlardan yigirmatasi kelsa ham bizga foydasi yo'q, chunki siz ularning oldiga bormaysiz».

paras.en: “Depend upon it, my dear, that when there are twenty, I will visit them all.”
paras.uz: «Ishonavering, azizim, yigirmatasi bo'lganda, hammasining oldiga boraman».

paras.en: Mr. Bennet was so odd a mixture of quick parts, sarcastic humour, reserve, and caprice, that the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character. Her mind was less difficult to develop. She was a woman of mean understanding, little information, and uncertain temper. When she was discontented, she fancied herself nervous. The business of her life was to get her daughters married; its solace was visiting and news.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet ziyraklik, kinoyali hazil, vazminlik va injiqlikning shunday g'alati aralashmasi ediki, yigirma uch yillik tajriba ham xotiniga uning xarakterini tushunish uchun yetmagan edi. Xotinining fe'l-atvorini tushunish esa qiyin emasdi. U aqli kalta, bilimi oz va fe'li o'zgaruvchan ayol edi. Biror narsadan norozi bo'lsa, o'zini asabiy deb o'ylardi. Uning hayotidagi asosiy ish qizlarini erga berish edi; ovunchog'i esa mehmonga borish va yangiliklar edi.

quiz.why_uz: Boy yosh janob Bingley Netherfield'ni ijaraga oladi.

chapters.title: Mr. Bennet's Surprise
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Bennet aslida Bingleyga birinchilardan bo'lib tashrif buyurgan ekan, lekin buni oilasiga ataylab kech aytadi. Oila xursand bo'lib ketadi.

paras.en: Mr. Bennet was among the earliest of those who waited on Mr. Bingley. He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go; and till the evening after the visit was paid she had no knowledge of it. It was then disclosed in the following manner. Observing his second daughter employed in trimming a hat, he suddenly addressed her with:
paras.uz: Janob Bennet janob Binglining oldiga birinchilardan bo'lib borganlardan edi. U doim unga tashrif buyurishni niyat qilgan, garchi oxirigacha xotinini bormasligiga ishontirib kelgan bo'lsa ham; tashrifdan keyingi oqshomgacha xotini bundan bexabar edi. So'ng bu quyidagicha oshkor bo'ldi. Ikkinchi qizining shlyapani bezatayotganini ko'rib, u birdan unga murojaat qildi:

paras.en: “I hope Mr. Bingley will like it, Lizzy.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, bu janob Bingliga yoqadi, Lizzi».

paras.en: “We are not in a way to know what Mr. Bingley likes,” said her mother resentfully, “since we are not to visit.”
paras.uz: «Janob Bingliga nima yoqishini biz bila olmaymiz, — dedi onasi ranjib, — chunki biz unga tashrif buyurmaymiz».

paras.en: “But you forget, mamma,” said Elizabeth, “that we shall meet him at the assemblies, and that Mrs. Long promised to introduce him.”
paras.uz: «Lekin unutyapsiz, oyijon, — dedi Elizabet, — biz u bilan ballarda uchrashamiz, missis Long esa uni tanishtirishga va'da bergan».

paras.en: “I do not believe Mrs. Long will do any such thing. She has two nieces of her own. She is a selfish, hypocritical woman, and I have no opinion of her.”
paras.uz: «Missis Long bunday qilishiga ishonmayman. Uning o'zining ikkita jiyani bor. U xudbin, ikkiyuzlamachi ayol, men u haqda hech qanday yaxshi fikrda emasman».

paras.en: “No more have I,” said Mr. Bennet; “and I am glad to find that you do not depend on her serving you.”
paras.uz: «Men ham, — dedi janob Bennet, — va uning sizga xizmat qilishiga umid bog'lamayotganingizdan xursandman».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet deigned not to make any reply, but, unable to contain herself, began scolding one of her daughters.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet javob berishni o'ziga ep ko'rmadi, lekin o'zini tutolmay, qizlaridan birini koyiy boshladi.

paras.en: “Don't keep coughing so, Kitty, for Heaven's sake! Have a little compassion on my nerves. You tear them to pieces.”
paras.uz: «Xudo haqqi, buncha yo'talma, Ketti! Asablarimga ozgina rahm qil. Ularni burda-burda qilib yuboryapsan».

paras.en: “Kitty has no discretion in her coughs,” said her father; “she times them ill.”
paras.uz: «Ketti yo'talishda ehtiyotkor emas, — dedi otasi, — vaqtini yomon tanlaydi».

paras.en: “I do not cough for my own amusement,” replied Kitty fretfully. “When is your next ball to be, Lizzy?”
paras.uz: «Men o'zimni ovutish uchun yo'talmayman», — dedi Ketti asabiylashib. — Keyingi baling qachon, Lizzi?»

paras.en: “To-morrow fortnight.”
paras.uz: «Ikki haftadan keyin, ertaga».

paras.en: “Aye, so it is,” cried her mother, “and Mrs. Long does not come back till the day before; so it will be impossible for her to introduce him, for she will not know him herself.”
paras.uz: «Ha, shunday, — deb qichqirdi onasi, — missis Long esa bir kun oldingina qaytadi; demak, uni tanishtira olmaydi, chunki o'zi ham uni tanimaydi».

paras.en: “Then, my dear, you may have the advantage of your friend, and introduce Mr. Bingley to her.”
paras.uz: «Unday bo'lsa, azizim, siz dugonangizdan ustun kelib, janob Binglini unga o'zingiz tanishtirishingiz mumkin».

paras.en: “Impossible, Mr. Bennet, impossible, when I am not acquainted with him myself; how can you be so teasing?”
paras.uz: «Mumkin emas, janob Bennet, mumkin emas, axir o'zim u bilan tanish emasman; qanday qilib bunchalik masxara qilasiz?»

paras.en: “I honour your circumspection. A fortnight's acquaintance is certainly very little. One cannot know what a man really is by the end of a fortnight. But if we do not venture somebody else will; and after all, Mrs. Long and her neices must stand their chance; and, therefore, as she will think it an act of kindness, if you decline the office, I will take it on myself.”
paras.uz: «Ehtiyotkorligingizni hurmat qilaman. Ikki haftalik tanishuv, albatta, juda oz. Ikki hafta ichida odamning aslida qanday ekanini bilib bo'lmaydi. Lekin biz jur'at qilmasak, boshqa kimdir qiladi; oxir-oqibat missis Long va uning jiyanlari ham o'z omadini sinashi kerak; shuning uchun, agar siz bu vazifadan bosh tortsangiz, u buni yaxshilik deb biladi — men uni o'z zimmamga olaman».

paras.en: The girls stared at their father. Mrs. Bennet said only, “Nonsense, nonsense!”
paras.uz: Qizlar otalariga tikilib qolishdi. Missis Bennet faqat: «Bema'nilik, bema'nilik!» — dedi.

paras.en: “What can be the meaning of that emphatic exclamation?” cried he. “Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense? I cannot quite agree with you there. What say you, Mary? For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books and make extracts.”
paras.uz: «Bu qat'iy xitob nimani anglatishi mumkin? — deb xitob qildi u. — Siz tanishtirish odoblarini va ularga beriladigan ahamiyatni bema'nilik deb hisoblaysizmi? Bunga to'liq qo'shila olmayman. Sen nima deysan, Meri? Bilaman, sen chuqur o'ylaydigan yosh xonimsan, katta kitoblar o'qib, ulardan ko'chirmalar olasan».

paras.en: Mary wished to say something sensible, but knew not how.
paras.uz: Meri biror aqlli gap aytmoqchi edi, lekin qanday aytishni bilmadi.

paras.en: “While Mary is adjusting her ideas,” he continued, “let us return to Mr. Bingley.”
paras.uz: «Meri fikrlarini tartibga solguncha, — davom etdi u, — janob Bingliga qaytaylik».

paras.en: “I am sick of Mr. Bingley,” cried his wife.
paras.uz: «Janob Bingli me'damga tegdi», — deb qichqirdi xotini.

paras.en: “I am sorry to hear that; but why did not you tell me that before? If I had known as much this morning I certainly would not have called on him. It is very unlucky; but as I have actually paid the visit, we cannot escape the acquaintance now.”
paras.uz: «Buni eshitganimdan afsusdaman; lekin nega buni avvalroq aytmadingiz? Bugun ertalab shuni bilganimda, uning oldiga aslo bormagan bo'lardim. Juda omadsizlik; lekin men rostdan ham tashrif buyurib qo'yganim uchun, endi tanishuvdan qochib qutula olmaymiz».

paras.en: The astonishment of the ladies was just what he wished; that of Mrs. Bennet perhaps surpassing the rest; though, when the first tumult of joy was over, she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while.
paras.uz: Xonimlarning hayrati aynan u istagandek bo'ldi; missis Bennetniki, ehtimol, hammanikidan oshib tushdi; garchi quvonchning birinchi to'lqini o'tgach, u buni boshidan kutib yurganini e'lon qila boshlagan bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: “How good it was in you, my dear Mr. Bennet! But I knew I should persuade you at last. I was sure you loved your girls too well to neglect such an acquaintance. Well, how pleased I am! and it is such a good joke, too, that you should have gone this morning and never said a word about it till now.”
paras.uz: «Qanday yaxshi ish qildingiz, aziz janob Bennet! Lekin oxiri sizni ko'ndirishimni bilardim. Qizlaringizni bunday tanishuvni e'tiborsiz qoldiradigan darajada sevmasligingizga ishonmasdim. Voy, qanchalik xursandman! Bugun ertalab borib, shu paytgacha bir og'iz ham gapirmaganingiz ham qanday zo'r hazil bo'ldi-ya».

paras.en: “Now, Kitty, you may cough as much as you choose,” said Mr. Bennet; and, as he spoke, he left the room, fatigued with the raptures of his wife.
paras.uz: «Endi, Ketti, istaganingcha yo'talishing mumkin», — dedi janob Bennet va shu gapni aytib, xotinining zavq-shavqidan charchab, xonadan chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: “What an excellent father you have, girls!” said she, when the door was shut. “I do not know how you will ever make him amends for his kindness; or me, either, for that matter. At our time of life it is not so pleasant, I can tell you, to be making new acquaintances every day; but for your sakes, we would do anything. Lydia, my love, though you are the youngest, I dare say Mr. Bingley will dance with you at the next ball.”
paras.uz: «Qanday ajoyib otangiz bor, qizlar! — dedi u eshik yopilgach. — Uning bu yaxshiligi uchun qanday qilib qarzingizni uzasizlar, bilmayman; aytgancha, meniki uchun ham. Bizning yoshimizda har kuni yangi tanishlar orttirish unchalik yoqimli emas, sizga aytib qo'yay; lekin sizlar uchun biz hamma narsaga tayyormiz. Lidiya, jonim, garchi eng kichigi bo'lsang ham, janob Bingli keyingi balda sen bilan raqsga tushishiga ishonaman».

paras.en: “Oh!” said Lydia stoutly, “I am not afraid; for though I am the youngest, I'm the tallest.”
paras.uz: «Oh! — dedi Lidiya dadil. — Men qo'rqmayman; garchi eng kichigi bo'lsam ham, eng bo'ychani menman».

paras.en: The rest of the evening was spent in conjecturing how soon he would return Mr. Bennet's visit, and determining when they should ask him to dinner.
paras.uz: Oqshomning qolgan qismi janob Bingli janob Bennetning tashrifiga qanchalik tez javob tashrifi bilan kelishini taxmin qilish va uni qachon tushlikka taklif qilishni belgilash bilan o'tdi.

gloss.ex: He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go; and till the evening after the visit was paid she…
Bennet perhaps surpassing the rest; though, when the first tumult of joy was over, she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while.
Bennet; and, as he spoke, he left the room, fatigued with the raptures of his wife.
A fortnight's acquaintance is certainly very little.
The astonishment of the ladies was just what he wished; that of Mrs.
Bennet deigned not to make any reply, but, unable to contain herself, began scolding one of her daughters.
Mary wished to say something sensible, but knew not how.

quiz.why_uz: U Bingleyga borib kelgan, lekin oilasini hazil bilan qiynab, oxirida aytadi.

chapters.title: The Meryton Ball
chapters.recap_uz: Balda Bingley quvnoq va hammaga yoqadi, ayniqsa Jeynga. Uning do'sti janob Darsi esa mag'rur ko'rinadi va Elizabetni «chidasa bo'ladi, lekin meni o'ziga tortadigan darajada chiroyli emas» deb rad etadi.

paras.en: Not all that Mrs. Bennet, however, with the assistance of her five daughters, could ask on the subject, was sufficient to draw from her husband any satisfactory description of Mr. Bingley. They attacked him in various ways--with barefaced questions, ingenious suppositions, and distant surmises; but he eluded the skill of them all, and they were at last obliged to accept the second-hand intelligence of their neighbour, Lady Lucas. Her report was highly favourable. Sir William had been delighted with him. He was quite young, wonderfully handsome, extremely agreeable, and, to crown the whole, he meant to be at the next assembly with a large party. Nothing could be more delightful! To be fond of dancing was a certain step towards falling in love; and very lively hopes of Mr. Bingley's heart were entertained.
paras.uz: Biroq missis Bennet besh qizining yordami bilan bu mavzuda nimaiki so'ramasin, eridan janob Bingli haqida qoniqarli ta'rif olishga bularning hammasi yetmadi. Ular unga har tomondan hujum qilishdi — ochiqdan-ochiq savollar, ustalik bilan qilingan taxminlar va uzoqdan shama qilishlar bilan; lekin u hammasining mahoratidan chap berdi va oxiri ular qo'shnilari ledi Lukasdan eshitilgan xabarlarga qanoat qilishga majbur bo'lishdi. Uning xabari juda ijobiy edi. Ser Uilyam undan juda mamnun bo'lib qolgan ekan. U ancha yosh, ajoyib kelishgan, nihoyatda yoqimli ekan va bularning ustiga, keyingi balga katta guruh bilan kelmoqchi ekan. Bundan yoqimliroq narsa bo'lishi mumkin emasdi! Raqsni yaxshi ko'rish oshiq bo'lish sari aniq qadam edi; janob Binglining yuragiga juda katta umidlar bog'landi.

paras.en: “If I can but see one of my daughters happily settled at Netherfield,” said Mrs. Bennet to her husband, “and all the others equally well married, I shall have nothing to wish for.”
paras.uz: «Qizlarimdan birini Nezerfildda baxtli turmush qurgan holda, qolganlarini ham xuddi shunday yaxshi erga tekkan holda ko'rsam, boshqa hech narsa tilamayman», — dedi missis Bennet eriga.

paras.en: In a few days Mr. Bingley returned Mr. Bennet's visit, and sat about ten minutes with him in his library. He had entertained hopes of being admitted to a sight of the young ladies, of whose beauty he had heard much; but he saw only the father. The ladies were somewhat more fortunate, for they had the advantage of ascertaining from an upper window that he wore a blue coat, and rode a black horse.
paras.uz: Bir necha kundan keyin janob Bingli janob Bennetga javob tashrifi bilan keldi va u bilan kutubxonada o'n daqiqacha o'tirdi. U go'zalligi haqida ko'p eshitgan yosh xonimlarni ko'rishga umid qilgan edi; lekin faqat otalarini ko'rdi. Xonimlar biroz omadliroq chiqishdi, chunki yuqori qavatdagi derazadan uning ko'k kamzul kiyganini va qora otda kelganini aniqlab olish imkoniga ega bo'lishdi.

paras.en: An invitation to dinner was soon afterwards dispatched; and already had Mrs. Bennet planned the courses that were to do credit to her housekeeping, when an answer arrived which deferred it all. Mr. Bingley was obliged to be in town the following day, and, consequently, unable to accept the honour of their invitation, etc. Mrs. Bennet was quite disconcerted. She could not imagine what business he could have in town so soon after his arrival in Hertfordshire; and she began to fear that he might be always flying about from one place to another, and never settled at Netherfield as he ought to be.
paras.uz: Ko'p o'tmay tushlikka taklif yuborildi; missis Bennet uy bekaligiga sharaf keltiradigan taomlarni allaqachon rejalashtirib qo'ygan ediki, hammasini keyinga qoldiradigan javob keldi. Janob Bingli ertasi kuni Londonda bo'lishi shart ekan, shuning uchun ularning taklifi sharafini qabul qila olmas ekan va hokazo. Missis Bennet ancha sarosimaga tushdi. Hertfordshirga kelganidan buncha tez Londonda qanday ishi bo'lishi mumkinligini tasavvur qila olmadi; va u doim bir joydan ikkinchisiga uchib yurib, Nezerfildda kerakli darajada hech qachon o'rnashmasligidan qo'rqa boshladi.

paras.en: Lady Lucas quieted her fears a little by starting the idea of his being gone to London only to get a large party for the ball; and a report soon followed that Mr. Bingley was to bring twelve ladies and seven gentlemen with him to the assembly. The girls grieved over such a number of ladies, but were comforted the day before the ball by hearing, that instead of twelve he brought only six with him from London--his five sisters and a cousin. And when the party entered the assembly room it consisted of only five altogether--Mr. Bingley, his two sisters, the husband of the eldest, and another young man.
paras.uz: Ledi Lukas uning qo'rquvini biroz tinchlantirdi: u Londonga faqat bal uchun katta guruh yig'ish maqsadida ketgan bo'lsa kerak, degan fikrni o'rtaga tashladi; ko'p o'tmay janob Bingli balga o'zi bilan o'n ikki xonim va yetti janobni olib kelar emish, degan mish-mish tarqaldi. Qizlar xonimlarning bunchalik ko'pligidan qayg'urishdi, lekin bal arafasida u Londondan o'n ikki emas, atigi olti kishini — besh opa-singlisi va bir amakivachchasini olib kelganini eshitib, tasalli topishdi. Guruh bal zaliga kirganida esa jami besh kishi bo'lib chiqdi: janob Bingli, uning ikki opa-singlisi, kattasining eri va yana bir yosh yigit.

paras.en: Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike; he had a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners. His sisters were fine women, with an air of decided fashion. His brother-in-law, Mr. Hurst, merely looked the gentleman; but his friend Mr. Darcy soon drew the attention of the room by his fine, tall person, handsome features, noble mien, and the report which was in general circulation within five minutes after his entrance, of his having ten thousand a year. The gentlemen pronounced him to be a fine figure of a man, the ladies declared he was much handsomer than Mr. Bingley, and he was looked at with great admiration for about half the evening, till his manners gave a disgust which turned the tide of his popularity; for he was discovered to be proud; to be above his company, and above being pleased; and not all his large estate in Derbyshire could then save him from having a most forbidding, disagreeable countenance, and being unworthy to be compared with his friend.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli kelishgan va asl janoblarga xos edi; yoqimli chehrasi, sodda va tabiiy muomalasi bor edi. Opa-singillari ko'rkam, aniq moda ruhidagi ayollar edi. Pochchasi janob Xerst shunchaki janobga o'xshab turardi; ammo uning do'sti janob Darsi o'zining kelishgan, baland qaddi-qomati, chiroyli yuzi, olijanob qiyofasi va u kirganidan besh daqiqa o'tmay hamma og'ziga tushgan yiliga o'n ming funt daromadi haqidagi gap bilan tezda butun zalning e'tiborini tortdi. Janoblar uni ajoyib erkak deb hukm qilishdi, xonimlar uni janob Binglidan ancha chiroyliroq deb e'lon qilishdi va oqshomning yarmiga yaqin unga katta hayrat bilan qarab turishdi — toki uning xulqi nafrat uyg'otib, mashhurligi teskari tomonga burilmaguncha; chunki u mag'rur, o'z davrasidan o'zini yuqori tutuvchi va hech narsadan mamnun bo'lmaydigan odam ekani ma'lum bo'ldi; shunda Derbishirdagi butun katta mulki ham uni o'ta sovuq, yoqimsiz chehrali va do'sti bilan solishtirishga noloyiq odam deb hisoblanishdan qutqara olmadi.

paras.en: Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room; he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield. Such amiable qualities must speak for themselves. What a contrast between him and his friend! Mr. Darcy danced only once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley, declined being introduced to any other lady, and spent the rest of the evening in walking about the room, speaking occasionally to one of his own party. His character was decided. He was the proudest, most disagreeable man in the world, and everybody hoped that he would never come there again. Amongst the most violent against him was Mrs. Bennet, whose dislike of his general behaviour was sharpened into particular resentment by his having slighted one of her daughters.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli zaldagi barcha asosiy odamlar bilan tezda tanishib oldi; u quvnoq va ochiq edi, har bir raqsga tushdi, bal juda erta tugaganidan achchiqlandi va Nezerfildda o'zi bal berish haqida gapirdi. Bunday yoqimli fazilatlar o'z-o'zidan ko'rinib turardi. Do'sti bilan uning o'rtasida qanday farq! Janob Darsi faqat bir marta missis Xerst bilan, bir marta miss Bingli bilan raqsga tushdi, boshqa biror xonim bilan tanishishni rad etdi va oqshomning qolgan qismini zalda u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurib, vaqti-vaqti bilan o'z guruhidagilardan biri bilan gaplashib o'tkazdi. Uning xarakteri aniq bo'ldi. U dunyodagi eng mag'rur, eng yoqimsiz odam edi va hamma u boshqa hech qachon bu yerga kelmasligini istardi. Unga qarshi eng qattiq gapiruvchilardan biri missis Bennet edi: uning umumiy xulqiga bo'lgan noroziligi qizlaridan birini mensimagani uchun alohida xafagarchilikka aylangan edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth Bennet had been obliged, by the scarcity of gentlemen, to sit down for two dances; and during part of that time, Mr. Darcy had been standing near enough for her to hear a conversation between him and Mr. Bingley, who came from the dance for a few minutes, to press his friend to join it.
paras.uz: Janoblar kamligi sababli Elizabet Bennet ikki raqs davomida o'tirib turishga majbur bo'ldi; shu vaqtning bir qismida janob Darsi unga shunchalik yaqin turdiki, u do'stini raqsga qo'shilishga undash uchun bir necha daqiqaga raqsdan chiqib kelgan janob Bingli bilan uning suhbatini eshitib qoldi.

paras.en: “Come, Darcy,” said he, “I must have you dance. I hate to see you standing about by yourself in this stupid manner. You had much better dance.”
paras.uz: «Qani, Darsi, — dedi u, — seni albatta raqsga tushirishim kerak. Bunday ahmoqona yolg'iz turganingni ko'rishni yomon ko'raman. Raqsga tushganing ancha yaxshi».

paras.en: “I certainly shall not. You know how I detest it, unless I am particularly acquainted with my partner. At such an assembly as this it would be insupportable. Your sisters are engaged, and there is not another woman in the room whom it would not be a punishment to me to stand up with.”
paras.uz: «Aslo tushmayman. Bilasan-ku, sherigim bilan alohida tanish bo'lmasam, buni qanchalik yomon ko'raman. Bunday yig'inda bu chidab bo'lmas bo'lardi. Opa-singillaring band, zalda esa yonida turish men uchun jazo bo'lmaydigan birorta ham ayol yo'q».

paras.en: “I would not be so fastidious as you are,” cried Mr. Bingley, “for a kingdom! Upon my honour, I never met with so many pleasant girls in my life as I have this evening; and there are several of them you see uncommonly pretty.”
paras.uz: «Men sendek tanlab-saralab o'tirmagan bo'lardim, — deb xitob qildi janob Bingli, — hatto butun bir qirollik evaziga ham! Or-nomusim haqqi, hayotimda hech qachon bugun oqshomdagidek ko'p yoqimli qizlarni uchratmaganman; ulardan bir nechtasi, ko'rib turibsan, g'ayrioddiy darajada chiroyli».

paras.en: “You are dancing with the only handsome girl in the room,” said Mr. Darcy, looking at the eldest Miss Bennet.
paras.uz: «Sen zaldagi yagona chiroyli qiz bilan raqsga tushyapsan», — dedi janob Darsi to'ng'ich miss Bennetga qarab.

paras.en: “Oh! She is the most beautiful creature I ever beheld! But there is one of her sisters sitting down just behind you, who is very pretty, and I dare say very agreeable. Do let me ask my partner to introduce you.”
paras.uz: «Oh! U men ko'rgan eng go'zal mavjudot! Lekin uning singillaridan biri aynan orqangda o'tiribdi, u juda chiroyli, ishonamanki, juda yoqimli ham. Ruxsat ber, sherigimdan seni u bilan tanishtirishni so'ray».

paras.en: “Which do you mean?” and turning round he looked for a moment at Elizabeth, till catching her eye, he withdrew his own and coldly said: “She is tolerable, but not handsome enough to tempt me; I am in no humour at present to give consequence to young ladies who are slighted by other men. You had better return to your partner and enjoy her smiles, for you are wasting your time with me.”
paras.uz: «Qaysi birini aytyapsan?» — dedi u va o'girilib bir lahza Elizabetga qaradi, toki uning nigohini ilg'agach, ko'zini olib qochdi va sovuqqonlik bilan dedi: «Chidasa bo'ladi, lekin meni o'ziga tortadigan darajada chiroyli emas; boshqa erkaklar mensimagan yosh xonimlarga ahamiyat berish hozir kayfiyatimda yo'q. Yaxshisi, sherigingning oldiga qaytib, uning tabassumlaridan zavqlan, chunki men bilan vaqtingni behuda o'tkazyapsan».

paras.en: Mr. Bingley followed his advice. Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings toward him. She told the story, however, with great spirit among her friends; for she had a lively, playful disposition, which delighted in anything ridiculous.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli uning maslahatiga amal qildi. Janob Darsi nari ketdi; Elizabet esa unga nisbatan unchalik samimiy bo'lmagan tuyg'ular bilan qoldi. Biroq u bu voqeani dugonalari orasida katta zavq bilan aytib berdi, chunki uning har qanday kulgili narsadan zavqlanadigan quvnoq, sho'x tabiati bor edi.

paras.en: The evening altogether passed off pleasantly to the whole family. Mrs. Bennet had seen her eldest daughter much admired by the Netherfield party. Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters. Jane was as much gratified by this as her mother could be, though in a quieter way. Elizabeth felt Jane's pleasure. Mary had heard herself mentioned to Miss Bingley as the most accomplished girl in the neighbourhood; and Catherine and Lydia had been fortunate enough never to be without partners, which was all that they had yet learnt to care for at a ball. They returned, therefore, in good spirits to Longbourn, the village where they lived, and of which they were the principal inhabitants. They found Mr. Bennet still up. With a book he was regardless of time; and on the present occasion he had a good deal of curiosity as to the event of an evening which had raised such splendid expectations. He had rather hoped that his wife's views on the stranger would be disappointed; but he soon found out that he had a different story to hear.
paras.uz: Umuman olganda, oqshom butun oila uchun yoqimli o'tdi. Missis Bennet to'ng'ich qiziga Nezerfild guruhi katta hayrat bilan qaraganini ko'rdi. Janob Bingli u bilan ikki marta raqsga tushdi, opa-singillari ham unga alohida e'tibor ko'rsatishdi. Jeyn bundan onasi qanchalik mamnun bo'lsa, shunchalik mamnun edi, faqat jimroq tarzda. Elizabet Jeynning quvonchini his qildi. Meri miss Bingliga o'zini mahalladagi eng bilimdon qiz deb tanishtirishganini eshitdi; Ketrin va Lidiya esa birorta ham raqssiz qolmaslik baxtiga muyassar bo'lishdi — ular balda hozircha faqat shuni qadrlashni o'rganishgan edi. Shu bois ular yaxshi kayfiyatda o'zlari yashaydigan va eng obro'li aholisi bo'lgan Longborn qishlog'iga qaytishdi. Janob Bennet hali uxlamagan ekan. Qo'lida kitob bo'lsa, u vaqtni unutardi; bu safar esa shunday ajoyib umidlar uyg'otgan oqshomning qanday o'tgani uni ancha qiziqtirardi. U xotinining notanish yigit haqidagi rejalari barbod bo'lishiga ko'proq umid qilgan edi; lekin tez orada butunlay boshqa hikoyani eshitishiga to'g'ri kelishini angladi.

paras.en: “Oh! my dear Mr. Bennet,” as she entered the room, “we have had a most delightful evening, a most excellent ball. I wish you had been there. Jane was so admired, nothing could be like it. Everybody said how well she looked; and Mr. Bingley thought her quite beautiful, and danced with her twice! Only think of that, my dear; he actually danced with her twice! and she was the only creature in the room that he asked a second time. First of all, he asked Miss Lucas. I was so vexed to see him stand up with her! But, however, he did not admire her at all; indeed, nobody can, you know; and he seemed quite struck with Jane as she was going down the dance. So he inquired who she was, and got introduced, and asked her for the two next. Then the two third he danced with Miss King, and the two fourth with Maria Lucas, and the two fifth with Jane again, and the two sixth with Lizzy, and the Boulanger--”
paras.uz: «Oh! Aziz janob Bennet, — dedi u xonaga kirib, — biz juda yoqimli oqshom o'tkazdik, ajoyib bal bo'ldi. Siz ham bo'lganingizda edi. Jeynga hamma shunday hayrat bilan qaradiki, bunga teng keladigani yo'q. Hamma uning qanchalik chiroyli ko'rinayotganini aytdi; janob Bingli esa uni juda go'zal deb topdi va u bilan ikki marta raqsga tushdi! Bir o'ylab ko'ring, azizim, u rostdan ham u bilan ikki marta raqsga tushdi! U zalda ikkinchi marta taklif qilgan yagona qiz Jeyn bo'ldi. Avval u miss Lukasni taklif qildi. Uning u bilan raqsga chiqqanini ko'rib, qanchalik achchiqlanganimni bilsangiz edi! Lekin baribir u unga umuman mahliyo bo'lmadi; aslida hech kim mahliyo bo'lolmaydi, bilasiz; Jeyn raqsda pastga tushib borayotganda esa u unga butunlay maftun bo'lib qolganday ko'rindi. Shunda u kimligini so'radi, tanishtirildi va keyingi ikki raqsga taklif qildi. Keyin uchinchi ikkitasida miss King bilan, to'rtinchi ikkitasida Mariya Lukas bilan, beshinchi ikkitasida yana Jeyn bilan, oltinchi ikkitasida Lizzi bilan, Bulanjeni esa...»

paras.en: “If he had had any compassion for me,” cried her husband impatiently, “he would not have danced half so much! For God's sake, say no more of his partners. Oh that he had sprained his ankle in the first dance!”
paras.uz: «Agar unda menga zarracha rahm bo'lganida, — deb qichqirdi eri sabrsizlanib, — bunchalik ko'p raqsga tushmagan bo'lardi! Xudo haqqi, uning sheriklari haqida boshqa gapirmang. Qani endi birinchi raqsdayoq oyog'ini chiqarib olgan bo'lsa!»

paras.en: “Oh! my dear, I am quite delighted with him. He is so excessively handsome! And his sisters are charming women. I never in my life saw anything more elegant than their dresses. I dare say the lace upon Mrs. Hurst's gown--”
paras.uz: «Oh! Azizim, men undan juda mamnunman. U nihoyatda kelishgan! Opa-singillari esa maftunkor ayollar. Umrimda ularning ko'ylaklaridan nafisroq narsa ko'rmaganman. Missis Xerstning ko'ylagidagi to'r esa, ishonavering...»

paras.en: Here she was interrupted again. Mr. Bennet protested against any description of finery. She was therefore obliged to seek another branch of the subject, and related, with much bitterness of spirit and some exaggeration, the shocking rudeness of Mr. Darcy.
paras.uz: Shu yerda uning gapi yana bo'lindi. Janob Bennet libos bezaklarining har qanday ta'rifiga qarshi chiqdi. Shuning uchun u mavzuning boshqa tarmog'ini izlashga majbur bo'ldi va katta alam bilan, biroz bo'rttirib, janob Darsining dahshatli qo'polligini hikoya qilib berdi.

paras.en: “But I can assure you,” she added, “that Lizzy does not lose much by not suiting his fancy; for he is a most disagreeable, horrid man, not at all worth pleasing. So high and so conceited that there was no enduring him! He walked here, and he walked there, fancying himself so very great! Not handsome enough to dance with! I wish you had been there, my dear, to have given him one of your set-downs. I quite detest the man.”
paras.uz: «Lekin sizni ishontirib aytamanki, — deb qo'shimcha qildi u, — Lizzi uning didiga mos kelmagani bilan ko'p narsa yo'qotmaydi; chunki u o'ta yoqimsiz, dahshatli odam, unga yoqishga umuman arzimaydi. Shunchalik takabbur va o'ziga bino qo'ygan ediki, unga chidab bo'lmasdi! U yoqqa yurdi, bu yoqqa yurdi, o'zini juda ulug' deb o'ylab! Raqsga tushishga arziydigan darajada chiroyli emas emish! Siz ham bo'lganingizda edi, azizim, unga o'zingizning keskin javoblaringizdan birini bergan bo'lardingiz. Men u odamni butunlay yomon ko'raman».

quiz.why_uz: Avvaliga uning boyligi hammaga yoqadi, keyin mag'rurligi uchun uni yomon ko'rishadi.

chapters.title: Jane and Elizabeth Talk
chapters.recap_uz: Jeyn Bingleyni yoqtirganini tan oladi. Elizabet opasining hammada faqat yaxshilik ko'rishini aytadi. Bingley va Darsining do'stligi, xarakterlari solishtiriladi.

paras.en: When Jane and Elizabeth were alone, the former, who had been cautious in her praise of Mr. Bingley before, expressed to her sister just how very much she admired him.
paras.uz: Jeyn va Elizabet yolg'iz qolishganda, avval janob Binglini maqtashda ehtiyotkor bo'lgan Jeyn singlisiga undan naqadar mahliyo bo'lganini izhor qildi.

paras.en: “He is just what a young man ought to be,” said she, “sensible, good-humoured, lively; and I never saw such happy manners!--so much ease, with such perfect good breeding!”
paras.uz: «U yosh yigit qanday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, aynan shunday, — dedi u, — aqlli, xushfe'l, quvnoq; men hech qachon bunday yoqimli muomalani ko'rmaganman! Shunchalik erkinlik va shu bilan birga shunday mukammal tarbiya!»

paras.en: “He is also handsome,” replied Elizabeth, “which a young man ought likewise to be, if he possibly can. His character is thereby complete.”
paras.uz: «U kelishgan ham, — dedi Elizabet, — yosh yigit iloji bo'lsa, shunday ham bo'lishi kerak. Shu bilan uning xarakteri mukammal bo'ladi».

paras.en: “I was very much flattered by his asking me to dance a second time. I did not expect such a compliment.”
paras.uz: «Uning meni ikkinchi marta raqsga taklif qilgani menga juda yoqdi. Bunday iltifotni kutmagandim».

paras.en: “Did not you? I did for you. But that is one great difference between us. Compliments always take you by surprise, and me never. What could be more natural than his asking you again? He could not help seeing that you were about five times as pretty as every other woman in the room. No thanks to his gallantry for that. Well, he certainly is very agreeable, and I give you leave to like him. You have liked many a stupider person.”
paras.uz: «Kutmaganmiding? Men sen uchun kutgandim. Lekin oramizdagi katta farqlardan biri shu. Iltifotlar seni doim hayratda qoldiradi, meni esa hech qachon. Uning seni yana taklif qilishidan tabiiyroq narsa bo'lishi mumkinmi? U sening zaldagi boshqa har qanday ayoldan besh barobarcha chiroyliroq ekaningni ko'rmay qolishi mumkin emasdi. Buning uchun uning xushmuomalaligiga rahmat aytish shart emas. Mayli, u, albatta, juda yoqimli, men senga uni yoqtirishga ruxsat beraman. Sen bundan ham ahmoqroq odamlarni ko'p yoqtirgansan».

paras.en: “Dear Lizzy!”
paras.uz: «Aziz Lizzi!»

paras.en: “Oh! you are a great deal too apt, you know, to like people in general. You never see a fault in anybody. All the world are good and agreeable in your eyes. I never heard you speak ill of a human being in your life.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Bilasanmi, sen umuman odamlarni yoqtirishga haddan tashqari moyilsan. Hech kimda kamchilik ko'rmaysan. Sening nazaringda butun dunyo yaxshi va yoqimli. Umrimda bironta odam haqida yomon gapirganingni eshitmaganman».

paras.en: “I would not wish to be hasty in censuring anyone; but I always speak what I think.”
paras.uz: «Men hech kimni shoshib ayblashni istamayman; lekin doim o'ylaganimni aytaman».

paras.en: “I know you do; and it is that which makes the wonder. With your good sense, to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others! Affectation of candour is common enough--one meets with it everywhere. But to be candid without ostentation or design--to take the good of everybody's character and make it still better, and say nothing of the bad--belongs to you alone. And so you like this man's sisters, too, do you? Their manners are not equal to his.”
paras.uz: «Bilaman, aytasan; ajablanarlisi ham shunda. Sendek aqlli odam boshqalarning ahmoqligi va bema'niliklariga shunchalik samimiy ko'r bo'lishi! Samimiy bo'lib ko'rinish odatiy hol — uni hamma joyda uchratish mumkin. Lekin ko'z-ko'z qilmasdan va g'arazsiz samimiy bo'lish — har kimning xarakteridagi yaxshi tomonni olib, uni yanada yaxshilash va yomoni haqida hech narsa demaslik — faqat senga xos. Demak, sen bu yigitning opa-singillarini ham yoqtirasan, shundaymi? Ularning muomalasi unikiga teng emas».

paras.en: “Certainly not--at first. But they are very pleasing women when you converse with them. Miss Bingley is to live with her brother, and keep his house; and I am much mistaken if we shall not find a very charming neighbour in her.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, emas — avvaliga. Lekin ular bilan suhbatlashsang, juda yoqimli ayollar. Miss Bingli akasi bilan birga yashab, uning uy-ro'zg'orini boshqaradi; agar u bizga juda maftunkor qo'shni bo'lib chiqmasa, qattiq adashgan bo'laman».

paras.en: Elizabeth listened in silence, but was not convinced; their behaviour at the assembly had not been calculated to please in general; and with more quickness of observation and less pliancy of temper than her sister, and with a judgement too unassailed by any attention to herself, she was very little disposed to approve them. They were in fact very fine ladies; not deficient in good humour when they were pleased, nor in the power of making themselves agreeable when they chose it, but proud and conceited. They were rather handsome, had been educated in one of the first private seminaries in town, had a fortune of twenty thousand pounds, were in the habit of spending more than they ought, and of associating with people of rank, and were therefore in every respect entitled to think well of themselves, and meanly of others. They were of a respectable family in the north of England; a circumstance more deeply impressed on their memories than that their brother's fortune and their own had been acquired by trade.
paras.uz: Elizabet jim tinglab turdi, lekin ishonmadi; ularning baldagi xulqi umuman hammaga yoqishga qaratilmagan edi; opasidan ko'ra ziyrakroq kuzatuvchan, fe'li kamroq yumshoq bo'lgani va hukmiga o'ziga ko'rsatilgan biror e'tibor ta'sir qilmagani uchun u ularni ma'qullashga unchalik moyil emasdi. Ular haqiqatan ham juda nafis xonimlar edi; xursand bo'lganlarida xushfe'llikdan ham, istasalar o'zlarini yoqimli ko'rsata olishdan ham mahrum emasdilar, lekin mag'rur va o'zlariga bino qo'ygan edilar. Ular ancha chiroyli edilar, Londondagi eng yaxshi xususiy pansionlardan birida tahsil olgan, yigirma ming funt boyligi bor, keragidan ko'p pul sarflashga va yuqori tabaqa vakillari bilan yurishga odatlangan edilar va shuning uchun har jihatdan o'zlari haqida yaxshi, boshqalar haqida past fikrda bo'lishga haqli edilar. Ular Angliya shimolidagi obro'li oiladan edi — bu holat ularning xotirasiga akalari va o'zlarining boyligi savdo orqali topilganidan ko'ra chuqurroq o'rnashgan edi.

paras.en: Mr. Bingley inherited property to the amount of nearly a hundred thousand pounds from his father, who had intended to purchase an estate, but did not live to do it. Mr. Bingley intended it likewise, and sometimes made choice of his county; but as he was now provided with a good house and the liberty of a manor, it was doubtful to many of those who best knew the easiness of his temper, whether he might not spend the remainder of his days at Netherfield, and leave the next generation to purchase.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli otasidan yuz ming funtga yaqin mulkni meros qilib olgan edi; otasi yer-mulk sotib olishni niyat qilgan, lekin bunga umri yetmagan edi. Janob Bingli ham shu niyatda edi va ba'zan grafligini ham tanlab qo'yardi; lekin endi unda yaxshi uy va mulkda ov qilish huquqi bo'lgani uchun, uning beg'am fe'lini yaxshi biladiganlarning ko'pchiligi u qolgan umrini Nezerfildda o'tkazib, sotib olishni keyingi avlodga qoldirmasmikan, deb shubhalanardi.

paras.en: His sisters were anxious for his having an estate of his own; but, though he was now only established as a tenant, Miss Bingley was by no means unwilling to preside at his table--nor was Mrs. Hurst, who had married a man of more fashion than fortune, less disposed to consider his house as her home when it suited her. Mr. Bingley had not been of age two years, when he was tempted by an accidental recommendation to look at Netherfield House. He did look at it, and into it for half-an-hour--was pleased with the situation and the principal rooms, satisfied with what the owner said in its praise, and took it immediately.
paras.uz: Opa-singillari uning o'z mulki bo'lishini juda istashardi; lekin u hozircha faqat ijarachi bo'lsa ham, miss Bingli uning dasturxoniga boshchilik qilishga aslo qarshi emasdi — boylikdan ko'ra ko'proq moda ruhidagi odamga turmushga chiqqan missis Xerst ham, o'ziga qulay bo'lganda, uning uyini o'z uyi deb bilishga kam moyil emasdi. Janob Bingli voyaga yetganiga hali ikki yil to'lmagan ediki, tasodifiy tavsiya uni Nezerfild uyini ko'rishga undadi. U uni ko'rdi, yarim soatcha ichini ham aylanib chiqdi — joylashuvi va asosiy xonalari unga yoqdi, egasining maqtovlari qoniqtirdi va uni darhol ijaraga oldi.

paras.en: Between him and Darcy there was a very steady friendship, in spite of great opposition of character. Bingley was endeared to Darcy by the easiness, openness, and ductility of his temper, though no disposition could offer a greater contrast to his own, and though with his own he never appeared dissatisfied. On the strength of Darcy's regard, Bingley had the firmest reliance, and of his judgement the highest opinion. In understanding, Darcy was the superior. Bingley was by no means deficient, but Darcy was clever. He was at the same time haughty, reserved, and fastidious, and his manners, though well-bred, were not inviting. In that respect his friend had greatly the advantage. Bingley was sure of being liked wherever he appeared, Darcy was continually giving offense.
paras.uz: U bilan Darsi o'rtasida xarakterlarining katta qarama-qarshiligiga qaramay, juda mustahkam do'stlik bor edi. Bingli Darsiga o'zining beg'amligi, ochiqligi va yumshoq fe'li bilan aziz edi, garchi hech qanday tabiat Darsinikiga bundan kattaroq qarama-qarshi bo'la olmasa ham va garchi Darsi o'z tabiatidan hech qachon norozi ko'rinmasa ham. Bingli Darsining hurmatiga qattiq ishonar va uning hukmini juda yuqori qadrlardi. Aql-idrokda Darsi ustun edi. Bingli aslo kamaqlli emasdi, lekin Darsi zukko edi. Shu bilan birga u takabbur, odamovi va o'ta tanlab ish tutuvchi edi, muomalasi esa tarbiyali bo'lsa ham, odamni o'ziga tortmasdi. Bu jihatdan do'sti undan ancha ustun edi. Bingli qayerda paydo bo'lmasin, uni yoqtirishlariga ishonchi komil edi, Darsi esa tinimsiz odamlarni ranjitardi.

paras.en: The manner in which they spoke of the Meryton assembly was sufficiently characteristic. Bingley had never met with more pleasant people or prettier girls in his life; everybody had been most kind and attentive to him; there had been no formality, no stiffness; he had soon felt acquainted with all the room; and, as to Miss Bennet, he could not conceive an angel more beautiful. Darcy, on the contrary, had seen a collection of people in whom there was little beauty and no fashion, for none of whom he had felt the smallest interest, and from none received either attention or pleasure. Miss Bennet he acknowledged to be pretty, but she smiled too much.
paras.uz: Ularning Meriton balasi haqida qanday gapirgani ham ularning xarakterini yaxshi ko'rsatardi. Bingli umrida bundan yoqimliroq odamlar yoki chiroyliroq qizlarni uchratmagan edi; hamma unga juda mehribon va e'tiborli bo'lgan; hech qanday rasmiyatchilik, hech qanday qotib qolganlik bo'lmagan; u tezda butun zal bilan tanishdek his qilgan; miss Bennetga kelsak, undan go'zalroq farishtani tasavvur qila olmasdi. Darsi esa, aksincha, unchalik go'zallik va hech qanday moda bo'lmagan odamlar to'plamini ko'rgan edi; ularning hech biriga zarracha qiziqish sezmagan va hech biridan na e'tibor, na zavq olgan edi. Miss Bennetni chiroyli deb tan oldi, lekin u haddan tashqari ko'p jilmayar ekan.

paras.en: Mrs. Hurst and her sister allowed it to be so--but still they admired her and liked her, and pronounced her to be a sweet girl, and one whom they would not object to know more of. Miss Bennet was therefore established as a sweet girl, and their brother felt authorized by such commendation to think of her as he chose.
paras.uz: Missis Xerst va singlisi bunga qo'shilishdi — lekin baribir undan mahliyo bo'lishdi, uni yoqtirishdi va uni shirin qiz deb, u bilan yaqinroq tanishishga qarshi emasliklarini aytishdi. Shunday qilib, miss Bennet shirin qiz deb e'tirof etildi va akalari bunday maqtovdan keyin u haqida xohlaganicha o'ylashga o'zini haqli deb bildi.

said she, “sensible, good-humoured, lively; and I never saw such happy manners!--so much ease, with such perfect good breeding!”

gloss.uz: samimiylik, hammaga yaxshi ko'z bilan qarash

quiz.q: What is Jane's typical way of seeing people?
o: She sees only good in everyone
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet buni opasining samimiyligi va soddaligi deb biladi.

quiz.q: How are Bingley and Darcy different?
o: Bingley is easy and open, Darcy is clever but proud
quiz.why_uz: Bingley ochiq va yoqimli, Darsi esa aqlli, lekin sovuq va mag'rur.

chapters.title: The Lucases
chapters.recap_uz: Lukaslar oilasi bal haqida gaplashishadi. Sharlotta Lukas Darsining mag'rurligini tushunsa bo'ladi deydi, Elizabet esa: «Agar u mening g'ururimni yerga urmaganida, men uning g'ururini kechirardim», deydi.

paras.en: Within a short walk of Longbourn lived a family with whom the Bennets were particularly intimate. Sir William Lucas had been formerly in trade in Meryton, where he had made a tolerable fortune, and risen to the honour of knighthood by an address to the king during his mayoralty. The distinction had perhaps been felt too strongly. It had given him a disgust to his business, and to his residence in a small market town; and, in quitting them both, he had removed with his family to a house about a mile from Meryton, denominated from that period Lucas Lodge, where he could think with pleasure of his own importance, and, unshackled by business, occupy himself solely in being civil to all the world. For, though elated by his rank, it did not render him supercilious; on the contrary, he was all attention to everybody. By nature inoffensive, friendly, and obliging, his presentation at St. James's had made him courteous.
paras.uz: Longborndan unchalik uzoq bo'lmagan joyda Bennetlar ayniqsa yaqin bo'lgan bir oila yashardi. Ser Uilyam Lukas ilgari Meritonda savdo bilan shug'ullangan, u yerda yetarlicha boylik orttirgan va shahar hokimi bo'lgan paytida qirolga murojaatnoma topshirgani uchun ritsarlik unvoniga sazovor bo'lgan edi. Bu sharafni u, ehtimol, haddan tashqari kuchli his qilgandir. U undan savdo ishidan ham, kichik bozor shaharchasida yashashdan ham bezdirgan edi; ikkalasini ham tashlab, u oilasi bilan Meritondan bir milcha uzoqdagi uyga ko'chib o'tdi; o'shandan beri uy Lukas Lodj deb ataladi; u yerda u o'z ahamiyati haqida zavq bilan o'ylashi va ishdan ozod bo'lib, faqat butun dunyoga xushmuomala bo'lish bilan mashg'ul bo'lishi mumkin edi. Chunki unvon uni mag'rurlantirgan bo'lsa ham, takabbur qilmagan edi; aksincha, u hammaga juda e'tiborli edi. Tabiatan beozor, do'stona va xizmatga tayyor odam bo'lgan bu kishini Sent-Jeyms saroyida qirolga tanishtirilgani yanada xushmuomala qilgan edi.

paras.en: Lady Lucas was a very good kind of woman, not too clever to be a valuable neighbour to Mrs. Bennet. They had several children. The eldest of them, a sensible, intelligent young woman, about twenty-seven, was Elizabeth's intimate friend.
paras.uz: Ledi Lukas juda yaxshi ayol edi — missis Bennetga qadrli qo'shni bo'lish uchun haddan tashqari aqlli ham emasdi. Ularning bir necha farzandi bor edi. Ularning to'ng'ichi, yigirma yetti yoshlardagi aqlli, zakovatli yosh ayol, Elizabetning yaqin dugonasi edi.

paras.en: That the Miss Lucases and the Miss Bennets should meet to talk over a ball was absolutely necessary; and the morning after the assembly brought the former to Longbourn to hear and to communicate.
paras.uz: Lukas qizlari bilan Bennet qizlari bal haqida gaplashish uchun uchrashishi mutlaqo zarur edi; baldan keyingi tongda Lukas qizlari eshitish va gapirib berish uchun Longbornga kelishdi.

paras.en: “You began the evening well, Charlotte,” said Mrs. Bennet with civil self-command to Miss Lucas. “You were Mr. Bingley's first choice.”
paras.uz: «Siz oqshomni yaxshi boshladingiz, Sharlotta, — dedi missis Bennet o'zini xushmuomala tutib miss Lukasga. — Siz janob Binglining birinchi tanlovi bo'ldingiz».

paras.en: “Yes; but he seemed to like his second better.”
paras.uz: «Ha; lekin ikkinchisi unga ko'proq yoqqanga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Oh! you mean Jane, I suppose, because he danced with her twice. To be sure that did seem as if he admired her--indeed I rather believe he did--I heard something about it--but I hardly know what--something about Mr. Robinson.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Siz Jeynni nazarda tutyapsiz shekilli, chunki u bilan ikki marta raqsga tushdi. To'g'ri, bu u unga mahliyo bo'lganday ko'rinardi — aslida shunday bo'lganiga ishonaman ham — bu haqda nimadir eshitgandim — lekin nima ekanini aniq bilmayman — janob Robinson haqida nimadir».

paras.en: “Perhaps you mean what I overheard between him and Mr. Robinson; did not I mention it to you? Mr. Robinson's asking him how he liked our Meryton assemblies, and whether he did not think there were a great many pretty women in the room, and which he thought the prettiest? and his answering immediately to the last question: 'Oh! the eldest Miss Bennet, beyond a doubt; there cannot be two opinions on that point.'”
paras.uz: «Balki men uning janob Robinson bilan suhbatidan eshitib qolgan narsamni aytyapsizdir; sizga aytmaganmidim? Janob Robinson undan Meriton ballarimiz qanday yoqqanini, zalda chiroyli ayollar juda ko'p deb o'ylamaydimi va kimni eng chiroyli deb hisoblashini so'radi; u esa oxirgi savolga darhol javob berdi: „Oh! To'ng'ich miss Bennet, shubhasiz; bu masalada ikki xil fikr bo'lishi mumkin emas“».

paras.en: “Upon my word! Well, that is very decided indeed--that does seem as if--but, however, it may all come to nothing, you know.”
paras.uz: «Rostdanmi! Mana bu juda aniq-ku — bu xuddi... lekin baribir hammasi hech narsa bilan tugashi mumkin, bilasiz».

paras.en: “My overhearings were more to the purpose than yours, Eliza,” said Charlotte. “Mr. Darcy is not so well worth listening to as his friend, is he?--poor Eliza!--to be only just tolerable.”
paras.uz: «Mening eshitib qolganim siznikidan ko'ra o'rinliroq bo'ldi, Eliza, — dedi Sharlotta. — Janob Darsini tinglash do'stinikichalik arzimaydi, shunday emasmi? Bechora Eliza! Atigi „chidasa bo'ladi“ ekan».

paras.en: “I beg you would not put it into Lizzy's head to be vexed by his ill-treatment, for he is such a disagreeable man, that it would be quite a misfortune to be liked by him. Mrs. Long told me last night that he sat close to her for half-an-hour without once opening his lips.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, Lizzining boshiga uning qo'polligidan xafa bo'lish fikrini solmang, chunki u shunday yoqimsiz odamki, uning yoqtirishi chinakam baxtsizlik bo'lardi. Missis Long kecha menga aytdi: u yarim soat uning yonida o'tirib, bir marta ham og'iz ochmabdi».

paras.en: “Are you quite sure, ma'am?--is not there a little mistake?” said Jane. “I certainly saw Mr. Darcy speaking to her.”
paras.uz: «Ishonchingiz komilmi, xonim? Biroz xato emasmi? — dedi Jeyn. — Men janob Darsining u bilan gaplashayotganini aniq ko'rdim».

paras.en: “Aye--because she asked him at last how he liked Netherfield, and he could not help answering her; but she said he seemed quite angry at being spoke to.”
paras.uz: «Ha — chunki oxiri u undan Nezerfild qanday yoqayotganini so'radi, u esa javob bermay ilojsiz qoldi; lekin uning aytishicha, u o'zi bilan gaplashishganidan juda jahli chiqqanday ko'rinibdi».

paras.en: “Miss Bingley told me,” said Jane, “that he never speaks much, unless among his intimate acquaintances. With them he is remarkably agreeable.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bingli menga aytdi, — dedi Jeyn, — u yaqin tanishlari orasida bo'lmasa, hech qachon ko'p gapirmas ekan. Ular bilan esa juda yoqimli ekan».

paras.en: “I do not believe a word of it, my dear. If he had been so very agreeable, he would have talked to Mrs. Long. But I can guess how it was; everybody says that he is eat up with pride, and I dare say he had heard somehow that Mrs. Long does not keep a carriage, and had come to the ball in a hack chaise.”
paras.uz: «Bunga bir so'z ham ishonmayman, azizim. Agar u shunchalik yoqimli bo'lganida, missis Long bilan gaplashgan bo'lardi. Lekin qanday bo'lganini taxmin qila olaman: hamma uni g'urur yeb tashlagan deydi; u qandaydir yo'l bilan missis Longning o'z aravasi yo'qligini va balga ijaraga olingan aravada kelganini eshitgan bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “I do not mind his not talking to Mrs. Long,” said Miss Lucas, “but I wish he had danced with Eliza.”
paras.uz: «Uning missis Long bilan gaplashmagani menga baribir, — dedi miss Lukas, — lekin Eliza bilan raqsga tushganida edi».

paras.en: “Another time, Lizzy,” said her mother, “I would not dance with him, if I were you.”
paras.uz: «Boshqa safar, Lizzi, — dedi onasi, — men sening o'rningda bo'lsam, u bilan raqsga tushmasdim».

paras.en: “I believe, ma'am, I may safely promise you never to dance with him.”
paras.uz: «O'ylaymanki, xonim, sizga u bilan hech qachon raqsga tushmaslikni bemalol va'da qila olaman».

paras.en: “His pride,” said Miss Lucas, “does not offend me so much as pride often does, because there is an excuse for it. One cannot wonder that so very fine a young man, with family, fortune, everything in his favour, should think highly of himself. If I may so express it, he has a right to be proud.”
paras.uz: «Uning g'ururi, — dedi miss Lukas, — g'urur odatda ranjitganchalik meni ranjitmaydi, chunki uning uchun uzr bor. Oilasi, boyligi — hamma narsa uning foydasiga bo'lgan shunday ajoyib yigitning o'zi haqida yuqori fikrda bo'lishiga hayron bo'lib bo'lmaydi. Agar shunday deyish mumkin bo'lsa, uning mag'rur bo'lishga haqqi bor».

paras.en: “That is very true,” replied Elizabeth, “and I could easily forgive his pride, if he had not mortified mine.”
paras.uz: «Bu juda to'g'ri, — dedi Elizabet, — agar u mening g'ururimni yerga urmaganida, men uning g'ururini osongina kechirgan bo'lardim».

paras.en: “Pride,” observed Mary, who piqued herself upon the solidity of her reflections, “is a very common failing, I believe. By all that I have ever read, I am convinced that it is very common indeed; that human nature is particularly prone to it, and that there are very few of us who do not cherish a feeling of self-complacency on the score of some quality or other, real or imaginary. Vanity and pride are different things, though the words are often used synonymously. A person may be proud without being vain. Pride relates more to our opinion of ourselves, vanity to what we would have others think of us.”
paras.uz: «G'urur, — dedi o'z mulohazalarining puxtaligi bilan faxrlanadigan Meri, — menimcha, juda keng tarqalgan kamchilik. O'qigan hamma narsamga asoslanib, men uning haqiqatan ham juda keng tarqalganiga, inson tabiati ayniqsa unga moyil ekaniga va qandaydir fazilati — haqiqiy yoki xayoliy — tufayli o'zidan mamnunlik tuyg'usini qalbida asramaydigan odam oramizda juda kam ekaniga aminman. Manmanlik va g'urur — turli narsalar, garchi bu so'zlar ko'pincha bir xil ma'noda ishlatilsa ham. Odam manman bo'lmasdan mag'rur bo'lishi mumkin. G'urur ko'proq o'zimiz haqidagi fikrimizga, manmanlik esa boshqalar biz haqimizda nima deb o'ylashini istashimizga tegishli».

paras.en: “If I were as rich as Mr. Darcy,” cried a young Lucas, who came with his sisters, “I should not care how proud I was. I would keep a pack of foxhounds, and drink a bottle of wine a day.”
paras.uz: «Agar men janob Darsidek boy bo'lganimda, — deb qichqirdi opa-singillari bilan kelgan yosh Lukas, — qanchalik mag'rur bo'lishim menga baribir bo'lardi. Bir to'da tulki ovlaydigan it boqib, kuniga bir shisha vino ichardim».

paras.en: “Then you would drink a great deal more than you ought,” said Mrs. Bennet; “and if I were to see you at it, I should take away your bottle directly.”
paras.uz: «Unda keragidan ancha ko'p ichgan bo'lardingiz, — dedi missis Bennet, — agar sizni shu ishda ko'rsam, shishangizni darhol olib qo'yardim».

paras.en: The boy protested that she should not; she continued to declare that she would, and the argument ended only with the visit.
paras.uz: Bola bunday qila olmasligini aytib e'tiroz bildirdi; u esa olib qo'yishini takrorlayverdi va bahs faqat mehmonlar ketgandagina tugadi.

gloss.ex: Within a short walk of Longbourn lived a family with whom the Bennets were particularly intimate.

o: Pride is our opinion of ourselves, vanity is what we want others to think of us
Vanity is good, pride is bad
