quiz.why_uz: Sharlotta — Elizabetning aqlli va amaliy dugonasi.

chapters.title: Darcy Begins to Notice
chapters.recap_uz: Bingley Jeynga tobora ko'ngil qo'yadi. Sharlotta Jeynga his-tuyg'ularini ko'proq ko'rsatish kerakligini aytadi. Darsi esa Elizabetning chiroyli ko'zlarini sezib, unga qiziqib qoladi.

paras.en: The ladies of Longbourn soon waited on those of Netherfield. The visit was soon returned in due form. Miss Bennet's pleasing manners grew on the goodwill of Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley; and though the mother was found to be intolerable, and the younger sisters not worth speaking to, a wish of being better acquainted with them was expressed towards the two eldest. By Jane, this attention was received with the greatest pleasure, but Elizabeth still saw superciliousness in their treatment of everybody, hardly excepting even her sister, and could not like them; though their kindness to Jane, such as it was, had a value as arising in all probability from the influence of their brother's admiration.
paras.uz: Longborn xonimlari tez orada Nezerfild xonimlarining oldiga tashrif buyurishdi. Javob tashrifi ham tez orada odob bo'yicha amalga oshirildi. Miss Bennetning yoqimli muomalasi missis Xerst va miss Binglining xayrixohligini tobora orttirdi; garchi onasi chidab bo'lmaydigan, kichik singillari esa gaplashishga arzimaydigan deb topilgan bo'lsa ham, ikki kattasi bilan yaqinroq tanishish istagi bildirildi. Jeyn bu e'tiborni katta mamnuniyat bilan qabul qildi, Elizabet esa hamon ularning hammaga, hatto opasiga ham deyarli istisnosiz takabburlik bilan munosabatda bo'layotganini ko'rar va ularni yoqtira olmasdi; garchi ularning Jeynga ko'rsatgan mehribonligi, qanday bo'lmasin, qimmatli edi, chunki u, katta ehtimol bilan, akalarining mahliyoligi ta'sirida paydo bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: It was generally evident whenever they met, that he did admire her and to her it was equally evident that Jane was yielding to the preference which she had begun to entertain for him from the first, and was in a way to be very much in love; but she considered with pleasure that it was not likely to be discovered by the world in general, since Jane united, with great strength of feeling, a composure of temper and a uniform cheerfulness of manner which would guard her from the suspicions of the impertinent. She mentioned this to her friend Miss Lucas.
paras.uz: Ular har uchrashganda u Jeynga mahliyo ekani umuman ochiq-oydin ko'rinib turardi; Elizabetga esa Jeyn ham unga boshidanoq his qila boshlagan moyilligiga berilib borayotgani va qattiq sevib qolish arafasida ekani xuddi shunday aniq edi; lekin u buni umuman olganda dunyo payqamasligini mamnuniyat bilan o'ylardi, chunki Jeyn kuchli his-tuyg'ularni vazmin fe'l va doimiy quvnoq muomala bilan uyg'unlashtirardi — bu uni surbet odamlarning shubhalaridan himoya qilardi. U buni dugonasi miss Lukasga aytdi.

paras.en: “It may perhaps be pleasant,” replied Charlotte, “to be able to impose on the public in such a case; but it is sometimes a disadvantage to be so very guarded. If a woman conceals her affection with the same skill from the object of it, she may lose the opportunity of fixing him; and it will then be but poor consolation to believe the world equally in the dark. There is so much of gratitude or vanity in almost every attachment, that it is not safe to leave any to itself. We can all begin freely--a slight preference is natural enough; but there are very few of us who have heart enough to be really in love without encouragement. In nine cases out of ten a women had better show more affection than she feels. Bingley likes your sister undoubtedly; but he may never do more than like her, if she does not help him on.”
paras.uz: «Bunday holatda omma ko'zini bo'yashga qodir bo'lish, balki, yoqimlidir, — dedi Sharlotta, — lekin ba'zan bunchalik ehtiyotkor bo'lish zararli. Agar ayol o'z mehrini uning egasidan ham xuddi shunday mahorat bilan yashirsa, uni o'ziga bog'lash imkonini qo'ldan boy berishi mumkin; shunda dunyo ham xuddi shunday bexabar ekaniga ishonish arzimas tasalli bo'ladi. Deyarli har bir bog'lanishda minnatdorlik yoki manmanlik shunchalik ko'pki, birortasini ham o'z holiga tashlab qo'yish xavfli. Hammamiz erkin boshlay olamiz — yengil moyillik tabiiy; lekin oramizda hech qanday dalda olmasdan chin dildan sevib qolishga yuragi yetadiganlar juda kam. O'ndan to'qqiz holatda ayol his qilganidan ko'proq mehr ko'rsatgani ma'qul. Bingli opangni shubhasiz yoqtiradi; lekin agar u unga yordam bermasa, u yoqtirishdan nariga o'tmasligi ham mumkin».

paras.en: “But she does help him on, as much as her nature will allow. If I can perceive her regard for him, he must be a simpleton, indeed, not to discover it too.”
paras.uz: «Lekin u yordam beryapti-ku, tabiati qanchalik imkon bersa, shunchalik. Agar men uning unga bo'lgan e'tiborini sezsam, u buni ham payqamasa, chindan ham soddadil bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Remember, Eliza, that he does not know Jane's disposition as you do.”
paras.uz: «Esingda bo'lsin, Eliza, u Jeynning fe'lini sendek bilmaydi».

paras.en: “But if a woman is partial to a man, and does not endeavour to conceal it, he must find it out.”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar ayol erkakka moyil bo'lsa va buni yashirishga urinmasa, u buni sezishi kerak».

paras.en: “Perhaps he must, if he sees enough of her. But, though Bingley and Jane meet tolerably often, it is never for many hours together; and, as they always see each other in large mixed parties, it is impossible that every moment should be employed in conversing together. Jane should therefore make the most of every half-hour in which she can command his attention. When she is secure of him, there will be more leisure for falling in love as much as she chooses.”
paras.uz: «Balki sezishi kerakdir, agar uni yetarlicha ko'rsa. Lekin Bingli va Jeyn ancha tez-tez uchrashsa ham, hech qachon ko'p soatlab birga bo'lishmaydi; va doim katta aralash davralarda ko'rishgani uchun, har bir lahzani bir-biri bilan suhbatlashishga sarflashlari mumkin emas. Shuning uchun Jeyn uning e'tiborini jalb qila oladigan har bir yarim soatdan maksimal foydalanishi kerak. Unga ishonchi komil bo'lgach, istaganicha sevib qolishga vaqti ko'proq bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Your plan is a good one,” replied Elizabeth, “where nothing is in question but the desire of being well married, and if I were determined to get a rich husband, or any husband, I dare say I should adopt it. But these are not Jane's feelings; she is not acting by design. As yet, she cannot even be certain of the degree of her own regard nor of its reasonableness. She has known him only a fortnight. She danced four dances with him at Meryton; she saw him one morning at his own house, and has since dined with him in company four times. This is not quite enough to make her understand his character.”
paras.uz: «Rejang yaxshi, — dedi Elizabet, — agar gap faqat yaxshi turmushga chiqish istagi haqida bo'lsa; agar men boy erga, yoki umuman biror erga tegishga qaror qilganimda, ehtimol, shuni qo'llagan bo'lardim. Lekin Jeynning tuyg'ulari bunday emas; u hisob-kitob bilan harakat qilmayapti. Hozircha u o'z mehrining darajasiga ham, uning oqilonaligiga ham ishonch hosil qila olmaydi. U bilan tanishganiga atigi ikki hafta bo'ldi. Meritonda u bilan to'rtta raqsga tushdi; bir kuni ertalab uni uyida ko'rdi va o'shandan beri u bilan to'rt marta davrada tushlik qildi. Bu uning xarakterini tushunishi uchun unchalik yetarli emas».

paras.en: “Not as you represent it. Had she merely dined with him, she might only have discovered whether he had a good appetite; but you must remember that four evenings have also been spent together--and four evenings may do a great deal.”
paras.uz: «Sen tasvirlaganday emas. Agar u u bilan faqat tushlik qilganida, faqat ishtahasi yaxshimi-yo'qmi, shuni bilib olishi mumkin edi; lekin to'rt oqshom ham birga o'tganini esdan chiqarma — to'rt oqshom esa ko'p narsa qilishi mumkin».

paras.en: “Yes; these four evenings have enabled them to ascertain that they both like Vingt-un better than Commerce; but with respect to any other leading characteristic, I do not imagine that much has been unfolded.”
paras.uz: «Ha; bu to'rt oqshom ularga ikkalasi ham Kommersdan ko'ra Yigirma birni ko'proq yoqtirishini aniqlash imkonini berdi; lekin boshqa biror muhim xususiyatga kelsak, ko'p narsa ochilgan deb o'ylamayman».

paras.en: “Well,” said Charlotte, “I wish Jane success with all my heart; and if she were married to him to-morrow, I should think she had as good a chance of happiness as if she were to be studying his character for a twelvemonth. Happiness in marriage is entirely a matter of chance. If the dispositions of the parties are ever so well known to each other or ever so similar beforehand, it does not advance their felicity in the least. They always continue to grow sufficiently unlike afterwards to have their share of vexation; and it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life.”
paras.uz: «Mayli, — dedi Sharlotta, — men Jeynga chin dildan omad tilayman; agar u ertaga unga turmushga chiqsa, uning baxtli bo'lish imkoniyati xuddi uning xarakterini bir yil o'rganganidagidek yaxshi bo'lardi, deb o'ylayman. Nikohdagi baxt butunlay tasodif ishi. Tomonlarning fe'llari bir-biriga oldindan qanchalik yaxshi ma'lum bo'lmasin yoki qanchalik o'xshash bo'lmasin, bu ularning baxtini zarracha ham oshirmaydi. Keyinchalik ular baribir yetarlicha bir-biriga o'xshamay qolib, o'z ulushidagi g'am-tashvishni oladilar; va butun umringni birga o'tkazadigan odamning kamchiliklari haqida iloji boricha kamroq bilganing yaxshiroq».

paras.en: “You make me laugh, Charlotte; but it is not sound. You know it is not sound, and that you would never act in this way yourself.”
paras.uz: «Meni kuldiryapsan, Sharlotta; lekin bu asosli emas. Buning asosli emasligini va o'zing hech qachon bunday yo'l tutmasligingni bilasan».

paras.en: Occupied in observing Mr. Bingley's attentions to her sister, Elizabeth was far from suspecting that she was herself becoming an object of some interest in the eyes of his friend. Mr. Darcy had at first scarcely allowed her to be pretty; he had looked at her without admiration at the ball; and when they next met, he looked at her only to criticise. But no sooner had he made it clear to himself and his friends that she hardly had a good feature in her face, than he began to find it was rendered uncommonly intelligent by the beautiful expression of her dark eyes. To this discovery succeeded some others equally mortifying. Though he had detected with a critical eye more than one failure of perfect symmetry in her form, he was forced to acknowledge her figure to be light and pleasing; and in spite of his asserting that her manners were not those of the fashionable world, he was caught by their easy playfulness. Of this she was perfectly unaware; to her he was only the man who made himself agreeable nowhere, and who had not thought her handsome enough to dance with.
paras.uz: Janob Binglining opasiga ko'rsatayotgan e'tiborini kuzatish bilan band bo'lgan Elizabet o'zi uning do'stining nazarida qandaydir qiziqish obyektiga aylanib borayotganidan mutlaqo bexabar edi. Janob Darsi avvaliga uni chiroyli deb ham arang tan olgan edi; balda unga hech qanday hayratsiz qaragan edi; keyingi uchrashganlarida esa unga faqat tanqid qilish uchun qaradi. Lekin o'ziga ham, do'stlariga ham uning yuzida birorta ham chiroyli xususiyat yo'qligini aniq aytib bo'lishi bilanoq, uning qora ko'zlarining go'zal ifodasi yuzini g'ayrioddiy darajada zukko ko'rsatishini seza boshladi. Bu kashfiyotdan keyin xuddi shunday izza qiluvchi boshqalari ham keldi. Garchi u tanqidiy ko'z bilan uning qaddi-qomatida mukammal mutanosiblikdan birdan ortiq chetlanishni topgan bo'lsa ham, uning qomati yengil va yoqimli ekanini tan olishga majbur bo'ldi; va uning muomalasi yuqori jamiyatnikiga o'xshamaydi, deb ta'kidlaganiga qaramay, uning erkin sho'xligiga maftun bo'lib qoldi. Elizabet bundan mutlaqo bexabar edi; uning uchun u hech qayerda o'zini yoqimli ko'rsatmaydigan va uni raqsga tushishga arziydigan darajada chiroyli deb hisoblamagan odam edi, xolos.

paras.en: He began to wish to know more of her, and as a step towards conversing with her himself, attended to her conversation with others. His doing so drew her notice. It was at Sir William Lucas's, where a large party were assembled.
paras.uz: U u haqida ko'proq bilishni istay boshladi va u bilan o'zi suhbatlashishga qadam sifatida uning boshqalar bilan suhbatini tinglay boshladi. Bu uning e'tiborini tortdi. Bu ser Uilyam Lukasnikida, katta davra yig'ilgan paytda bo'ldi.

paras.en: “What does Mr. Darcy mean,” said she to Charlotte, “by listening to my conversation with Colonel Forster?”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi mening polkovnik Forster bilan suhbatimni tinglab nima demoqchi?» — dedi u Sharlottaga.

paras.en: “That is a question which Mr. Darcy only can answer.”
paras.uz: «Bu savolga faqat janob Darsining o'zi javob bera oladi».

paras.en: “But if he does it any more I shall certainly let him know that I see what he is about. He has a very satirical eye, and if I do not begin by being impertinent myself, I shall soon grow afraid of him.”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar u yana shunday qilsa, uning nima qilayotganini ko'rib turganimni albatta unga bildirib qo'yaman. Uning nigohi juda kinoyali, agar men o'zim birinchi bo'lib shaddodlik qilishni boshlamasam, tez orada undan qo'rqa boshlayman».

paras.en: On his approaching them soon afterwards, though without seeming to have any intention of speaking, Miss Lucas defied her friend to mention such a subject to him; which immediately provoking Elizabeth to do it, she turned to him and said:
paras.uz: Ko'p o'tmay u ularga yaqinlashganida, garchi gaplashish niyati borday ko'rinmasa ham, miss Lukas dugonasini bu mavzuni unga aytishga jur'at etolmasligi bilan qitiqladi; bu Elizabetni darhol shunday qilishga undadi va u unga o'girilib dedi:

paras.en: “Did you not think, Mr. Darcy, that I expressed myself uncommonly well just now, when I was teasing Colonel Forster to give us a ball at Meryton?”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi, hozir polkovnik Forsterga Meritonda bal o'tkazib berishni hazil bilan qistaganimda, o'zimni g'ayrioddiy yaxshi ifoda etdim, deb o'ylamadingizmi?»

paras.en: “With great energy; but it is always a subject which makes a lady energetic.”
paras.uz: «Katta g'ayrat bilan; lekin bu har doim xonimni g'ayratga keltiradigan mavzu».

paras.en: “You are severe on us.”
paras.uz: «Siz bizga nisbatan qattiqqo'lsiz».

paras.en: “It will be her turn soon to be teased,” said Miss Lucas. “I am going to open the instrument, Eliza, and you know what follows.”
paras.uz: «Tez orada uni masxara qilish navbati keladi, — dedi miss Lukas. — Men cholg'uni ochaman, Eliza, keyin nima bo'lishini bilasan».

paras.en: “You are a very strange creature by way of a friend!--always wanting me to play and sing before anybody and everybody! If my vanity had taken a musical turn, you would have been invaluable; but as it is, I would really rather not sit down before those who must be in the habit of hearing the very best performers.” On Miss Lucas's persevering, however, she added, “Very well, if it must be so, it must.” And gravely glancing at Mr. Darcy, “There is a fine old saying, which everybody here is of course familiar with: 'Keep your breath to cool your porridge'; and I shall keep mine to swell my song.”
paras.uz: «Do'st sifatida juda g'alati mavjudotsan! Doim meni har kimning va hammaning oldida chalib-kuylashga majbur qilmoqchisan! Agar manmanligim musiqa tomonga burilganida, sen bebaho bo'larding; lekin hozircha, eng zo'r ijrochilarni eshitishga odatlangan odamlar oldida o'tirmaganim ma'qul». Biroq miss Lukas qistashda davom etgach, u qo'shib qo'ydi: «Mayli, shunday bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, shunday bo'lsin». Va janob Darsiga jiddiy qarab: «Bu yerdagilarning hammasiga tanish bo'lgan ajoyib eski maqol bor: „Nafasingni bo'tqangni sovutishga asra“; men esa o'zimnikini qo'shig'imni balandlatishga asrayman».

paras.en: Her performance was pleasing, though by no means capital. After a song or two, and before she could reply to the entreaties of several that she would sing again, she was eagerly succeeded at the instrument by her sister Mary, who having, in consequence of being the only plain one in the family, worked hard for knowledge and accomplishments, was always impatient for display.
paras.uz: Uning ijrosi yoqimli edi, garchi aslo a'lo bo'lmasa ham. Bir-ikki qo'shiqdan keyin, bir necha kishining yana kuylash iltimosiga javob berishga ulgurmasidanoq, cholg'u oldiga uning o'rniga singlisi Meri shoshib o'tirdi; oiladagi yagona xunuk qiz bo'lgani uchun u bilim va hunarlar ustida tirishib ishlagan edi va doim ularni namoyish qilishga intiqib turardi.

paras.en: Mary had neither genius nor taste; and though vanity had given her application, it had given her likewise a pedantic air and conceited manner, which would have injured a higher degree of excellence than she had reached. Elizabeth, easy and unaffected, had been listened to with much more pleasure, though not playing half so well; and Mary, at the end of a long concerto, was glad to purchase praise and gratitude by Scotch and Irish airs, at the request of her younger sisters, who, with some of the Lucases, and two or three officers, joined eagerly in dancing at one end of the room.
paras.uz: Merida na iste'dod, na did bor edi; manmanlik unga tirishqoqlik bergan bo'lsa ham, bilag'onlik qiyofasi va o'ziga bino qo'ygan muomalani ham bergan edi — bu u erishgan darajadan ancha yuqori mahoratga ham zarar yetkazgan bo'lardi. Erkin va tabiiy Elizabetni, garchi yarim darajada ham yaxshi chalmasa-da, ancha katta zavq bilan tinglashgan edi; Meri esa uzun kontsertning oxirida kichik singillarining iltimosiga ko'ra shotland va irland kuylarini chalib, maqtov va minnatdorlik sotib olishdan xursand bo'ldi; singillari esa ba'zi Lukaslar va ikki-uchta ofitser bilan zalning bir chetida ishtiyoq bilan raqsga tushishdi.

paras.en: Mr. Darcy stood near them in silent indignation at such a mode of passing the evening, to the exclusion of all conversation, and was too much engrossed by his thoughts to perceive that Sir William Lucas was his neighbour, till Sir William thus began:
paras.uz: Janob Darsi har qanday suhbatni chetlab o'tadigan bunday oqshom o'tkazish tarzidan indamay g'azablanib, ularning yonida turardi va o'z xayollariga shunchalik berilib ketgan ediki, ser Uilyam Lukas yonida turganini sezmadi, toki ser Uilyam gap boshlamaguncha:

paras.en: “What a charming amusement for young people this is, Mr. Darcy! There is nothing like dancing after all. I consider it as one of the first refinements of polished society.”
paras.uz: «Bu yoshlar uchun qanday maftunkor ermak, janob Darsi! Oxir-oqibat raqsga teng keladigan narsa yo'q. Men uni nafis jamiyatning eng birinchi go'zalliklaridan biri deb hisoblayman».

paras.en: “Certainly, sir; and it has the advantage also of being in vogue amongst the less polished societies of the world. Every savage can dance.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, ser; uning yana bir afzalligi — dunyodagi kamroq nafis jamiyatlarda ham urfda ekani. Har qanday yovvoyi raqsga tusha oladi».

paras.en: Sir William only smiled. “Your friend performs delightfully,” he continued after a pause, on seeing Bingley join the group; “and I doubt not that you are an adept in the science yourself, Mr. Darcy.”
paras.uz: Ser Uilyam faqat jilmaydi. «Do'stingiz ajoyib raqs tushadi, — dedi u biroz jim turib, Binglining davraga qo'shilganini ko'rib. — Shubham yo'qki, siz ham bu ilmda ustasiz, janob Darsi».

paras.en: “You saw me dance at Meryton, I believe, sir.”
paras.uz: «Meni Meritonda raqsga tushganimni ko'rgansiz shekilli, ser».

paras.en: “Yes, indeed, and received no inconsiderable pleasure from the sight. Do you often dance at St. James's?”
paras.uz: «Ha, albatta, va bu manzaradan oz bo'lmagan zavq oldim. Sent-Jeymsda tez-tez raqsga tushasizmi?»

paras.en: “Never, sir.”
paras.uz: «Hech qachon, ser».

paras.en: “Do you not think it would be a proper compliment to the place?”
paras.uz: «Bu o'sha joyga munosib hurmat bo'lardi, deb o'ylamaysizmi?»

paras.en: “It is a compliment which I never pay to any place if I can avoid it.”
paras.uz: «Bu iloji bo'lsa, hech qanday joyga ko'rsatmaydigan hurmatim».

paras.en: “You have a house in town, I conclude?”
paras.uz: «Londonda uyingiz bor, shekilli?»

paras.en: Mr. Darcy bowed.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi ta'zim qildi.

paras.en: “I had once had some thought of fixing in town myself--for I am fond of superior society; but I did not feel quite certain that the air of London would agree with Lady Lucas.”
paras.uz: «Men ham bir vaqtlar Londonda o'rnashish haqida o'ylagan edim — chunki yuksak jamiyatni yaxshi ko'raman; lekin London havosi ledi Lukasga mos kelishiga to'liq ishonchim komil emasdi».

paras.en: He paused in hopes of an answer; but his companion was not disposed to make any; and Elizabeth at that instant moving towards them, he was struck with the action of doing a very gallant thing, and called out to her:
paras.uz: U javob kutib to'xtadi; lekin suhbatdoshi javob berishga moyil emasdi; va shu lahzada Elizabet ular tomon kelayotgani uchun, uning xayoliga juda xushmuomala ish qilish fikri keldi va u unga murojaat qildi:

paras.en: “My dear Miss Eliza, why are you not dancing? Mr. Darcy, you must allow me to present this young lady to you as a very desirable partner. You cannot refuse to dance, I am sure when so much beauty is before you.” And, taking her hand, he would have given it to Mr. Darcy who, though extremely surprised, was not unwilling to receive it, when she instantly drew back, and said with some discomposure to Sir William:
paras.uz: «Aziz miss Eliza, nega raqsga tushmayapsiz? Janob Darsi, ruxsat bering, bu yosh xonimni sizga juda munosib raqs sherigi sifatida tavsiya qilay. Oldingizda shunchalik go'zallik turganda, raqsdan bosh tortolmasligingizga ishonaman». Va uning qo'lini olib, uni janob Darsiga bermoqchi bo'ldi — u esa juda hayron bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, uni olishga qarshi emasdi — biroq u darhol qo'lini tortib oldi va biroz xijolat bilan ser Uilyamga dedi:

paras.en: “Indeed, sir, I have not the least intention of dancing. I entreat you not to suppose that I moved this way in order to beg for a partner.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham, ser, raqsga tushish niyatim zarracha yo'q. Iltimos, bu tomonga sherik so'rash uchun keldim deb o'ylamang».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy, with grave propriety, requested to be allowed the honour of her hand, but in vain. Elizabeth was determined; nor did Sir William at all shake her purpose by his attempt at persuasion.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi jiddiy odob bilan unga qo'lini berish sharafini so'radi, lekin befoyda. Elizabet qat'iy edi; ser Uilyam ham ko'ndirishga urinishi bilan uning qarorini zarracha ham o'zgartira olmadi.

paras.en: “You excel so much in the dance, Miss Eliza, that it is cruel to deny me the happiness of seeing you; and though this gentleman dislikes the amusement in general, he can have no objection, I am sure, to oblige us for one half-hour.”
paras.uz: «Siz raqsda shunchalik mohirsizki, miss Eliza, meni sizni ko'rish baxtidan mahrum qilish shafqatsizlik; garchi bu janob umuman bu ermakni yoqtirmasa ham, ishonamanki, bizning xotirimiz uchun yarim soatga rozi bo'lishga qarshi emas».

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy is all politeness,” said Elizabeth, smiling.
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi xushmuomalalikning o'zi», — dedi Elizabet jilmayib.

paras.en: “He is, indeed; but, considering the inducement, my dear Miss Eliza, we cannot wonder at his complaisance--for who would object to such a partner?”
paras.uz: «Shunday, albatta; lekin sababini hisobga olsak, aziz miss Eliza, uning muloyimligiga hayron bo'lmasak ham bo'ladi — axir bunday sherikka kim qarshi bo'lardi?»

paras.en: Elizabeth looked archly, and turned away. Her resistance had not injured her with the gentleman, and he was thinking of her with some complacency, when thus accosted by Miss Bingley:
paras.uz: Elizabet sho'xona qaradi va yuzini burdi. Uning qarshiligi janobning nazarida unga zarar yetkazmadi va u u haqida biroz mamnuniyat bilan o'ylab turganida, miss Bingli unga shunday murojaat qildi:

paras.en: “I can guess the subject of your reverie.”
paras.uz: «Xayolingiz nimada ekanini taxmin qila olaman».

paras.en: “I should imagine not.”
paras.uz: «Taxmin qila olmaysiz deb o'ylayman».

paras.en: “You are considering how insupportable it would be to pass many evenings in this manner--in such society; and indeed I am quite of your opinion. I was never more annoyed! The insipidity, and yet the noise--the nothingness, and yet the self-importance of all those people! What would I give to hear your strictures on them!”
paras.uz: «Siz ko'p oqshomlarni shu tarzda — shunday davrada o'tkazish naqadar chidab bo'lmas ekanini o'ylayapsiz; men ham butunlay siz bilan bir fikrdaman. Hech qachon bunchalik jig'im chiqmagan edi! Bu odamlarning hammasidagi zerikarlilik, lekin shovqin — puchlik, lekin o'zini muhim sanash! Ular haqidagi keskin fikrlaringizni eshitish uchun nimalarni bermasdim!»

paras.en: “Your conjecture is totally wrong, I assure you. My mind was more agreeably engaged. I have been meditating on the very great pleasure which a pair of fine eyes in the face of a pretty woman can bestow.”
paras.uz: «Taxminingiz mutlaqo noto'g'ri, sizni ishontirib aytaman. Xayolim yoqimliroq narsa bilan band edi. Men chiroyli ayolning yuzidagi bir juft go'zal ko'z naqadar katta zavq bag'ishlashi mumkinligi haqida o'ylayotgandim».

paras.en: Miss Bingley immediately fixed her eyes on his face, and desired he would tell her what lady had the credit of inspiring such reflections. Mr. Darcy replied with great intrepidity:
paras.uz: Miss Bingli darhol ko'zlarini uning yuziga tikdi va qaysi xonim bunday mulohazalarni uyg'otish sharafiga muyassar bo'lganini aytishini so'radi. Janob Darsi katta jasorat bilan javob berdi:

paras.en: “Miss Elizabeth Bennet.”
paras.uz: «Miss Elizabet Bennet».

paras.en: “Miss Elizabeth Bennet!” repeated Miss Bingley. “I am all astonishment. How long has she been such a favourite?--and pray, when am I to wish you joy?”
paras.uz: «Miss Elizabet Bennet! — deb takrorladi miss Bingli. — Butunlay hayratdaman. U qachondan beri bunchalik sevimli bo'lib qoldi? Ayting-chi, sizni qachon tabriklashim kerak?»

paras.en: “That is exactly the question which I expected you to ask. A lady's imagination is very rapid; it jumps from admiration to love, from love to matrimony, in a moment. I knew you would be wishing me joy.”
paras.uz: «Aynan shu savolni berishingizni kutgandim. Xonimning tasavvuri juda tez ishlaydi: bir lahzada mahliyolikdan sevgiga, sevgidan nikohga sakraydi. Meni tabriklamoqchi bo'lishingizni bilardim».

paras.en: “Nay, if you are serious about it, I shall consider the matter is absolutely settled. You will be having a charming mother-in-law, indeed; and, of course, she will always be at Pemberley with you.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, agar bu borada jiddiy bo'lsangiz, masala butunlay hal bo'lgan deb hisoblayman. Sizda chindan ham maftunkor qaynona bo'ladi; albatta, u doim siz bilan Pemberlida bo'ladi».

paras.en: He listened to her with perfect indifference while she chose to entertain herself in this manner; and as his composure convinced her that all was safe, her wit flowed long.
paras.uz: U shu tarzda o'zini ovutib turganida, Darsi uni mutlaq befarqlik bilan tingladi; uning xotirjamligi esa miss Binglini hammasi xavfsiz ekaniga ishontirgani uchun, uning zehnli gaplari uzoq davom etdi.

gloss.ex: If a woman conceals her affection with the same skill from the object of it, she may lose the opportunity of fixing him; and it will then be but poor…
If a woman conceals her affection with the same skill from the object of it, she may lose the opportunity of fixing him; and it will then be but poor…
“But if a woman is partial to a man, and does not endeavour to conceal it, he must find it out.”
It was generally evident whenever they met, that he did admire her and to her it was equally evident that Jane was yielding to the preference which she had begun…
He listened to her with perfect indifference while she chose to entertain herself in this manner; and as his composure convinced her that all was safe, her wit flowed long.
“I am all astonishment.
He began to wish to know more of her, and as a step towards conversing with her himself, attended to her conversation with others.

quiz.q: What does Darcy begin to notice about Elizabeth?
quiz.why_uz: U Elizabetni avval rad etgan bo'lsa ham, endi uning ko'zlari va zakovatiga qiziqadi.

quiz.q: What does Charlotte think about marriage?
o: Happiness in marriage is entirely a matter of chance
quiz.why_uz: Sharlottaning amaliy qarashi keyinroq uning o'z tanlovida ko'rinadi.

chapters.title: Jane Rides in the Rain
chapters.recap_uz: Mulk qonun bo'yicha faqat erkak merosxo'rga o'tadi. Jeyn Netherfieldga taklif qilinadi; onasi uni ataylab otda, yomg'irda jo'natadi — Jeyn shamollab qoladi. Elizabet opasini ko'rgani loydan piyoda boradi.

paras.en: Mr. Bennet's property consisted almost entirely in an estate of two thousand a year, which, unfortunately for his daughters, was entailed, in default of heirs male, on a distant relation; and their mother's fortune, though ample for her situation in life, could but ill supply the deficiency of his. Her father had been an attorney in Meryton, and had left her four thousand pounds.
paras.uz: Janob Bennetning mol-mulki deyarli butunlay yiliga ikki ming funt daromad keltiradigan yer-mulkdan iborat edi; qizlarining baxtiga qarshi, u erkak merosxo'r bo'lmagan taqdirda uzoq bir qarindoshga o'tishi qonun bilan belgilab qo'yilgan edi; onalarining boyligi esa uning ijtimoiy mavqeiga ko'ra yetarli bo'lsa-da, erining kamini arang to'ldira olardi. Uning otasi Meritonda advokat bo'lgan va unga to'rt ming funt qoldirgan edi.

paras.en: She had a sister married to a Mr. Phillips, who had been a clerk to their father and succeeded him in the business, and a brother settled in London in a respectable line of trade.
paras.uz: Uning otasining mirzasi bo'lib, keyin uning ishini davom ettirgan janob Fillipsga turmushga chiqqan singlisi va Londonda obro'li savdo bilan shug'ullanadigan akasi bor edi.

paras.en: The village of Longbourn was only one mile from Meryton; a most convenient distance for the young ladies, who were usually tempted thither three or four times a week, to pay their duty to their aunt and to a milliner's shop just over the way. The two youngest of the family, Catherine and Lydia, were particularly frequent in these attentions; their minds were more vacant than their sisters', and when nothing better offered, a walk to Meryton was necessary to amuse their morning hours and furnish conversation for the evening; and however bare of news the country in general might be, they always contrived to learn some from their aunt. At present, indeed, they were well supplied both with news and happiness by the recent arrival of a militia regiment in the neighbourhood; it was to remain the whole winter, and Meryton was the headquarters.
paras.uz: Longborn qishlog'i Meritondan atigi bir mil uzoqda edi; bu yosh xonimlar uchun juda qulay masofa edi: ular odatda haftasiga uch-to'rt marta xolalari va ro'paradagi shlyapa do'koni oldida o'z burchlarini ado etish uchun u yerga borishga mayl qilishardi. Oiladagi eng kichik ikki qiz — Ketrin va Lidiya bunday tashriflarni ayniqsa tez-tez qilishardi; ularning boshi opalarinikidan bo'shroq edi va yaxshiroq ish bo'lmasa, tongni o'tkazish va kechki suhbatga mavzu topish uchun Meritonga sayr zarur edi; atrof umuman olganda yangiliklarga qanchalik kambag'al bo'lmasin, ular xolalaridan doim biror yangilik bilib olishning uddasidan chiqishardi. Hozir esa yaqinda mahallaga opolchenie polki kelgani tufayli ular ham yangilik, ham baxt bilan yaxshi ta'minlangan edilar; polk butun qish qolishi kerak edi, shtab esa Meritonda edi.

paras.en: Their visits to Mrs. Phillips were now productive of the most interesting intelligence. Every day added something to their knowledge of the officers' names and connections. Their lodgings were not long a secret, and at length they began to know the officers themselves. Mr. Phillips visited them all, and this opened to his nieces a store of felicity unknown before. They could talk of nothing but officers; and Mr. Bingley's large fortune, the mention of which gave animation to their mother, was worthless in their eyes when opposed to the regimentals of an ensign.
paras.uz: Endi ularning missis Fillipsnikiga borishlari eng qiziqarli xabarlarni olib kelardi. Har kun ularning ofitserlarning ismlari va aloqalari haqidagi bilimiga nimadir qo'shardi. Ofitserlarning qayerda turishi uzoq sir bo'lib qolmadi va oxiri ular ofitserlarning o'zlari bilan ham tanisha boshladilar. Janob Fillips hammasiga tashrif buyurdi va bu jiyanlari uchun ilgari noma'lum bo'lgan baxt xazinasini ochdi. Ular ofitserlardan boshqa hech narsa haqida gapira olmasdilar; onalarini jonlantiradigan janob Binglining katta boyligi esa praporshchikning formasi oldida ularning nazarida hech narsaga arzimasdi.

paras.en: After listening one morning to their effusions on this subject, Mr. Bennet coolly observed:
paras.uz: Bir kuni ertalab ularning bu mavzudagi zavq-shavqli gaplarini tinglagach, janob Bennet sovuqqonlik bilan dedi:

paras.en: “From all that I can collect by your manner of talking, you must be two of the silliest girls in the country. I have suspected it some time, but I am now convinced.”
paras.uz: «Gapirish tarzingizdan bilib olganlarimga qaraganda, sizlar butun grafllikdagi eng ahmoq ikki qiz bo'lsangiz kerak. Buni ancha vaqtdan beri gumon qilardim, endi esa ishonch hosil qildim».

paras.en: Catherine was disconcerted, and made no answer; but Lydia, with perfect indifference, continued to express her admiration of Captain Carter, and her hope of seeing him in the course of the day, as he was going the next morning to London.
paras.uz: Ketrin xijolat bo'lib, javob bermadi; Lidiya esa mutlaq befarqlik bilan kapitan Karterga mahliyoligini va u ertasi kuni ertalab Londonga ketayotgani uchun kun davomida uni ko'rishga umid qilayotganini aytishda davom etdi.

paras.en: “I am astonished, my dear,” said Mrs. Bennet, “that you should be so ready to think your own children silly. If I wished to think slightingly of anybody's children, it should not be of my own, however.”
paras.uz: «Hayronman, azizim, — dedi missis Bennet, — o'z bolalaringizni ahmoq deb o'ylashga buncha tayyorsiz. Agar kimningdir bolalari haqida past fikrda bo'lishni istaganimda ham, baribir o'zimnikilar haqida emas».

paras.en: “If my children are silly, I must hope to be always sensible of it.”
paras.uz: «Agar bolalarim ahmoq bo'lsa, buni doim anglab turishimga umid qilishim kerak».

paras.en: “Yes--but as it happens, they are all of them very clever.”
paras.uz: «Ha — lekin qarangki, ularning hammasi juda aqlli».

paras.en: “This is the only point, I flatter myself, on which we do not agree. I had hoped that our sentiments coincided in every particular, but I must so far differ from you as to think our two youngest daughters uncommonly foolish.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, bu biz kelisha olmaydigan yagona masala. Men hislarimiz har jihatdan mos keladi deb umid qilgan edim, lekin ikki kichik qizimizni g'ayrioddiy darajada ahmoq deb hisoblashda sizdan farq qilishim kerak».

paras.en: “My dear Mr. Bennet, you must not expect such girls to have the sense of their father and mother. When they get to our age, I dare say they will not think about officers any more than we do. I remember the time when I liked a red coat myself very well--and, indeed, so I do still at my heart; and if a smart young colonel, with five or six thousand a year, should want one of my girls I shall not say nay to him; and I thought Colonel Forster looked very becoming the other night at Sir William's in his regimentals.”
paras.uz: «Aziz janob Bennet, bunday qizlardan ota-onasidek aqlni kutmasligingiz kerak. Bizning yoshimizga yetganda, ishonamanki, ular ham bizdan ortiq ofitserlar haqida o'ylamaydi. Esimda, bir vaqtlar o'zim ham qizil kamzulni juda yaxshi ko'rardim — aslida hozir ham yuragimda shunday; agar yiliga besh-olti ming funt daromadi bo'lgan chaqqon yosh polkovnik qizlarimdan birini so'rasa, unga yo'q demayman; o'tgan oqshom ser Uilyamnikida polkovnik Forster formasida juda yarashgan ko'rindi, deb o'yladim».

paras.en: “Mamma,” cried Lydia, “my aunt says that Colonel Forster and Captain Carter do not go so often to Miss Watson's as they did when they first came; she sees them now very often standing in Clarke's library.”
paras.uz: «Oyijon, — deb qichqirdi Lidiya, — xolamning aytishicha, polkovnik Forster va kapitan Karter miss Uotsonnikiga ilk kelgan paytlaridagidek tez-tez borishmay qo'yibdi; endi u ularni ko'pincha Klark kutubxonasida turgan holda ko'rarkan».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet was prevented replying by the entrance of the footman with a note for Miss Bennet; it came from Netherfield, and the servant waited for an answer. Mrs. Bennet's eyes sparkled with pleasure, and she was eagerly calling out, while her daughter read,
paras.uz: Missis Bennetga javob berishga miss Bennetga xat ko'tarib kirgan xizmatkor xalaqit berdi; xat Nezerfilddan kelgan edi va xizmatkor javob kutib turardi. Missis Bennetning ko'zlari xursandchilikdan chaqnab ketdi va qizi o'qiyotgan paytda u shoshib so'ray boshladi:

paras.en: “Well, Jane, who is it from? What is it about? What does he say? Well, Jane, make haste and tell us; make haste, my love.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, Jeyn, kimdan? Nima haqida? U nima deyapti? Xo'sh, Jeyn, tezroq aytib ber; tezroq, jonim».

paras.en: “It is from Miss Bingley,” said Jane, and then read it aloud.
paras.uz: «Miss Binglidan», — dedi Jeyn va uni ovoz chiqarib o'qidi.

paras.en: “MY DEAR FRIEND,--
paras.uz: «AZIZ DUGONAM,

paras.en: “If you are not so compassionate as to dine to-day with Louisa and me, we shall be in danger of hating each other for the rest of our lives, for a whole day's tete-a-tete between two women can never end without a quarrel. Come as soon as you can on receipt of this. My brother and the gentlemen are to dine with the officers.--Yours ever,
paras.uz: Agar bugun Luiza va men bilan tushlik qilishga rahmingiz kelmasa, umrimizning oxirigacha bir-birimizni yomon ko'rib qolish xavfi tug'iladi, chunki ikki ayolning butun kun yuzma-yuz o'tirishi hech qachon janjalsiz tugamaydi. Buni olishingiz bilan iloji boricha tezroq keling. Akam va janoblar ofitserlar bilan tushlik qilishadi. Doimo sizniki,

paras.en: “CAROLINE BINGLEY”
paras.uz: KAROLAYN BINGLI»

paras.en: “With the officers!” cried Lydia. “I wonder my aunt did not tell us of that.”
paras.uz: «Ofitserlar bilan! — deb qichqirdi Lidiya. — Hayronman, xolam bu haqda bizga aytmabdi».

paras.en: “Dining out,” said Mrs. Bennet, “that is very unlucky.”
paras.uz: «Tashqarida tushlik qilisharkan, — dedi missis Bennet, — bu juda omadsizlik».

paras.en: “Can I have the carriage?” said Jane.
paras.uz: «Aravani olsam bo'ladimi?» — dedi Jeyn.

paras.en: “No, my dear, you had better go on horseback, because it seems likely to rain; and then you must stay all night.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, azizim, yaxshisi otda bor, chunki yomg'ir yog'adiganga o'xshaydi; shunda tunab qolishingga to'g'ri keladi».

paras.en: “That would be a good scheme,” said Elizabeth, “if you were sure that they would not offer to send her home.”
paras.uz: «Bu yaxshi reja bo'lardi, — dedi Elizabet, — agar ular uni uyga jo'natishni taklif qilmasligiga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsa».

paras.en: “Oh! but the gentlemen will have Mr. Bingley's chaise to go to Meryton, and the Hursts have no horses to theirs.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Lekin janoblar Meritonga borish uchun janob Binglining aravasini olishadi, Xerstlarning esa aravasiga oti yo'q».

paras.en: “I had much rather go in the coach.”
paras.uz: «Men aravada borganim ancha ma'qul».

paras.en: “But, my dear, your father cannot spare the horses, I am sure. They are wanted in the farm, Mr. Bennet, are they not?”
paras.uz: «Lekin, azizim, otang otlarni bera olmasligiga ishonchim komil. Ular fermada kerak, janob Bennet, shunday emasmi?»

paras.en: “They are wanted in the farm much oftener than I can get them.”
paras.uz: «Ular fermada men ularni ola olganimdan ancha tez-tez kerak bo'ladi».

paras.en: “But if you have got them to-day,” said Elizabeth, “my mother's purpose will be answered.”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar bugun ularni olgan bo'lsangiz, — dedi Elizabet, — onamning maqsadi amalga oshadi».

paras.en: She did at last extort from her father an acknowledgment that the horses were engaged. Jane was therefore obliged to go on horseback, and her mother attended her to the door with many cheerful prognostics of a bad day. Her hopes were answered; Jane had not been gone long before it rained hard. Her sisters were uneasy for her, but her mother was delighted. The rain continued the whole evening without intermission; Jane certainly could not come back.
paras.uz: Oxiri u otasidan otlar band ekanini tan oldirishga muvaffaq bo'ldi. Shunday qilib, Jeyn otda borishga majbur bo'ldi va onasi uni yomon havo haqidagi ko'plab quvnoq bashoratlar bilan eshikkacha kuzatib qo'ydi. Uning umidlari ro'yobga chiqdi: Jeyn ketganidan ko'p o'tmay qattiq yomg'ir yog'a boshladi. Opa-singillari uning uchun xavotirlanishdi, onasi esa xursand edi. Yomg'ir butun oqshom to'xtovsiz yog'di; Jeyn, albatta, qaytib kela olmasdi.

paras.en: “This was a lucky idea of mine, indeed!” said Mrs. Bennet more than once, as if the credit of making it rain were all her own. Till the next morning, however, she was not aware of all the felicity of her contrivance. Breakfast was scarcely over when a servant from Netherfield brought the following note for Elizabeth:
paras.uz: «Bu chindan ham omadli fikr bo'ldi!» — dedi missis Bennet bir necha marta, go'yo yomg'ir yog'dirish sharafi butunlay uniki bo'lganday. Biroq ertasi kungacha u o'z hiylasining butun baxtidan bexabar edi. Nonushta endigina tugagan ediki, Nezerfilddan xizmatkor Elizabetga quyidagi maktubni olib keldi:

paras.en: “MY DEAREST LIZZY,--
paras.uz: «ENG AZIZ LIZZIM,

paras.en: “I find myself very unwell this morning, which, I suppose, is to be imputed to my getting wet through yesterday. My kind friends will not hear of my returning till I am better. They insist also on my seeing Mr. Jones--therefore do not be alarmed if you should hear of his having been to me--and, excepting a sore throat and headache, there is not much the matter with me.--Yours, etc.”
paras.uz: Bugun ertalab o'zimni juda yomon his qilyapman, buni, ehtimol, kecha jiqqa ho'l bo'lganimga bog'lash kerak. Mehribon dugonalarim tuzalgunimcha qaytishim haqida eshitishni ham istamayapti. Ular janob Jonsni ko'rishimni ham talab qilishyapti — shuning uchun uning menikiga kelganini eshitsangiz, qo'rqmang — tomog'im og'rishi va bosh og'rig'ini hisobga olmaganda, unchalik jiddiy narsa yo'q. Sizniki va hokazo».

paras.en: “Well, my dear,” said Mr. Bennet, when Elizabeth had read the note aloud, “if your daughter should have a dangerous fit of illness--if she should die, it would be a comfort to know that it was all in pursuit of Mr. Bingley, and under your orders.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, azizim, — dedi janob Bennet, Elizabet maktubni ovoz chiqarib o'qib bo'lgach, — agar qizingiz xavfli kasallikka chalinsa — agar u o'lib qolsa, bularning hammasi janob Bingli ortidan quvish uchun va sizning buyrug'ingiz bilan bo'lganini bilish tasalli bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Oh! I am not afraid of her dying. People do not die of little trifling colds. She will be taken good care of. As long as she stays there, it is all very well. I would go and see her if I could have the carriage.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Uning o'lishidan qo'rqmayman. Odamlar arzimas shamollashdan o'lishmaydi. Unga yaxshi qarashadi. U o'sha yerda ekan, hammasi juda yaxshi. Agar aravani ola olganimda, borib uni ko'rgan bo'lardim».

paras.en: Elizabeth, feeling really anxious, was determined to go to her, though the carriage was not to be had; and as she was no horsewoman, walking was her only alternative. She declared her resolution.
paras.uz: Chindan ham xavotirga tushgan Elizabet, arava bo'lmasa ham, uning oldiga borishga qaror qildi; u chavandoz bo'lmagani uchun piyoda borishdan boshqa iloji yo'q edi. U o'z qarorini e'lon qildi.

paras.en: “How can you be so silly,” cried her mother, “as to think of such a thing, in all this dirt! You will not be fit to be seen when you get there.”
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib bunchalik ahmoq bo'lasan, — deb qichqirdi onasi, — shuncha loyda bunday narsani o'ylab! U yerga yetib borganingda ko'rinadigan ahvolda bo'lmaysan».

paras.en: “I shall be very fit to see Jane--which is all I want.”
paras.uz: «Jeynni ko'rish uchun juda munosib ahvolda bo'laman — menga kerak bo'lgani faqat shu».

paras.en: “Is this a hint to me, Lizzy,” said her father, “to send for the horses?”
paras.uz: «Bu menga otlarni chaqirtirish haqida ishorami, Lizzi?» — dedi otasi.

paras.en: “No, indeed, I do not wish to avoid the walk. The distance is nothing when one has a motive; only three miles. I shall be back by dinner.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, aslo, men piyoda yurishdan qochmoqchi emasman. Maqsad bo'lsa, masofa hech narsa emas; atigi uch mil. Tushlikkacha qaytaman».

paras.en: “I admire the activity of your benevolence,” observed Mary, “but every impulse of feeling should be guided by reason; and, in my opinion, exertion should always be in proportion to what is required.”
paras.uz: «Mehribonligingdagi g'ayratga qoyil qolaman, — dedi Meri, — lekin tuyg'uning har bir turtkisini aql boshqarishi kerak; menimcha, sa'y-harakat doim talab qilinadigan narsaga mutanosib bo'lishi lozim».

paras.en: “We will go as far as Meryton with you,” said Catherine and Lydia. Elizabeth accepted their company, and the three young ladies set off together.
paras.uz: «Biz sen bilan Meritongacha boramiz», — deyishdi Ketrin va Lidiya. Elizabet ularning hamrohligini qabul qildi va uch yosh xonim birga yo'lga chiqishdi.

paras.en: “If we make haste,” said Lydia, as they walked along, “perhaps we may see something of Captain Carter before he goes.”
paras.uz: «Agar shoshilsak, — dedi Lidiya yo'lda ketayotib, — balki kapitan Karterni ketishidan oldin ko'rib qolarmiz».

paras.en: In Meryton they parted; the two youngest repaired to the lodgings of one of the officers' wives, and Elizabeth continued her walk alone, crossing field after field at a quick pace, jumping over stiles and springing over puddles with impatient activity, and finding herself at last within view of the house, with weary ankles, dirty stockings, and a face glowing with the warmth of exercise.
paras.uz: Meritonda ular ajralishdi; eng kichik ikkitasi ofitserlardan birining xotini turadigan joyga yo'l oldi, Elizabet esa yolg'iz yo'lini davom ettirdi: tez qadamlar bilan daladan dalaga o'tib, to'siq zinalaridan oshib, ko'lmaklardan sabrsizlik bilan sakrab, oxiri charchagan to'piqlari, loy paypoqlari va jismoniy harakatdan qizarib ketgan yuzi bilan uy ko'rinadigan joyga yetib keldi.

paras.en: She was shown into the breakfast-parlour, where all but Jane were assembled, and where her appearance created a great deal of surprise. That she should have walked three miles so early in the day, in such dirty weather, and by herself, was almost incredible to Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley; and Elizabeth was convinced that they held her in contempt for it. She was received, however, very politely by them; and in their brother's manners there was something better than politeness; there was good humour and kindness. Mr. Darcy said very little, and Mr. Hurst nothing at all. The former was divided between admiration of the brilliancy which exercise had given to her complexion, and doubt as to the occasion's justifying her coming so far alone. The latter was thinking only of his breakfast.
paras.uz: Uni nonushta xonasiga olib kirishdi, u yerda Jeyndan boshqa hamma yig'ilgan edi va uning ko'rinishi katta hayrat uyg'otdi. Uning kunning shunday erta paytida, shunday loy havoda, yolg'iz o'zi uch mil piyoda kelgani missis Xerst va miss Bingliga deyarli aql bovar qilmaydigan narsa bo'lib tuyuldi; Elizabet ular buning uchun undan nafratlanayotganiga ishonch hosil qildi. Biroq ular uni juda xushmuomalalik bilan kutib olishdi; akalarining muomalasida esa xushmuomalalikdan ham yaxshiroq narsa — xushfe'llik va mehribonlik bor edi. Janob Darsi juda kam gapirdi, janob Xerst esa umuman gapirmadi. Birinchisi harakatdan uning yuziga kirgan yorqinlikdan hayratlanish bilan bunday sabab uning shuncha yo'lni yolg'iz bosib kelishini oqlaydimi, degan shubha o'rtasida ikkilanardi. Ikkinchisi esa faqat nonushtasi haqida o'ylardi.

paras.en: Her inquiries after her sister were not very favourably answered. Miss Bennet had slept ill, and though up, was very feverish, and not well enough to leave her room. Elizabeth was glad to be taken to her immediately; and Jane, who had only been withheld by the fear of giving alarm or inconvenience from expressing in her note how much she longed for such a visit, was delighted at her entrance. She was not equal, however, to much conversation, and when Miss Bingley left them together, could attempt little besides expressions of gratitude for the extraordinary kindness she was treated with. Elizabeth silently attended her.
paras.uz: Opasi haqidagi so'roqlariga unchalik yaxshi javob berilmadi. Miss Bennet yomon uxlagan ekan, o'rnidan tursa ham, qattiq isitmalab turibdi va xonasidan chiqadigan ahvolda emas ekan. Elizabet darhol uning oldiga olib borilganidan xursand bo'ldi; xavotir yoki noqulaylik tug'dirishdan qo'rqqani uchungina maktubida bunday tashrifni qanchalik orziqib kutayotganini yozmagan Jeyn uning kirib kelganidan juda shod bo'ldi. Biroq u ko'p gaplashishga qodir emasdi va miss Bingli ularni yolg'iz qoldirgach, unga ko'rsatilayotgan g'ayrioddiy mehribonlik uchun minnatdorlik bildirishdan boshqa narsaga deyarli urinmadi. Elizabet jimgina unga qarab o'tirdi.

paras.en: When breakfast was over they were joined by the sisters; and Elizabeth began to like them herself, when she saw how much affection and solicitude they showed for Jane. The apothecary came, and having examined his patient, said, as might be supposed, that she had caught a violent cold, and that they must endeavour to get the better of it; advised her to return to bed, and promised her some draughts. The advice was followed readily, for the feverish symptoms increased, and her head ached acutely. Elizabeth did not quit her room for a moment; nor were the other ladies often absent; the gentlemen being out, they had, in fact, nothing to do elsewhere.
paras.uz: Nonushta tugagach, opa-singillar ularga qo'shilishdi; Elizabet ularning Jeynga qanchalik mehr va g'amxo'rlik ko'rsatayotganini ko'rib, o'zi ham ularni yoqtira boshladi. Dorishunos kelib, bemorni ko'rgach, kutilganidek, u qattiq shamollaganini va uni yengish uchun harakat qilish kerakligini aytdi; unga yana yotishni maslahat berdi va bir necha qaynatma dori va'da qildi. Maslahatga darhol amal qilindi, chunki isitma belgilari kuchaydi va boshi qattiq og'riy boshladi. Elizabet bir lahza ham uning xonasidan chiqmadi; boshqa xonimlar ham tez-tez yo'q bo'lishmadi; janoblar tashqarida bo'lgani uchun, aslida ularning boshqa joyda qiladigan ishi ham yo'q edi.

paras.en: When the clock struck three, Elizabeth felt that she must go, and very unwillingly said so. Miss Bingley offered her the carriage, and she only wanted a little pressing to accept it, when Jane testified such concern in parting with her, that Miss Bingley was obliged to convert the offer of the chaise to an invitation to remain at Netherfield for the present. Elizabeth most thankfully consented, and a servant was dispatched to Longbourn to acquaint the family with her stay and bring back a supply of clothes.
paras.uz: Soat uchni urganda Elizabet ketishi kerakligini his qildi va buni juda istamay aytdi. Miss Bingli unga aravasini taklif qildi va u ozgina qistovdan keyin qabul qilmoqchi bo'lib turganida, Jeyn u bilan xayrlashishdan shunchalik xavotirga tushdiki, miss Bingli arava taklifini hozircha Nezerfildda qolish taklifiga aylantirishga majbur bo'ldi. Elizabet katta minnatdorlik bilan rozi bo'ldi va oilaga uning qolganini xabar qilish hamda kiyim-kechak olib kelish uchun Longbornga xizmatkor jo'natildi.

quiz.q: Why does Mrs. Bennet send Jane on horseback?
o: So that rain will force her to stay at Netherfield
quiz.why_uz: Missis Bennetning hiylasi Jeynning kasal bo'lishiga olib keladi.

quiz.q: How does Elizabeth go to Netherfield?
quiz.why_uz: Bingley opa-singillari uning loy etagini masxara qiladi, Darsi esa uning ko'zlari yorishganini sezadi.

chapters.title: At Netherfield
chapters.recap_uz: Bingleyning opa-singillari Elizabetni orqasidan masxara qilishadi. Kechqurun «har tomonlama yetuk ayol» haqida bahs bo'ladi: Darsining talablari juda yuqori ekanini Elizabet ochiq aytadi.

paras.en: At five o'clock the two ladies retired to dress, and at half-past six Elizabeth was summoned to dinner. To the civil inquiries which then poured in, and amongst which she had the pleasure of distinguishing the much superior solicitude of Mr. Bingley's, she could not make a very favourable answer. Jane was by no means better. The sisters, on hearing this, repeated three or four times how much they were grieved, how shocking it was to have a bad cold, and how excessively they disliked being ill themselves; and then thought no more of the matter: and their indifference towards Jane when not immediately before them restored Elizabeth to the enjoyment of all her former dislike.
paras.uz: Soat beshda ikki xonim kiyinish uchun xonalariga chiqib ketishdi, soat oltiyarimda esa Elizabetni tushlikka chaqirishdi. Shunda yog'ilgan xushmuomala so'roqlarga — ular orasida janob Binglining ancha samimiyroq tashvishini ajratib ko'rish unga yoqimli edi — u unchalik ijobiy javob bera olmadi. Jeyn aslo yaxshilanmagan edi. Buni eshitgan opa-singillar qanchalik qayg'urayotganlarini, qattiq shamollash naqadar dahshatli ekanini va o'zlari kasal bo'lishni nihoyatda yomon ko'rishlarini uch-to'rt marta takrorlashdi; keyin bu haqda boshqa o'ylashmadi; ularning Jeyn ko'z oldilarida bo'lmaganda unga befarqligi Elizabetga avvalgi butun yoqtirmasligini qaytarib berdi.

paras.en: Their brother, indeed, was the only one of the party whom she could regard with any complacency. His anxiety for Jane was evident, and his attentions to herself most pleasing, and they prevented her feeling herself so much an intruder as she believed she was considered by the others. She had very little notice from any but him. Miss Bingley was engrossed by Mr. Darcy, her sister scarcely less so; and as for Mr. Hurst, by whom Elizabeth sat, he was an indolent man, who lived only to eat, drink, and play at cards; who, when he found her to prefer a plain dish to a ragout, had nothing to say to her.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham, davradagilardan faqat ularning akasigagina u biroz mamnuniyat bilan qaray olardi. Uning Jeyn uchun xavotiri ochiq-oydin edi, Elizabetning o'ziga ko'rsatgan e'tibori esa juda yoqimli edi va ular uni boshqalar o'ylaganchalik ortiqcha mehmon deb his qilishdan saqlardi. Undan boshqa hech kim unga deyarli e'tibor bermadi. Miss Bingli janob Darsi bilan band edi, singlisi ham deyarli shunday; Elizabet yonida o'tirgan janob Xerstga kelsak, u faqat yeyish, ichish va karta o'ynash uchun yashaydigan dangasa odam edi; Elizabetning ragudan ko'ra oddiy taomni afzal ko'rishini bilgach, unga aytadigan gapi qolmadi.

paras.en: When dinner was over, she returned directly to Jane, and Miss Bingley began abusing her as soon as she was out of the room. Her manners were pronounced to be very bad indeed, a mixture of pride and impertinence; she had no conversation, no style, no beauty. Mrs. Hurst thought the same, and added:
paras.uz: Tushlik tugagach, u to'g'ri Jeynning oldiga qaytdi va u xonadan chiqishi bilanoq miss Bingli uni yomonlay boshladi. Uning muomalasi haqiqatan ham juda yomon — g'urur va surbetlik aralashmasi deb topildi; unda na suhbat, na uslub, na go'zallik bor edi. Missis Xerst ham shunday deb o'yladi va qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “She has nothing, in short, to recommend her, but being an excellent walker. I shall never forget her appearance this morning. She really looked almost wild.”
paras.uz: «Qisqasi, unda zo'r piyoda yurishdan boshqa maqtashga arziydigan hech narsa yo'q. Bugun ertalabki ko'rinishini hech qachon unutmayman. U chindan ham deyarli yovvoyiga o'xshardi».

paras.en: “She did, indeed, Louisa. I could hardly keep my countenance. Very nonsensical to come at all! Why must she be scampering about the country, because her sister had a cold? Her hair, so untidy, so blowsy!”
paras.uz: «Rostdan ham shunday edi, Luiza. Kulgimni arang tiyib turdim. Umuman kelishi qanday bema'nilik! Opasi shamollagani uchun nega u dalama-dala yugurib yurishi kerak? Sochi esa shunday tartibsiz, to'zg'igan!»

paras.en: “Yes, and her petticoat; I hope you saw her petticoat, six inches deep in mud, I am absolutely certain; and the gown which had been let down to hide it not doing its office.”
paras.uz: «Ha, ichki yubkasi-chi; umid qilamanki, ichki yubkasini ko'rdingiz, olti dyuymgacha loyga botgan edi, aniq bilaman; uni yashirish uchun tushirilgan ko'ylak esa vazifasini bajarmayotgan edi».

paras.en: “Your picture may be very exact, Louisa,” said Bingley; “but this was all lost upon me. I thought Miss Elizabeth Bennet looked remarkably well when she came into the room this morning. Her dirty petticoat quite escaped my notice.”
paras.uz: «Sening tasviring juda aniq bo'lishi mumkin, Luiza, — dedi Bingli, — lekin bularning hammasi mendan chetda qoldi. Menimcha, miss Elizabet Bennet bugun ertalab xonaga kirganda ajoyib ko'rindi. Loy ichki yubkasi umuman e'tiborimdan chetda qoldi».

paras.en: “You observed it, Mr. Darcy, I am sure,” said Miss Bingley; “and I am inclined to think that you would not wish to see your sister make such an exhibition.”
paras.uz: «Siz buni payqagansiz, janob Darsi, ishonchim komil, — dedi miss Bingli, — va menimcha, siz singlingizning bunday tomosha ko'rsatishini istamagan bo'lardingiz».

paras.en: “Certainly not.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, yo'q».

paras.en: “To walk three miles, or four miles, or five miles, or whatever it is, above her ankles in dirt, and alone, quite alone! What could she mean by it? It seems to me to show an abominable sort of conceited independence, a most country-town indifference to decorum.”
paras.uz: «To'pig'idan yuqori loyga botib, yolg'iz, butunlay yolg'iz uch mil, yoki to'rt mil, yoki besh mil, yoki qancha bo'lsa ham, yurish! Bu bilan u nima demoqchi edi? Menimcha, bu o'ziga bino qo'ygan jirkanch mustaqillikni, odob-axloqqa provinsial shaharchalarga xos befarqlikni ko'rsatadi».

paras.en: “It shows an affection for her sister that is very pleasing,” said Bingley.
paras.uz: «Bu opasiga bo'lgan juda yoqimli mehrni ko'rsatadi», — dedi Bingli.

paras.en: “I am afraid, Mr. Darcy,” observed Miss Bingley in a half whisper, “that this adventure has rather affected your admiration of her fine eyes.”
paras.uz: «Qo'rqaman, janob Darsi, — dedi miss Bingli yarim shivirlab, — bu sarguzasht uning chiroyli ko'zlariga bo'lgan hayratingizga biroz ta'sir qilgandir».

paras.en: “Not at all,” he replied; “they were brightened by the exercise.” A short pause followed this speech, and Mrs. Hurst began again:
paras.uz: «Aslo, — dedi u, — ular harakatdan yanada yorqinlashgan edi». Bu gapdan keyin qisqa sukunat cho'kdi va missis Xerst yana gap boshladi:

paras.en: “I have an excessive regard for Miss Jane Bennet, she is really a very sweet girl, and I wish with all my heart she were well settled. But with such a father and mother, and such low connections, I am afraid there is no chance of it.”
paras.uz: «Men miss Jeyn Bennetni juda hurmat qilaman, u chindan ham juda shirin qiz va chin dildan uning yaxshi turmush qurishini tilayman. Lekin shunday otasi va onasi, shunday past qarindoshlari bilan bunga imkoniyat yo'q deb qo'rqaman».

paras.en: “I think I have heard you say that their uncle is an attorney in Meryton.”
paras.uz: «Ularning amakisi Meritonda advokat ekanini aytganingizni eshitgandekman».

paras.en: “Yes; and they have another, who lives somewhere near Cheapside.”
paras.uz: «Ha; yana bittasi bor, Cheapside yaqinida qayerdadir yashaydi».

paras.en: “That is capital,” added her sister, and they both laughed heartily.
paras.uz: «Bu ajoyib», — deb qo'shib qo'ydi singlisi va ikkalasi qah-qah urib kulishdi.

paras.en: “If they had uncles enough to fill all Cheapside,” cried Bingley, “it would not make them one jot less agreeable.”
paras.uz: «Agar ularning butun Cheapsideni to'ldiradigan darajada ko'p amakilari bo'lsa ham, — deb qichqirdi Bingli, — bu ularni zarracha ham kamroq yoqimli qilmaydi».

paras.en: “But it must very materially lessen their chance of marrying men of any consideration in the world,” replied Darcy.
paras.uz: «Lekin bu ularning dunyoda biror obro'ga ega erkaklarga turmushga chiqish imkoniyatini juda sezilarli kamaytiradi», — dedi Darsi.

paras.en: To this speech Bingley made no answer; but his sisters gave it their hearty assent, and indulged their mirth for some time at the expense of their dear friend's vulgar relations.
paras.uz: Bu gapga Bingli javob bermadi; lekin opa-singillari unga chin dildan qo'shilishdi va bir muddat aziz dugonalarining past qarindoshlari hisobiga ermak qilishdi.

paras.en: With a renewal of tenderness, however, they returned to her room on leaving the dining-parlour, and sat with her till summoned to coffee. She was still very poorly, and Elizabeth would not quit her at all, till late in the evening, when she had the comfort of seeing her sleep, and when it seemed to her rather right than pleasant that she should go downstairs herself. On entering the drawing-room she found the whole party at loo, and was immediately invited to join them; but suspecting them to be playing high she declined it, and making her sister the excuse, said she would amuse herself for the short time she could stay below, with a book. Mr. Hurst looked at her with astonishment.
paras.uz: Biroq ovqat xonasidan chiqishgach, ular yangilangan mehribonlik bilan uning xonasiga qaytishdi va qahvaga chaqirilgunlaricha uning yonida o'tirishdi. U hali ham juda betob edi va Elizabet uni umuman tashlab ketmadi — toki kech oqshomda uning uxlab qolganini ko'rib taskin topguncha va o'zining pastga tushishi yoqimli bo'lmasa-da, to'g'riroq ekanini his qilguncha. Mehmonxonaga kirib, u butun davrani lu o'ynayotgan holda topdi va darhol unga qo'shilishga taklif qilishdi; lekin ular katta pulga o'ynayotganidan shubhalanib, rad etdi va opasini bahona qilib, pastda qola oladigan qisqa vaqtni kitob bilan o'tkazishini aytdi. Janob Xerst unga hayrat bilan qaradi.

paras.en: “Do you prefer reading to cards?” said he; “that is rather singular.”
paras.uz: «Kartadan ko'ra o'qishni afzal ko'rasizmi? — dedi u. — Bu ancha g'alati».

paras.en: “Miss Eliza Bennet,” said Miss Bingley, “despises cards. She is a great reader, and has no pleasure in anything else.”
paras.uz: «Miss Eliza Bennet, — dedi miss Bingli, — kartani mensimaydi. U katta kitobxon va boshqa hech narsadan zavq olmaydi».

paras.en: “I deserve neither such praise nor such censure,” cried Elizabeth; “I am not a great reader, and I have pleasure in many things.”
paras.uz: «Men na bunday maqtovga, na bunday tanqidga loyiqman, — deb xitob qildi Elizabet. — Men katta kitobxon emasman va ko'p narsalardan zavq olaman».

paras.en: “In nursing your sister I am sure you have pleasure,” said Bingley; “and I hope it will be soon increased by seeing her quite well.”
paras.uz: «Opangizga qarashdan zavq olishingizga ishonaman, — dedi Bingli, — va umid qilamanki, uni butunlay sog'ayganini ko'rib, bu zavq tez orada ortadi».

paras.en: Elizabeth thanked him from her heart, and then walked towards the table where a few books were lying. He immediately offered to fetch her others--all that his library afforded.
paras.uz: Elizabet unga chin dildan minnatdorchilik bildirdi va bir nechta kitob yotgan stol tomon yurdi. U darhol unga boshqalarini — kutubxonasida bor hamma kitoblarni olib kelishni taklif qildi.

paras.en: “And I wish my collection were larger for your benefit and my own credit; but I am an idle fellow, and though I have not many, I have more than I ever looked into.”
paras.uz: «Sizning foydangiz va o'z obro'yim uchun to'plamim kattaroq bo'lishini istardim; lekin men dangasa odamman, kitoblarim ko'p bo'lmasa ham, hech qachon ochib ko'rmaganlarim ko'proq».

paras.en: Elizabeth assured him that she could suit herself perfectly with those in the room.
paras.uz: Elizabet uni xonadagi kitoblardan bemalol tanlab olishiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “I am astonished,” said Miss Bingley, “that my father should have left so small a collection of books. What a delightful library you have at Pemberley, Mr. Darcy!”
paras.uz: «Hayronman, — dedi miss Bingli, — otam shunchalik kichik kitob to'plami qoldirgan ekan. Pemberlida qanday ajoyib kutubxonangiz bor, janob Darsi!»

paras.en: “It ought to be good,” he replied, “it has been the work of many generations.”
paras.uz: «U yaxshi bo'lishi kerak, — dedi u, — bu ko'p avlodlarning mehnati».

paras.en: “And then you have added so much to it yourself, you are always buying books.”
paras.uz: «Keyin unga o'zingiz ham shunchalik ko'p qo'shdingiz, doim kitob sotib olasiz».

paras.en: “I cannot comprehend the neglect of a family library in such days as these.”
paras.uz: «Bunday zamonda oila kutubxonasiga e'tiborsizlikni tushuna olmayman».

paras.en: “Neglect! I am sure you neglect nothing that can add to the beauties of that noble place. Charles, when you build your house, I wish it may be half as delightful as Pemberley.”
paras.uz: «E'tiborsizlik! Ishonamanki, siz o'sha muhtasham joyning go'zalligiga qo'shilishi mumkin bo'lgan hech narsani e'tiborsiz qoldirmaysiz. Charlz, uyingni qurganingda, u Pemberlining yarmichalik ham ajoyib bo'lishini istardim».

paras.en: “I wish it may.”
paras.uz: «Men ham shuni istardim».

paras.en: “But I would really advise you to make your purchase in that neighbourhood, and take Pemberley for a kind of model. There is not a finer county in England than Derbyshire.”
paras.uz: «Lekin men senga rostdan ham o'sha atrofdan yer sotib olishni va Pemberlini o'ziga xos namuna qilib olishni maslahat bergan bo'lardim. Angliyada Derbishirdan yaxshiroq grafllik yo'q».

paras.en: “With all my heart; I will buy Pemberley itself if Darcy will sell it.”
paras.uz: «Chin dildan; agar Darsi sotsa, Pemberlining o'zini sotib olaman».

paras.en: “I am talking of possibilities, Charles.”
paras.uz: «Men imkoniyatlar haqida gapiryapman, Charlz».

paras.en: “Upon my word, Caroline, I should think it more possible to get Pemberley by purchase than by imitation.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan aytaman, Karolayn, menimcha, Pemberliga taqlid qilishdan ko'ra uni sotib olish osonroq».

paras.en: Elizabeth was so much caught with what passed, as to leave her very little attention for her book; and soon laying it wholly aside, she drew near the card-table, and stationed herself between Mr. Bingley and his eldest sister, to observe the game.
paras.uz: Elizabet bo'layotgan gaplarga shunchalik berilib ketdiki, kitobiga deyarli e'tibor qolmadi; tez orada uni butunlay chetga qo'yib, karta stoliga yaqinlashdi va o'yinni kuzatish uchun janob Bingli bilan uning katta opasi o'rtasida turdi.

paras.en: “Is Miss Darcy much grown since the spring?” said Miss Bingley; “will she be as tall as I am?”
paras.uz: «Miss Darsi bahordan beri ancha o'sdimi? — dedi miss Bingli. — Mendek baland bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “I think she will. She is now about Miss Elizabeth Bennet's height, or rather taller.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, bo'ladi. Hozir u miss Elizabet Bennet bo'yicha, balki biroz balandroqdir».

paras.en: “How I long to see her again! I never met with anybody who delighted me so much. Such a countenance, such manners! And so extremely accomplished for her age! Her performance on the pianoforte is exquisite.”
paras.uz: «Uni yana ko'rishni qanchalik orziqib kutyapman! Hech kim menga bunchalik yoqmagan. Qanday chehra, qanday muomala! Yoshiga nisbatan nihoyatda har tomonlama yetuk! Uning fortepianoda chalishi ajoyib».

paras.en: “It is amazing to me,” said Bingley, “how young ladies can have patience to be so very accomplished as they all are.”
paras.uz: «Men uchun hayratlanarli, — dedi Bingli, — yosh xonimlar hammasi bunchalik har tomonlama yetuk bo'lishga qanday qilib sabr topishadi».

paras.en: “All young ladies accomplished! My dear Charles, what do you mean?”
paras.uz: «Hamma yosh xonimlar har tomonlama yetuk! Aziz Charlz, nima demoqchisan?»

paras.en: “Yes, all of them, I think. They all paint tables, cover screens, and net purses. I scarcely know anyone who cannot do all this, and I am sure I never heard a young lady spoken of for the first time, without being informed that she was very accomplished.”
paras.uz: «Ha, hammasi, menimcha. Hammasi stollarga rasm chizadi, pardalarni bezaydi, hamyon to'qiydi. Bularning hammasini qila olmaydigan birorta odamni deyarli bilmayman va ishonamanki, biror yosh xonim haqida birinchi marta gapirilganda, uning juda har tomonlama yetuk ekani aytilmaganini hech qachon eshitmaganman».

paras.en: “Your list of the common extent of accomplishments,” said Darcy, “has too much truth. The word is applied to many a woman who deserves it no otherwise than by netting a purse or covering a screen. But I am very far from agreeing with you in your estimation of ladies in general. I cannot boast of knowing more than half-a-dozen, in the whole range of my acquaintance, that are really accomplished.”
paras.uz: «Sizning hunarlarning odatiy doirasi ro'yxatingizda haqiqat juda ko'p, — dedi Darsi. — Bu so'z ko'plab ayollarga faqat hamyon to'qigani yoki parda bezagani uchun ishlatiladi. Lekin men umuman xonimlarni baholashda siz bilan aslo kelisha olmayman. Butun tanishlarim doirasida haqiqatan ham har tomonlama yetuk bo'lgan yarim o'nlabdan ortiq ayolni bilaman deb maqtana olmayman».

paras.en: “Nor I, I am sure,” said Miss Bingley.
paras.uz: «Men ham, albatta», — dedi miss Bingli.

paras.en: “Then,” observed Elizabeth, “you must comprehend a great deal in your idea of an accomplished woman.”
paras.uz: «Unda, — dedi Elizabet, — sizning har tomonlama yetuk ayol haqidagi tasavvuringizga juda ko'p narsa kirsa kerak».

paras.en: “Yes, I do comprehend a great deal in it.”
paras.uz: «Ha, unga juda ko'p narsani kiritaman».

paras.en: “Oh! certainly,” cried his faithful assistant, “no one can be really esteemed accomplished who does not greatly surpass what is usually met with. A woman must have a thorough knowledge of music, singing, drawing, dancing, and the modern languages, to deserve the word; and besides all this, she must possess a certain something in her air and manner of walking, the tone of her voice, her address and expressions, or the word will be but half-deserved.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Albatta, — deb qichqirdi uning sodiq yordamchisi, — odatda uchraydigan narsadan ancha ustun bo'lmagan hech kim chindan har tomonlama yetuk deb hisoblanishi mumkin emas. Bu so'zga loyiq bo'lish uchun ayol musiqa, qo'shiq, rasm, raqs va zamonaviy tillarni puxta bilishi kerak; bularning hammasidan tashqari, uning qiyofasi va yurishida, ovozining ohangida, muomalasi va ifodalarida qandaydir alohida bir narsa bo'lishi kerak, aks holda bu so'zga faqat yarim loyiq bo'ladi».

paras.en: “All this she must possess,” added Darcy, “and to all this she must yet add something more substantial, in the improvement of her mind by extensive reading.”
paras.uz: «Bularning hammasi unda bo'lishi kerak, — deb qo'shimcha qildi Darsi, — va bularning hammasiga yana bir muhimroq narsani — keng mutolaa orqali aqlini rivojlantirishni qo'shishi kerak».

paras.en: “I am no longer surprised at your knowing only six accomplished women. I rather wonder now at your knowing any.”
paras.uz: «Endi sizning faqat oltita har tomonlama yetuk ayolni bilishingizdan hayron emasman. Aksincha, endi umuman birortasini bilishingizdan hayronman».

paras.en: “Are you so severe upon your own sex as to doubt the possibility of all this?”
paras.uz: «Nahotki o'z jinsingizga shunchalik qattiqqo'l bo'lsangizki, bularning barchasi mumkinligiga shubha qilsangiz?»

paras.en: “I never saw such a woman. I never saw such capacity, and taste, and application, and elegance, as you describe united.”
paras.uz: «Men hech qachon bunday ayolni ko'rmaganman. Siz tasvirlagan qobiliyat, did, tirishqoqlik va nafislikning birgalikda bo'lganini hech qachon ko'rmaganman».

paras.en: Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley both cried out against the injustice of her implied doubt, and were both protesting that they knew many women who answered this description, when Mr. Hurst called them to order, with bitter complaints of their inattention to what was going forward. As all conversation was thereby at an end, Elizabeth soon afterwards left the room.
paras.uz: Missis Xerst va miss Bingli ikkalasi ham uning shama qilingan shubhasining adolatsizligiga qarshi chiqib, bunday tavsifga mos keladigan ko'plab ayollarni bilishlarini aytayotgan edilarki, janob Xerst bo'layotgan o'yinga e'tiborsizliklaridan qattiq shikoyat qilib, ularni tartibga chaqirdi. Shu bilan butun suhbat tugagani uchun Elizabet tez orada xonadan chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: “Elizabeth Bennet,” said Miss Bingley, when the door was closed on her, “is one of those young ladies who seek to recommend themselves to the other sex by undervaluing their own; and with many men, I dare say, it succeeds. But, in my opinion, it is a paltry device, a very mean art.”
paras.uz: «Elizabet Bennet, — dedi miss Bingli, eshik uning ortidan yopilgach, — o'z jinsini kamsitib, o'zini boshqa jinsga yaxshi ko'rsatishga intiladigan yosh xonimlardan. Ko'p erkaklarda bu, ishonamanki, ish beradi. Lekin menimcha, bu arzimas nayrang, juda past hiyla».

paras.en: “Undoubtedly,” replied Darcy, to whom this remark was chiefly addressed, “there is a meanness in all the arts which ladies sometimes condescend to employ for captivation. Whatever bears affinity to cunning is despicable.”
paras.uz: «Shubhasiz, — dedi asosan bu gap qaratilgan Darsi, — xonimlar ba'zan maftun qilish uchun qo'llashga tushadigan barcha hiylalarda pastkashlik bor. Ayyorlikka yaqin bo'lgan har qanday narsa jirkanchdir».

paras.en: Miss Bingley was not so entirely satisfied with this reply as to continue the subject.
paras.uz: Miss Bingli bu javobdan mavzuni davom ettiradigan darajada mamnun bo'lmadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth joined them again only to say that her sister was worse, and that she could not leave her. Bingley urged Mr. Jones being sent for immediately; while his sisters, convinced that no country advice could be of any service, recommended an express to town for one of the most eminent physicians. This she would not hear of; but she was not so unwilling to comply with their brother's proposal; and it was settled that Mr. Jones should be sent for early in the morning, if Miss Bennet were not decidedly better. Bingley was quite uncomfortable; his sisters declared that they were miserable. They solaced their wretchedness, however, by duets after supper, while he could find no better relief to his feelings than by giving his housekeeper directions that every attention might be paid to the sick lady and her sister.
paras.uz: Elizabet ularning oldiga faqat opasining ahvoli yomonlashganini va uni tashlab keta olmasligini aytish uchun qaytdi. Bingli darhol janob Jonsni chaqirtirishni qistadi; opa-singillari esa qishloq maslahati hech qanday foyda bermasligiga ishonib, eng mashhur shifokorlardan birini chaqirish uchun Londonga shoshilinch chopar jo'natishni tavsiya qilishdi. Elizabet bunga quloq ham solmadi; lekin akalarining taklifiga rozi bo'lishga unchalik qarshi emasdi; agar miss Bennet sezilarli darajada yaxshilanmasa, ertalab erta janob Jonsni chaqirtirishga kelishildi. Bingli o'zini juda noqulay his qildi; opa-singillari esa juda baxtsiz ekanliklarini e'lon qilishdi. Biroq ular baxtsizliklarini kechki ovqatdan keyin duetlar kuylab ovutishdi, u esa o'z his-tuyg'ulariga uy bekasiga bemor xonim va uning singlisiga har tomonlama e'tibor ko'rsatish haqida ko'rsatma berishdan yaxshiroq taskin topa olmadi.

gloss.ex: It seems to me to show an abominable sort of conceited independence, a most country-town indifference to decorum.”
