quiz.q: What do Miss Bingley and Mrs. Hurst do when Elizabeth leaves the room?
quiz.why_uz: Ular Elizabetning ko'rinishini masxara qilishadi, Bingley esa uni himoya qiladi.

quiz.q: What does Darcy add to the list of an accomplished woman?
o: The improvement of her mind by extensive reading
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet bunday ayolni hech qachon ko'rmaganini aytadi.

chapters.title: Mrs. Bennet Visits
chapters.recap_uz: Missis Bennet qizlari bilan Netherfieldga keladi va o'zini uyatli tutadi: Darsiga qishloq hayoti haqida bahslashadi. Lidiya Bingleydan bal o'tkazishni talab qiladi.

paras.en: Elizabeth passed the chief of the night in her sister's room, and in the morning had the pleasure of being able to send a tolerable answer to the inquiries which she very early received from Mr. Bingley by a housemaid, and some time afterwards from the two elegant ladies who waited on his sisters. In spite of this amendment, however, she requested to have a note sent to Longbourn, desiring her mother to visit Jane, and form her own judgement of her situation. The note was immediately dispatched, and its contents as quickly complied with. Mrs. Bennet, accompanied by her two youngest girls, reached Netherfield soon after the family breakfast.
paras.uz: Elizabet tunning ko'p qismini opasining xonasida o'tkazdi va ertalab janob Bingli oqsoch orqali juda erta yuborgan so'roqqa, biroz keyin esa uning opa-singillariga xizmat qiladigan ikki nafis xizmatkor ayol orqali kelgan so'roqlarga ancha qoniqarli javob yuborish baxtiga muyassar bo'ldi. Biroq bu yaxshilanishga qaramay, u Longbornga xat yuborishni so'radi va onasidan Jeynni ko'rgani kelib, uning ahvoli haqida o'zi xulosa chiqarishini iltimos qildi. Xat darhol jo'natildi va uning mazmuni xuddi shunday tez bajarildi. Missis Bennet ikki kichik qizi bilan oilaviy nonushtadan ko'p o'tmay Nezerfildga yetib keldi.

paras.en: Had she found Jane in any apparent danger, Mrs. Bennet would have been very miserable; but being satisfied on seeing her that her illness was not alarming, she had no wish of her recovering immediately, as her restoration to health would probably remove her from Netherfield. She would not listen, therefore, to her daughter's proposal of being carried home; neither did the apothecary, who arrived about the same time, think it at all advisable. After sitting a little while with Jane, on Miss Bingley's appearance and invitation, the mother and three daughters all attended her into the breakfast parlour. Bingley met them with hopes that Mrs. Bennet had not found Miss Bennet worse than she expected.
paras.uz: Agar Jeynni biror aniq xavf ostida topganida, missis Bennet juda baxtsiz bo'lardi; lekin uni ko'rib, kasalligi xavotirli emasligiga ishonch hosil qilgach, uning darhol tuzalishini istamadi, chunki sog'ayishi, ehtimol, uni Nezerfilddan olib ketgan bo'lardi. Shuning uchun u qizining uyga olib ketish haqidagi taklifiga quloq solmadi; deyarli shu paytda kelgan dorishunos ham buni umuman maqsadga muvofiq deb hisoblamadi. Jeyn bilan biroz o'tirgandan keyin, miss Bingli kelib taklif qilgach, ona va uch qiz uning ortidan nonushta xonasiga tushishdi. Bingli ularni missis Bennet miss Bennetni kutganidan yomonroq ahvolda topmagan bo'lsa kerak, degan umid bilan kutib oldi.

paras.en: “Indeed I have, sir,” was her answer. “She is a great deal too ill to be moved. Mr. Jones says we must not think of moving her. We must trespass a little longer on your kindness.”
paras.uz: «Topdim, ser, — deb javob berdi u. — U ko'chirish uchun haddan tashqari kasal. Janob Jons uni ko'chirishni o'ylamasligimiz kerakligini aytyapti. Biz yana bir oz mehribonligingizni suiiste'mol qilishimizga to'g'ri keladi».

paras.en: “Removed!” cried Bingley. “It must not be thought of. My sister, I am sure, will not hear of her removal.”
paras.uz: «Ko'chirish! — deb xitob qildi Bingli. — Buni o'ylash ham mumkin emas. Ishonamanki, singlim uni ko'chirish haqida eshitishni ham istamaydi».

paras.en: “You may depend upon it, Madam,” said Miss Bingley, with cold civility, “that Miss Bennet will receive every possible attention while she remains with us.”
paras.uz: «Ishonavering, xonim, — dedi miss Bingli sovuq xushmuomalalik bilan, — miss Bennet biz bilan qolgan vaqtida unga mumkin bo'lgan barcha e'tibor ko'rsatiladi».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet was profuse in her acknowledgments.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet minnatdorchilik bildirishda mo'l-ko'l edi.

paras.en: “I am sure,” she added, “if it was not for such good friends I do not know what would become of her, for she is very ill indeed, and suffers a vast deal, though with the greatest patience in the world, which is always the way with her, for she has, without exception, the sweetest temper I have ever met with. I often tell my other girls they are nothing to her. You have a sweet room here, Mr. Bingley, and a charming prospect over the gravel walk. I do not know a place in the country that is equal to Netherfield. You will not think of quitting it in a hurry, I hope, though you have but a short lease.”
paras.uz: «Ishonaman, — deb qo'shib qo'ydi u, — agar bunday yaxshi do'stlar bo'lmaganida, uning holi nima bo'lardi, bilmayman, chunki u chindan ham juda kasal va ko'p azob chekyapti, garchi dunyodagi eng katta sabr bilan bo'lsa ham — u doim shunday, chunki istisnosiz, men uchratgan eng yoqimli fe'lli qiz. Boshqa qizlarimga ko'pincha ular unga yetolmaydi, deb aytaman. Bu yerda sizning yoqimli xonangiz bor, janob Bingli, shag'al yo'lka tomonga maftunkor manzara ochiladi. Grafllikda Nezerfildga teng keladigan joyni bilmayman. Umid qilamanki, ijara muddatingiz qisqa bo'lsa ham, uni shoshib tashlab ketishni o'ylamaysiz».

paras.en: “Whatever I do is done in a hurry,” replied he; “and therefore if I should resolve to quit Netherfield, I should probably be off in five minutes. At present, however, I consider myself as quite fixed here.”
paras.uz: «Men nima qilsam, shoshib qilaman, — dedi u, — shuning uchun agar Nezerfildni tashlab ketishga qaror qilsam, ehtimol, besh daqiqada jo'nab ketardim. Biroq hozircha o'zimni bu yerda butunlay o'rnashgan deb hisoblayman».

paras.en: “That is exactly what I should have supposed of you,” said Elizabeth.
paras.uz: «Men siz haqingizda aynan shunday deb o'ylagan bo'lardim», — dedi Elizabet.

paras.en: “You begin to comprehend me, do you?” cried he, turning towards her.
paras.uz: «Meni tushuna boshlayapsizmi?» — deb xitob qildi u unga o'girilib.

paras.en: “Oh! yes--I understand you perfectly.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Ha — sizni mukammal tushunaman».

paras.en: “I wish I might take this for a compliment; but to be so easily seen through I am afraid is pitiful.”
paras.uz: «Buni maqtov deb qabul qilishni istardim; lekin bunchalik oson tushunilish, qo'rqaman, achinarli».

paras.en: “That is as it happens. It does not follow that a deep, intricate character is more or less estimable than such a one as yours.”
paras.uz: «Bu vaziyatga bog'liq. Chuqur, murakkab xarakter siznikidek xarakterdan ko'proq yoki kamroq qadrli bo'lishi shart emas».

paras.en: “Lizzy,” cried her mother, “remember where you are, and do not run on in the wild manner that you are suffered to do at home.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, — deb qichqirdi onasi, — qayerdaligingni esla, uyda senga ruxsat berilgandek yovvoyilarcha gapiraverma».

paras.en: “I did not know before,” continued Bingley immediately, “that you were a studier of character. It must be an amusing study.”
paras.uz: «Men avval bilmagan ekanman, — dedi darhol Bingli, — siz xarakterlarni o'rganuvchi ekansiz. Bu qiziqarli mashg'ulot bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “Yes, but intricate characters are the most amusing. They have at least that advantage.”
paras.uz: «Ha, lekin murakkab xarakterlar eng qiziqarlisi. Hech bo'lmasa ularning shunday afzalligi bor».

paras.en: “The country,” said Darcy, “can in general supply but a few subjects for such a study. In a country neighbourhood you move in a very confined and unvarying society.”
paras.uz: «Qishloq, — dedi Darsi, — umuman olganda bunday o'rganish uchun juda oz obyekt bera oladi. Qishloq mahallasida juda tor va o'zgarmas jamiyatda yurasiz».

paras.en: “But people themselves alter so much, that there is something new to be observed in them for ever.”
paras.uz: «Lekin odamlarning o'zlari shunchalik o'zgaradiki, ularda doim kuzatishga arziydigan yangi narsa bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Yes, indeed,” cried Mrs. Bennet, offended by his manner of mentioning a country neighbourhood. “I assure you there is quite as much of that going on in the country as in town.”
paras.uz: «Ha, albatta, — deb qichqirdi uning qishloq mahallasini tilga olish tarzidan ranjigan missis Bennet. — Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, qishloqda ham shaharda qanchalik bo'lsa, shunchalik bo'ladi».

paras.en: Everybody was surprised, and Darcy, after looking at her for a moment, turned silently away. Mrs. Bennet, who fancied she had gained a complete victory over him, continued her triumph.
paras.uz: Hamma hayron qoldi, Darsi esa unga bir lahza qarab, indamay yuzini burdi. U ustidan to'liq g'alaba qozondim deb o'ylagan missis Bennet tantanasini davom ettirdi.

paras.en: “I cannot see that London has any great advantage over the country, for my part, except the shops and public places. The country is a vast deal pleasanter, is it not, Mr. Bingley?”
paras.uz: «Men o'zim Londonning qishloqdan katta afzalligi borligini ko'rmayapman, do'konlar va jamoat joylaridan tashqari. Qishloq ancha yoqimliroq, shunday emasmi, janob Bingli?»

paras.en: “When I am in the country,” he replied, “I never wish to leave it; and when I am in town it is pretty much the same. They have each their advantages, and I can be equally happy in either.”
paras.uz: «Qishloqda bo'lganimda, — dedi u, — hech qachon uni tark etishni istamayman; shaharda bo'lganimda ham deyarli shunday. Ikkalasining ham o'z afzalliklari bor, men ikkalasida ham bir xil baxtli bo'la olaman».

paras.en: “Aye--that is because you have the right disposition. But that gentleman,” looking at Darcy, “seemed to think the country was nothing at all.”
paras.uz: «Ha — chunki sizning fe'lingiz to'g'ri. Lekin anavi janob, — Darsiga qarab, — qishloqni umuman hech narsa emas deb o'ylaganga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Indeed, Mamma, you are mistaken,” said Elizabeth, blushing for her mother. “You quite mistook Mr. Darcy. He only meant that there was not such a variety of people to be met with in the country as in the town, which you must acknowledge to be true.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan, oyijon, siz adashyapsiz, — dedi Elizabet onasi uchun qizarib. — Siz janob Darsini butunlay noto'g'ri tushundingiz. U faqat qishloqda shahardagidek turli-tuman odamlarni uchratib bo'lmasligini aytmoqchi edi, buning to'g'riligini tan olishingiz kerak».

paras.en: “Certainly, my dear, nobody said there were; but as to not meeting with many people in this neighbourhood, I believe there are few neighbourhoods larger. I know we dine with four-and-twenty families.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, azizim, hech kim bor demadi; lekin bu mahallada ko'p odam bilan uchrashmaslikka kelsak, menimcha, bundan kattaroq mahallalar kam. Bilaman, biz yigirma to'rt oila bilan tushlik qilamiz».

paras.en: Nothing but concern for Elizabeth could enable Bingley to keep his countenance. His sister was less delicate, and directed her eyes towards Mr. Darcy with a very expressive smile. Elizabeth, for the sake of saying something that might turn her mother's thoughts, now asked her if Charlotte Lucas had been at Longbourn since her coming away.
paras.uz: Faqat Elizabetga bo'lgan hamdardlikkina Binglining kulib yubormasligiga imkon berdi. Singlisi kamroq nozik edi va juda ma'noli tabassum bilan ko'zlarini janob Darsiga qaratdi. Elizabet onasining fikrini boshqa tomonga burish uchun biror gap aytish maqsadida endi undan Sharlotta Lukas o'zi ketganidan beri Longbornga kelganmi, deb so'radi.

paras.en: “Yes, she called yesterday with her father. What an agreeable man Sir William is, Mr. Bingley, is not he? So much the man of fashion! So genteel and easy! He has always something to say to everybody. That is my idea of good breeding; and those persons who fancy themselves very important, and never open their mouths, quite mistake the matter.”
paras.uz: «Ha, kecha otasi bilan kelgan edi. Ser Uilyam qanday yoqimli odam, janob Bingli, shunday emasmi? Qanday zamonaviy odam! Shunday nazokatli va erkin! Uning hammaga doim aytadigan gapi bor. Men yaxshi tarbiya deb shuni tushunaman; o'zlarini juda muhim deb o'ylab, hech qachon og'iz ochmaydigan odamlar esa masalani butunlay noto'g'ri tushunishadi».

paras.en: “Did Charlotte dine with you?”
paras.uz: «Sharlotta siz bilan tushlik qildimi?»

paras.en: “No, she would go home. I fancy she was wanted about the mince-pies. For my part, Mr. Bingley, I always keep servants that can do their own work; my daughters are brought up very differently. But everybody is to judge for themselves, and the Lucases are a very good sort of girls, I assure you. It is a pity they are not handsome! Not that I think Charlotte so very plain--but then she is our particular friend.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, u uyga ketaman, dedi. Menimcha, uni qiyma pishiriqlar uchun kutishgan bo'lsa kerak. Men o'zim, janob Bingli, doim o'z ishini o'zi bajara oladigan xizmatkorlar saqlayman; qizlarim butunlay boshqacha tarbiyalangan. Lekin har kim o'zi uchun hukm qiladi, Lukas qizlari esa juda yaxshi qizlar, sizni ishontiraman. Afsuski, chiroyli emaslar! Sharlottani unchalik xunuk deb o'ylayman demoqchi emasman — axir u bizning yaqin do'stimiz».

paras.en: “She seems a very pleasant young woman.”
paras.uz: «U juda yoqimli yosh ayolga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Oh! dear, yes; but you must own she is very plain. Lady Lucas herself has often said so, and envied me Jane's beauty. I do not like to boast of my own child, but to be sure, Jane--one does not often see anybody better looking. It is what everybody says. I do not trust my own partiality. When she was only fifteen, there was a man at my brother Gardiner's in town so much in love with her that my sister-in-law was sure he would make her an offer before we came away. But, however, he did not. Perhaps he thought her too young. However, he wrote some verses on her, and very pretty they were.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Albatta; lekin uning juda xunukligini tan olishingiz kerak. Ledi Lukasning o'zi buni ko'p marta aytgan va Jeynning go'zalligi uchun menga havas qilgan. O'z farzandim bilan maqtanishni yoqtirmayman, lekin, albatta, Jeyn — undan chiroyliroq odamni kamdan-kam ko'rasiz. Hamma shunday deydi. Men o'zimning tarafkashligimga ishonmayman. U endigina o'n besh yoshda bo'lganida, Londonda akam Gardinernikida bir odam unga shunchalik oshiq bo'lgan ediki, kelinoyim biz ketishimizdan oldin u unga taklif qiladi, deb ishongan edi. Biroq u taklif qilmadi. Balki uni juda yosh deb o'ylagandir. Biroq u unga bag'ishlab she'rlar yozdi, juda chiroyli she'rlar edi».

paras.en: “And so ended his affection,” said Elizabeth impatiently. “There has been many a one, I fancy, overcome in the same way. I wonder who first discovered the efficacy of poetry in driving away love!”
paras.uz: «Shunday qilib uning muhabbati tugadi, — dedi Elizabet sabrsizlanib. — Menimcha, ko'plar xuddi shunday yengilgan. Kim birinchi bo'lib she'riyatning muhabbatni quvib chiqarishdagi samaradorligini kashf qilgan ekan!»

paras.en: “I have been used to consider poetry as the food of love,” said Darcy.
paras.uz: «Men she'riyatni muhabbatning ozuqasi deb hisoblashga odatlangan edim», — dedi Darsi.

paras.en: “Of a fine, stout, healthy love it may. Everything nourishes what is strong already. But if it be only a slight, thin sort of inclination, I am convinced that one good sonnet will starve it entirely away.”
paras.uz: «Yaxshi, baquvvat, sog'lom muhabbatnikidir, ehtimol. Allaqachon kuchli bo'lgan narsani hamma narsa oziqlantiradi. Lekin agar bu yengil, ingichka moyillik bo'lsa, ishonchim komilki, bitta yaxshi sonet uni butunlay ochdan o'ldiradi».

paras.en: Darcy only smiled; and the general pause which ensued made Elizabeth tremble lest her mother should be exposing herself again. She longed to speak, but could think of nothing to say; and after a short silence Mrs. Bennet began repeating her thanks to Mr. Bingley for his kindness to Jane, with an apology for troubling him also with Lizzy. Mr. Bingley was unaffectedly civil in his answer, and forced his younger sister to be civil also, and say what the occasion required. She performed her part indeed without much graciousness, but Mrs. Bennet was satisfied, and soon afterwards ordered her carriage. Upon this signal, the youngest of her daughters put herself forward. The two girls had been whispering to each other during the whole visit, and the result of it was, that the youngest should tax Mr. Bingley with having promised on his first coming into the country to give a ball at Netherfield.
paras.uz: Darsi faqat jilmaydi; keyin cho'kkan umumiy sukunat Elizabetni onasi yana o'zini sharmanda qilmasin, deb titratdi. U gapirishni juda istardi, lekin aytadigan hech narsa o'ylab topa olmadi; qisqa sukunatdan keyin missis Bennet janob Bingliga Jeynga ko'rsatgan mehribonligi uchun minnatdorchiligini takrorlay boshladi va uni Lizzi bilan ham bezovta qilgani uchun uzr so'radi. Janob Bingli javobida samimiy xushmuomala bo'ldi va kichik singlisini ham xushmuomala bo'lishga, vaziyat talab qilgan gaplarni aytishga majbur qildi. To'g'ri, u o'z rolini unchalik iltifot bilan bajarmadi, lekin missis Bennet mamnun bo'ldi va ko'p o'tmay aravasini keltirishni buyurdi. Bu ishoradan keyin qizlarining eng kichigi oldinga chiqdi. Ikki qiz butun tashrif davomida bir-biri bilan shivirlashgan edi va buning natijasi shu bo'ldiki, eng kichigi janob Binglidan qishloqqa ilk kelganida Nezerfildda bal berishga va'da berganini talab qilishi kerak edi.

paras.en: Lydia was a stout, well-grown girl of fifteen, with a fine complexion and good-humoured countenance; a favourite with her mother, whose affection had brought her into public at an early age. She had high animal spirits, and a sort of natural self-consequence, which the attention of the officers, to whom her uncle's good dinners, and her own easy manners recommended her, had increased into assurance. She was very equal, therefore, to address Mr. Bingley on the subject of the ball, and abruptly reminded him of his promise; adding, that it would be the most shameful thing in the world if he did not keep it. His answer to this sudden attack was delightful to their mother's ear:
paras.uz: Lidiya o'n besh yoshli, baquvvat, yaxshi o'sgan, yuzi tiniq va xushchaqchaq qiz edi; onasining erkatoyi edi, onasining mehri uni erta yoshdan jamiyatga olib chiqqan edi. Unda kuchli tabiiy g'ayrat va qandaydir tug'ma o'ziga ishonch bor edi; amakisining yaxshi ziyofatlari va o'zining erkin muomalasi tufayli ofitserlarning e'tibori bu ishonchni surbetlikka aylantirgan edi. Shuning uchun u janob Bingliga bal haqida murojaat qilishga to'liq qodir edi va to'satdan unga va'dasini eslatdi; buning ustiga, agar u uni bajarmasa, bu dunyodagi eng sharmandali ish bo'lishini qo'shib qo'ydi. Uning bu kutilmagan hujumga javobi onasining qulog'iga juda yoqimli eshitildi:

paras.en: “I am perfectly ready, I assure you, to keep my engagement; and when your sister is recovered, you shall, if you please, name the very day of the ball. But you would not wish to be dancing when she is ill.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, va'damni bajarishga mutlaqo tayyorman; opangiz tuzalgach, xohlasangiz, balning aniq kunini o'zingiz belgilaysiz. Lekin u kasal paytda raqsga tushishni istamasangiz kerak».

paras.en: Lydia declared herself satisfied. “Oh! yes--it would be much better to wait till Jane was well, and by that time most likely Captain Carter would be at Meryton again. And when you have given your ball,” she added, “I shall insist on their giving one also. I shall tell Colonel Forster it will be quite a shame if he does not.”
paras.uz: Lidiya mamnunligini bildirdi. «Oh! Ha — Jeyn tuzalguncha kutish ancha yaxshi bo'lardi, o'shanda kapitan Karter ham, ehtimol, yana Meritonda bo'ladi. Siz balingizni bergach, — deb qo'shib qo'ydi u, — men ularning ham bal berishini talab qilaman. Polkovnik Forsterga aytamanki, agar bermasa, bu juda uyat bo'ladi».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet and her daughters then departed, and Elizabeth returned instantly to Jane, leaving her own and her relations' behaviour to the remarks of the two ladies and Mr. Darcy; the latter of whom, however, could not be prevailed on to join in their censure of her, in spite of all Miss Bingley's witticisms on fine eyes.
paras.uz: Shundan keyin missis Bennet qizlari bilan jo'nab ketdi, Elizabet esa darhol Jeynning oldiga qaytdi va o'zining hamda qarindoshlarining xulqini ikki xonim va janob Darsining muhokamasiga qoldirdi; biroq oxirgisini, miss Binglining chiroyli ko'zlar haqidagi barcha zehnli gaplariga qaramay, ularning uni tanqid qilishiga qo'shilishga ko'ndira olishmadi.

quiz.q: Why is Elizabeth embarrassed in this chapter?
o: Because of her mother's foolish behaviour
quiz.why_uz: Onasining gaplari Elizabetni uyaltiradi.

chapters.title: Letters and Music
chapters.recap_uz: Darsi singlisiga xat yozadi, Miss Bingli unga xushomad qiladi. Elizabet va Darsi bahslashadi. Darsi Elizabetning tabiiyligi va zukkoligiga tobora mahliyo bo'ladi.

paras.en: The day passed much as the day before had done. Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley had spent some hours of the morning with the invalid, who continued, though slowly, to mend; and in the evening Elizabeth joined their party in the drawing-room. The loo-table, however, did not appear. Mr. Darcy was writing, and Miss Bingley, seated near him, was watching the progress of his letter and repeatedly calling off his attention by messages to his sister. Mr. Hurst and Mr. Bingley were at piquet, and Mrs. Hurst was observing their game.
paras.uz: Kun xuddi oldingi kundek o'tdi. Missis Xerst va miss Bingli ertalab bir necha soatni sekin bo'lsa ham tuzalib borayotgan bemor bilan o'tkazishdi; kechqurun esa Elizabet mehmonxonada ularning davrasiga qo'shildi. Biroq lu stoli ko'rinmadi. Janob Darsi xat yozayotgan edi, uning yonida o'tirgan miss Bingli esa xatining qanday borayotganini kuzatar va singlisiga salomlar yo'llab, tinimsiz uning e'tiborini chalg'itardi. Janob Xerst bilan janob Bingli piket o'ynashardi, missis Xerst esa ularning o'yinini kuzatardi.

paras.en: Elizabeth took up some needlework, and was sufficiently amused in attending to what passed between Darcy and his companion. The perpetual commendations of the lady, either on his handwriting, or on the evenness of his lines, or on the length of his letter, with the perfect unconcern with which her praises were received, formed a curious dialogue, and was exactly in union with her opinion of each.
paras.uz: Elizabet kashta tikishga o'tirdi va Darsi bilan uning hamrohi o'rtasidagi gaplarni tinglab, yetarlicha ko'ngil ochdi. Xonimning uning yozuvi, yo satrlarining tekisligi, yo xatining uzunligi haqidagi tinimsiz maqtovlari va bu maqtovlarning mutlaq befarqlik bilan qabul qilinishi qiziq bir dialog hosil qilardi va Elizabetning har ikkisi haqidagi fikriga to'liq mos edi.

paras.en: “How delighted Miss Darcy will be to receive such a letter!”
paras.uz: «Miss Darsi bunday xat olganidan qanchalik xursand bo'ladi!»

paras.en: He made no answer.
paras.uz: U javob bermadi.

paras.en: “You write uncommonly fast.”
paras.uz: «Siz g'ayrioddiy tez yozasiz».

paras.en: “You are mistaken. I write rather slowly.”
paras.uz: «Adashyapsiz. Men ancha sekin yozaman».

paras.en: “How many letters you must have occasion to write in the course of a year! Letters of business, too! How odious I should think them!”
paras.uz: «Bir yil davomida qancha xat yozishingizga to'g'ri kelsa kerak! Ish xatlari ham! Ular menga qanchalik jirkanch tuyulgan bo'lardi!»

paras.en: “It is fortunate, then, that they fall to my lot instead of yours.”
paras.uz: «Unday bo'lsa, ular sizning emas, mening zimmamga tushgani yaxshi».

paras.en: “Pray tell your sister that I long to see her.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, singlingizga uni ko'rishni orziqib kutayotganimni ayting».

paras.en: “I have already told her so once, by your desire.”
paras.uz: «Sizning xohishingiz bilan buni unga bir marta aytib bo'ldim».

paras.en: “I am afraid you do not like your pen. Let me mend it for you. I mend pens remarkably well.”
paras.uz: «Qo'rqaman, qalamingiz sizga yoqmayapti. Ruxsat bering, uni tuzatib beray. Men qalamlarni juda yaxshi tuzataman».

paras.en: “Thank you--but I always mend my own.”
paras.uz: «Rahmat — lekin men doim o'z qalamimni o'zim tuzataman».

paras.en: “How can you contrive to write so even?”
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib bunchalik tekis yoza olasiz?»

paras.en: He was silent.
paras.uz: U jim qoldi.

paras.en: “Tell your sister I am delighted to hear of her improvement on the harp; and pray let her know that I am quite in raptures with her beautiful little design for a table, and I think it infinitely superior to Miss Grantley's.”
paras.uz: «Singlingizga ayting, uning arfada chalishi yaxshilanganini eshitib, juda xursand bo'ldim; iltimos, unga stol uchun chizgan kichkina chiroyli naqshidan butunlay zavqlanganimni ham ayting, menimcha, u miss Grantlinikidan cheksiz ustun».

paras.en: “Will you give me leave to defer your raptures till I write again? At present I have not room to do them justice.”
paras.uz: «Zavq-shavqingizni keyingi xatimgacha qoldirishga ruxsat berasizmi? Hozir ularni munosib ifodalashga joyim yo'q».

paras.en: “Oh! it is of no consequence. I shall see her in January. But do you always write such charming long letters to her, Mr. Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Bu muhim emas. Men uni yanvarda ko'raman. Lekin unga doim shunday maftunkor uzun xatlar yozasizmi, janob Darsi?»

paras.en: “They are generally long; but whether always charming it is not for me to determine.”
paras.uz: «Ular odatda uzun bo'ladi; lekin doim maftunkormi-yo'qmi, buni hal qilish menga tegishli emas».

paras.en: “It is a rule with me, that a person who can write a long letter with ease, cannot write ill.”
paras.uz: «Mening qoidam shunday: uzun xatni oson yoza oladigan odam yomon yoza olmaydi».

paras.en: “That will not do for a compliment to Darcy, Caroline,” cried her brother, “because he does not write with ease. He studies too much for words of four syllables. Do not you, Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Bu Darsiga maqtov bo'lmaydi, Karolayn, — deb xitob qildi akasi, — chunki u oson yozmaydi. U to'rt bo'g'inli so'zlar ustida haddan tashqari ko'p bosh qotiradi. Shunday emasmi, Darsi?»

paras.en: “My style of writing is very different from yours.”
paras.uz: «Mening yozish uslubim siznikidan juda farq qiladi».

paras.en: “Oh!” cried Miss Bingley, “Charles writes in the most careless way imaginable. He leaves out half his words, and blots the rest.”
paras.uz: «Oh! — deb qichqirdi miss Bingli. — Charlz tasavvur qilish mumkin bo'lgan eng beparvo tarzda yozadi. So'zlarining yarmini tushirib qoldiradi, qolganini esa siyoh bilan bulg'aydi».

paras.en: “My ideas flow so rapidly that I have not time to express them--by which means my letters sometimes convey no ideas at all to my correspondents.”
paras.uz: «Fikrlarim shunchalik tez oqadiki, ularni ifodalashga vaqtim yetmaydi — shu sababli xatlarim ba'zan yozishganlarimga umuman hech qanday fikr yetkazmaydi».

paras.en: “Your humility, Mr. Bingley,” said Elizabeth, “must disarm reproof.”
paras.uz: «Sizning kamtarligingiz, janob Bingli, — dedi Elizabet, — har qanday tanbehni qurolsizlantirsa kerak».

paras.en: “Nothing is more deceitful,” said Darcy, “than the appearance of humility. It is often only carelessness of opinion, and sometimes an indirect boast.”
paras.uz: «Hech narsa kamtarlik ko'rinishidan aldamchiroq emas, — dedi Darsi. — Bu ko'pincha shunchaki fikrga beparvolik, ba'zan esa bilvosita maqtanishdir».

paras.en: “And which of the two do you call my little recent piece of modesty?”
paras.uz: «Mening yaqindagi kichkina kamtarligimni ulardan qaysi biri deb ataysan?»

paras.en: “The indirect boast; for you are really proud of your defects in writing, because you consider them as proceeding from a rapidity of thought and carelessness of execution, which, if not estimable, you think at least highly interesting. The power of doing anything with quickness is always prized much by the possessor, and often without any attention to the imperfection of the performance. When you told Mrs. Bennet this morning that if you ever resolved upon quitting Netherfield you should be gone in five minutes, you meant it to be a sort of panegyric, of compliment to yourself--and yet what is there so very laudable in a precipitance which must leave very necessary business undone, and can be of no real advantage to yourself or anyone else?”
paras.uz: «Bilvosita maqtanish; chunki sen yozishdagi kamchiliklaring bilan aslida faxrlanasan, chunki ularni fikrning tezligi va bajarishdagi beparvolikdan kelib chiqqan deb hisoblaysan — bu, qadrli bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmasa juda qiziqarli deb o'ylaysan. Biror ishni tez qila olish qobiliyatini egasi doim juda qadrlaydi, ko'pincha bajarilishdagi nuqsonlarga e'tibor bermay. Bugun ertalab missis Bennetga Nezerfildni tark etishga qaror qilsang, besh daqiqada jo'nab ketishingni aytganingda, sen buni o'zingga qandaydir maqtov, olqish sifatida aytding — holbuki juda zarur ishlarni bajarilmay qoldiradigan va o'zingga ham, boshqa hech kimga ham haqiqiy foyda keltirmaydigan shoshqaloqlikda shunchalik maqtovga arziydigan nima bor?»

paras.en: “Nay,” cried Bingley, “this is too much, to remember at night all the foolish things that were said in the morning. And yet, upon my honour, I believe what I said of myself to be true, and I believe it at this moment. At least, therefore, I did not assume the character of needless precipitance merely to show off before the ladies.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — deb qichqirdi Bingli, — ertalab aytilgan barcha ahmoqona gaplarni kechqurun eslash — bu haddan tashqari. Shunga qaramay, or-nomusim haqqi, o'zim haqimda aytganlarim to'g'ri deb ishonaman va hozir ham ishonaman. Demak, hech bo'lmasa, men xonimlar oldida maqtanish uchun keraksiz shoshqaloqlik qiyofasini olmaganman».

paras.en: “I dare say you believed it; but I am by no means convinced that you would be gone with such celerity. Your conduct would be quite as dependent on chance as that of any man I know; and if, as you were mounting your horse, a friend were to say, 'Bingley, you had better stay till next week,' you would probably do it, you would probably not go--and at another word, might stay a month.”
paras.uz: «Ishonganingga shubham yo'q; lekin sening shunchalik tezlik bilan jo'nab ketishingga aslo ishonmayman. Sening xatti-harakating men bilgan har qanday odamnikidek tasodifga bog'liq bo'lardi; va agar otingga minayotganingda bir do'sting: „Bingli, yaxshisi kelasi haftagacha qol“, desa, ehtimol, qolarding, ehtimol, ketmasding — yana bir og'iz gap bilan esa bir oy qolib ketishing mumkin edi».

paras.en: “You have only proved by this,” cried Elizabeth, “that Mr. Bingley did not do justice to his own disposition. You have shown him off now much more than he did himself.”
paras.uz: «Siz bu bilan faqat janob Bingli o'z fe'liga adolat qilmaganini isbotladingiz, — deb xitob qildi Elizabet. — Endi siz uni o'zi ko'rsatganidan ancha yaxshiroq ko'rsatdingiz».

paras.en: “I am exceedingly gratified,” said Bingley, “by your converting what my friend says into a compliment on the sweetness of my temper. But I am afraid you are giving it a turn which that gentleman did by no means intend; for he would certainly think better of me, if under such a circumstance I were to give a flat denial, and ride off as fast as I could.”
paras.uz: «Do'stimning gapini fe'limning yumshoqligiga maqtovga aylantirganingizdan nihoyatda mamnunman, — dedi Bingli. — Lekin qo'rqamanki, siz unga bu janob aslo nazarda tutmagan ma'no beryapsiz; chunki bunday vaziyatda men qat'iy rad etib, iloji boricha tez otni haydab ketsam, u, albatta, men haqimda yaxshiroq fikrda bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Would Mr. Darcy then consider the rashness of your original intentions as atoned for by your obstinacy in adhering to it?”
paras.uz: «Unda janob Darsi dastlabki niyatingizning shoshqaloqligini unga o'jarlik bilan sodiq qolishingiz bilan yuvilgan deb hisoblarmidi?»

paras.en: “Upon my word, I cannot exactly explain the matter; Darcy must speak for himself.”
paras.uz: «Rostini aytsam, masalani aniq tushuntira olmayman; Darsi o'zi uchun o'zi gapirsin».

paras.en: “You expect me to account for opinions which you choose to call mine, but which I have never acknowledged. Allowing the case, however, to stand according to your representation, you must remember, Miss Bennet, that the friend who is supposed to desire his return to the house, and the delay of his plan, has merely desired it, asked it without offering one argument in favour of its propriety.”
paras.uz: «Siz mendan o'zingiz meniki deb atashni xohlagan, lekin men hech qachon tan olmagan fikrlar uchun javob berishimni kutyapsiz. Biroq vaziyat sizning tasviringizga ko'ra bo'lsa ham, esingizda bo'lsin, miss Bennet, uning uyga qaytishini va rejasining kechiktirilishini istaydi deb faraz qilingan do'st buni shunchaki istagan, uning to'g'riligi foydasiga birorta ham dalil keltirmasdan so'ragan, xolos».

paras.en: “To yield readily--easily--to the persuasion of a friend is no merit with you.”
paras.uz: «Do'stning ko'ndirishiga tezda — osonlikcha — bo'ysunish siz uchun fazilat emas».

paras.en: “To yield without conviction is no compliment to the understanding of either.”
paras.uz: «Ishonch hosil qilmasdan bo'ysunish ikkalasining ham aql-idrokiga hurmat emas».

paras.en: “You appear to me, Mr. Darcy, to allow nothing for the influence of friendship and affection. A regard for the requester would often make one readily yield to a request, without waiting for arguments to reason one into it. I am not particularly speaking of such a case as you have supposed about Mr. Bingley. We may as well wait, perhaps, till the circumstance occurs before we discuss the discretion of his behaviour thereupon. But in general and ordinary cases between friend and friend, where one of them is desired by the other to change a resolution of no very great moment, should you think ill of that person for complying with the desire, without waiting to be argued into it?”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, janob Darsi, siz do'stlik va mehrning ta'siriga hech qanday o'rin qoldirmaysiz. So'rovchiga bo'lgan hurmat ko'pincha odamni dalillar kutmasdan iltimosga tezda bo'ysunishga majbur qiladi. Men aynan siz janob Bingli haqida faraz qilgan holat haqida gapirmayapman. Balki, uning bu holatdagi xatti-harakatining oqilonaligini muhokama qilishdan oldin, o'sha holat yuz berishini kutganimiz ma'qul. Lekin do'st bilan do'st o'rtasidagi umumiy va odatiy holatlarda, biri ikkinchisidan unchalik muhim bo'lmagan qarorini o'zgartirishni so'raganda, o'sha odam dalil keltirilishini kutmasdan iltimosga rozi bo'lgani uchun u haqida yomon o'ylarmidingiz?»

paras.en: “Will it not be advisable, before we proceed on this subject, to arrange with rather more precision the degree of importance which is to appertain to this request, as well as the degree of intimacy subsisting between the parties?”
paras.uz: «Bu mavzuni davom ettirishdan oldin, bu iltimosga qanchalik ahamiyat berilishi va tomonlar o'rtasidagi yaqinlik darajasini biroz aniqroq belgilab olish maqsadga muvofiq emasmi?»

paras.en: “By all means,” cried Bingley; “let us hear all the particulars, not forgetting their comparative height and size; for that will have more weight in the argument, Miss Bennet, than you may be aware of. I assure you, that if Darcy were not such a great tall fellow, in comparison with myself, I should not pay him half so much deference. I declare I do not know a more awful object than Darcy, on particular occasions, and in particular places; at his own house especially, and of a Sunday evening, when he has nothing to do.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, — deb qichqirdi Bingli, — barcha tafsilotlarni eshitaylik, ularning nisbiy bo'yi va gavdasini ham unutmaylik; chunki bu bahsda, miss Bennet, siz o'ylaganingizdan ham kattaroq vazn qiladi. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, agar Darsi men bilan solishtirganda bunday katta, baland yigit bo'lmaganida, unga yarim darajada ham hurmat ko'rsatmagan bo'lardim. Ochig'ini aytaman, ma'lum vaziyatlarda va ma'lum joylarda — ayniqsa o'z uyida, yakshanba oqshomi, qiladigan ishi yo'q paytda — Darsidan dahshatliroq narsani bilmayman».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy smiled; but Elizabeth thought she could perceive that he was rather offended, and therefore checked her laugh. Miss Bingley warmly resented the indignity he had received, in an expostulation with her brother for talking such nonsense.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi jilmaydi; lekin Elizabet uning biroz ranjiganini sezganday bo'ldi va shuning uchun kulgisini tiydi. Miss Bingli uning ko'rgan haqoratidan qattiq ranjidi va akasini bunday bema'ni gaplar uchun koyidi.

paras.en: “I see your design, Bingley,” said his friend. “You dislike an argument, and want to silence this.”
paras.uz: «Niyatingni ko'ryapman, Bingli, — dedi do'sti. — Sen bahsni yoqtirmaysan va buni to'xtatmoqchisan».

paras.en: “Perhaps I do. Arguments are too much like disputes. If you and Miss Bennet will defer yours till I am out of the room, I shall be very thankful; and then you may say whatever you like of me.”
paras.uz: «Balki shundaydir. Bahslar janjalga juda o'xshaydi. Agar sen va miss Bennet o'zingiznikini men xonadan chiqqunimcha qoldirsangiz, juda minnatdor bo'laman; keyin men haqimda xohlaganingizni aytishingiz mumkin».

paras.en: “What you ask,” said Elizabeth, “is no sacrifice on my side; and Mr. Darcy had much better finish his letter.”
paras.uz: «Siz so'ragan narsa, — dedi Elizabet, — men tomondan hech qanday qurbonlik emas; janob Darsi esa xatini tugatgani ancha ma'qul».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy took her advice, and did finish his letter.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi uning maslahatiga amal qilib, xatini tugatdi.

paras.en: When that business was over, he applied to Miss Bingley and Elizabeth for an indulgence of some music. Miss Bingley moved with some alacrity to the pianoforte; and, after a polite request that Elizabeth would lead the way which the other as politely and more earnestly negatived, she seated herself.
paras.uz: Bu ish tugagach, u miss Bingli va Elizabetdan biroz musiqa ijro etishni iltimos qildi. Miss Bingli biroz shoshib fortepiano tomon yurdi va Elizabetdan birinchi bo'lib chalishni xushmuomalalik bilan so'ragach — u ham xuddi shunday xushmuomalalik bilan, lekin qat'iyroq rad etdi — o'zi o'tirdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Hurst sang with her sister, and while they were thus employed, Elizabeth could not help observing, as she turned over some music-books that lay on the instrument, how frequently Mr. Darcy's eyes were fixed on her. She hardly knew how to suppose that she could be an object of admiration to so great a man; and yet that he should look at her because he disliked her, was still more strange. She could only imagine, however, at last that she drew his notice because there was something more wrong and reprehensible, according to his ideas of right, than in any other person present. The supposition did not pain her. She liked him too little to care for his approbation.
paras.uz: Missis Xerst singlisi bilan birga kuyladi; ular shu bilan band bo'lganlarida, Elizabet cholg'u ustida yotgan nota daftarlarini varaqlab, janob Darsining ko'zlari unga qanchalik tez-tez tikilayotganini payqamay qololmadi. U shunday ulug' odamning hayrat obyekti bo'lishi mumkinligini qanday tasavvur qilishni bilmasdi; ammo uni yoqtirmagani uchun unga qarashi yanada g'alatiroq edi. Oxiri u faqat shunday tasavvur qila oldi: uning to'g'rilik haqidagi tushunchalariga ko'ra, unda bu yerdagi boshqa har qanday odamdagidan ko'ra ko'proq noto'g'ri va tanbehga loyiq narsa borligi uchun uning e'tiborini tortayotgan bo'lsa kerak. Bu taxmin uni og'ritmadi. U uni uning ma'qullashiga e'tibor beradigan darajada yoqtirmasdi.

paras.en: After playing some Italian songs, Miss Bingley varied the charm by a lively Scotch air; and soon afterwards Mr. Darcy, drawing near Elizabeth, said to her:
paras.uz: Bir nechta italyan qo'shiqlarini chalgach, miss Bingli sehrni jo'shqin shotland kuyi bilan o'zgartirdi; ko'p o'tmay janob Darsi Elizabetga yaqinlashib, unga dedi:

paras.en: “Do not you feel a great inclination, Miss Bennet, to seize such an opportunity of dancing a reel?”
paras.uz: «Shunday imkoniyatdan foydalanib, rill raqsiga tushishga katta xohishingiz yo'qmi, miss Bennet?»

paras.en: She smiled, but made no answer. He repeated the question, with some surprise at her silence.
paras.uz: U jilmaydi, lekin javob bermadi. U uning jimligidan biroz hayron bo'lib, savolni takrorladi.

paras.en: “Oh!” said she, “I heard you before, but I could not immediately determine what to say in reply. You wanted me, I know, to say 'Yes,' that you might have the pleasure of despising my taste; but I always delight in overthrowing those kind of schemes, and cheating a person of their premeditated contempt. I have, therefore, made up my mind to tell you, that I do not want to dance a reel at all--and now despise me if you dare.”
paras.uz: «Oh! — dedi u. — Sizni avval ham eshitdim, lekin nima deb javob berishni darhol hal qila olmadim. Bilaman, siz mening „Ha“ deyishimni xohladingiz, toki mening didimdan nafratlanish zavqiga ega bo'lishingiz uchun; lekin men doim bunday rejalarni barbod qilishdan va odamni oldindan tayyorlab qo'ygan nafratidan mahrum qilishdan zavqlanaman. Shuning uchun sizga umuman rill raqsiga tushishni istamasligimni aytishga qaror qildim — endi jur'atingiz yetsa, mendan nafratlaning».

paras.en: “Indeed I do not dare.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan, jur'atim yetmaydi».

paras.en: Elizabeth, having rather expected to affront him, was amazed at his gallantry; but there was a mixture of sweetness and archness in her manner which made it difficult for her to affront anybody; and Darcy had never been so bewitched by any woman as he was by her. He really believed, that were it not for the inferiority of her connections, he should be in some danger.
paras.uz: Uni ranjitishni kutgan Elizabet uning xushmuomalaligidan hayratda qoldi; lekin uning muomalasida shunday shirinlik va sho'xlik aralashmasi bor ediki, u hech kimni ranjitishi qiyin edi; Darsi esa hech qachon hech bir ayolga unga mahliyo bo'lganchalik mahliyo bo'lmagan edi. U chindan ham ishonardi: agar uning qarindoshlari past bo'lmaganida, u qandaydir xavf ostida bo'lardi.

paras.en: Miss Bingley saw, or suspected enough to be jealous; and her great anxiety for the recovery of her dear friend Jane received some assistance from her desire of getting rid of Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Miss Bingli rashk qilish uchun yetarlicha narsani ko'rdi yoki gumon qildi; uning aziz dugonasi Jeynning tuzalishiga bo'lgan katta tashvishiga Elizabetdan qutulish istagi ham biroz yordam berdi.

paras.en: She often tried to provoke Darcy into disliking her guest, by talking of their supposed marriage, and planning his happiness in such an alliance.
paras.uz: U tez-tez ularning go'yoki bo'ladigan nikohi haqida gapirib va bunday ittifoqda uning baxtini rejalashtirib, Darsini mehmonini yoqtirmaslikka undashga urinardi.

paras.en: “I hope,” said she, as they were walking together in the shrubbery the next day, “you will give your mother-in-law a few hints, when this desirable event takes place, as to the advantage of holding her tongue; and if you can compass it, do cure the younger girls of running after officers. And, if I may mention so delicate a subject, endeavour to check that little something, bordering on conceit and impertinence, which your lady possesses.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, — dedi u ertasi kuni ular butazorda birga sayr qilib yurganlarida, — bu orzu qilingan voqea sodir bo'lganda, qaynonangizga tilini tiyib yurishning foydasi haqida bir nechta ishora qilasiz; agar uddasidan chiqsangiz, kichik qizlarni ofitserlar ortidan yugurishdan davolang. Agar shunday nozik mavzuni tilga olishga ruxsat bo'lsa, xonimingizdagi manmanlik va surbetlikka yaqin o'sha kichkina narsani ham jilovlashga harakat qiling».

paras.en: “Have you anything else to propose for my domestic felicity?”
paras.uz: «Mening oilaviy baxtim uchun yana biror taklifingiz bormi?»

paras.en: “Oh! yes. Do let the portraits of your uncle and aunt Phillips be placed in the gallery at Pemberley. Put them next to your great-uncle the judge. They are in the same profession, you know, only in different lines. As for your Elizabeth's picture, you must not have it taken, for what painter could do justice to those beautiful eyes?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Ha. Albatta, Fillips xola va pochchangizning portretlarini Pemberlidagi galereyaga osib qo'ying. Ularni sudya bo'lgan katta tog'angiz yoniga qo'ying. Bilasiz, ular bir kasbda, faqat turli yo'nalishlarda. Elizabetingizning portretiga kelsak, uni chizdirmasligingiz kerak, chunki qaysi rassom o'sha go'zal ko'zlarga munosib adolat qila oladi?»

paras.en: “It would not be easy, indeed, to catch their expression, but their colour and shape, and the eyelashes, so remarkably fine, might be copied.”
paras.uz: «Ularning ifodasini ilg'ash, albatta, oson bo'lmasdi, lekin ranggi va shakli, shunday g'ayrioddiy chiroyli kipriklarini ko'chirish mumkin edi».

paras.en: At that moment they were met from another walk by Mrs. Hurst and Elizabeth herself.
paras.uz: Shu payt boshqa yo'lkadan missis Xerst va Elizabetning o'zi ularga duch kelishdi.

paras.en: “I did not know that you intended to walk,” said Miss Bingley, in some confusion, lest they had been overheard.
paras.uz: «Sayr qilmoqchi ekanligingizni bilmagan edim», — dedi miss Bingli, gaplarini eshitib qolishmadimikan, deb biroz sarosimaga tushib.

paras.en: “You used us abominably ill,” answered Mrs. Hurst, “running away without telling us that you were coming out.”
paras.uz: «Siz bizga juda yomon muomala qildingiz, — deb javob berdi missis Xerst, — tashqariga chiqayotganingizni aytmay qochib ketdingiz».

paras.en: Then taking the disengaged arm of Mr. Darcy, she left Elizabeth to walk by herself. The path just admitted three. Mr. Darcy felt their rudeness, and immediately said:
paras.uz: So'ng janob Darsining bo'sh qo'lidan ushlab, Elizabetni yolg'iz yurishga qoldirdi. Yo'lka faqat uch kishiga sig'ardi. Janob Darsi ularning qo'polligini his qildi va darhol dedi:

paras.en: “This walk is not wide enough for our party. We had better go into the avenue.”
paras.uz: «Bu yo'lka davramiz uchun yetarlicha keng emas. Yaxshisi xiyobonga o'taylik».

paras.en: But Elizabeth, who had not the least inclination to remain with them, laughingly answered:
paras.uz: Lekin ular bilan qolishga zarracha ham xohishi bo'lmagan Elizabet kulib javob berdi:

paras.en: “No, no; stay where you are. You are charmingly grouped, and appear to uncommon advantage. The picturesque would be spoilt by admitting a fourth. Good-bye.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, yo'q; joyingizda qoling. Siz maftunkor guruh bo'lib turibsiz va g'ayrioddiy yaxshi ko'rinyapsiz. To'rtinchisini qo'shsak, manzara buziladi. Xayr».

paras.en: She then ran gaily off, rejoicing as she rambled about, in the hope of being at home again in a day or two. Jane was already so much recovered as to intend leaving her room for a couple of hours that evening.
paras.uz: So'ng u quvnoq yugurib ketdi va sayr qilib yurarkan, bir-ikki kundan keyin yana uyda bo'lish umidi bilan sevindi. Jeyn allaqachon shunchalik tuzalgan ediki, o'sha oqshom bir-ikki soatga xonasidan chiqmoqchi edi.

quiz.q: How does Miss Bingley try to win Darcy?
quiz.why_uz: Uning xushomadi Darsiga yoqmaydi.

quiz.q: What does Darcy feel about Elizabeth here?
o: He has never been so bewitched by any woman
quiz.why_uz: U uning oilasi past darajada bo'lmaganida xavfli ekanini o'ylaydi.

chapters.title: Pride and Weakness
chapters.recap_uz: Jeyn tuzalib mehmonxonaga tushadi. Elizabet va Darsi xarakter haqida bahslashadi: Darsi uning kamchiligi — xafa qilinsa abadiy kechirmasligini tan oladi; Elizabet: «Sizning kamchiligingiz — hammani yomon ko'rish», deydi.

paras.en: When the ladies removed after dinner, Elizabeth ran up to her sister, and seeing her well guarded from cold, attended her into the drawing-room, where she was welcomed by her two friends with many professions of pleasure; and Elizabeth had never seen them so agreeable as they were during the hour which passed before the gentlemen appeared. Their powers of conversation were considerable. They could describe an entertainment with accuracy, relate an anecdote with humour, and laugh at their acquaintance with spirit.
paras.uz: Tushlikdan keyin xonimlar chiqib ketishganda, Elizabet opasining oldiga yugurib chiqdi va uni sovuqdan yaxshi o'ralganini ko'rib, mehmonxonaga kuzatib keldi; u yerda ikki dugonasi uni ko'p xursandchilik izhorlari bilan kutib olishdi; Elizabet ularni janoblar kelgunga qadar o'tgan bir soat davomidagidek yoqimli hech qachon ko'rmagan edi. Ularning suhbatlashish qobiliyati ancha katta edi. Ular ziyofatni aniq tasvirlab bera olardilar, latifani hazil bilan aytib berardilar va tanishlari ustidan zavq bilan kulardilar.

paras.en: But when the gentlemen entered, Jane was no longer the first object; Miss Bingley's eyes were instantly turned toward Darcy, and she had something to say to him before he had advanced many steps. He addressed himself to Miss Bennet, with a polite congratulation; Mr. Hurst also made her a slight bow, and said he was “very glad;” but diffuseness and warmth remained for Bingley's salutation. He was full of joy and attention. The first half-hour was spent in piling up the fire, lest she should suffer from the change of room; and she removed at his desire to the other side of the fireplace, that she might be further from the door. He then sat down by her, and talked scarcely to anyone else. Elizabeth, at work in the opposite corner, saw it all with great delight.
paras.uz: Lekin janoblar kirishi bilan Jeyn endi birinchi e'tibor markazi emasdi; miss Binglining ko'zlari darhol Darsiga qadaldi va u bir necha qadam tashlamasidanoq unga aytadigan gapi bor edi. U miss Bennetga xushmuomalalik bilan tabrik aytdi; janob Xerst ham unga yengil ta'zim qilib, «juda xursandman» dedi; lekin samimiylik va iliqlik Binglining salomiga qolgan edi. U quvonch va e'tiborga to'la edi. Birinchi yarim soat xona almashinuvidan zarar ko'rmasin deb o'choqqa o'tin qalash bilan o'tdi; uning iltimosi bilan Jeyn eshikdan uzoqroq bo'lishi uchun kaminning narigi tomoniga o'tdi. So'ng u uning yoniga o'tirdi va deyarli hech kim bilan gaplashmadi. Qarama-qarshi burchakda kashta tikayotgan Elizabet bularning hammasini katta zavq bilan kuzatdi.

paras.en: When tea was over, Mr. Hurst reminded his sister-in-law of the card-table--but in vain. She had obtained private intelligence that Mr. Darcy did not wish for cards; and Mr. Hurst soon found even his open petition rejected. She assured him that no one intended to play, and the silence of the whole party on the subject seemed to justify her. Mr. Hurst had therefore nothing to do, but to stretch himself on one of the sofas and go to sleep. Darcy took up a book; Miss Bingley did the same; and Mrs. Hurst, principally occupied in playing with her bracelets and rings, joined now and then in her brother's conversation with Miss Bennet.
paras.uz: Choy tugagach, janob Xerst qaynsingilisiga karta stolini eslatdi — lekin befoyda. U janob Darsi karta o'ynashni istamasligini maxfiy ravishda bilib olgan edi; tez orada janob Xerst hatto ochiq iltimosi ham rad etilganini ko'rdi. U hech kim o'ynash niyatida emasligini aytdi va butun davraning bu masaladagi jimligi uni oqlayotganday edi. Shunday qilib, janob Xerstga divanlardan biriga cho'zilib uxlashdan boshqa ish qolmadi. Darsi kitob oldi; miss Bingli ham shunday qildi; asosan bilaguzuklari va uzuklari bilan o'ynash bilan band bo'lgan missis Xerst vaqti-vaqti bilan akasining miss Bennet bilan suhbatiga qo'shilib turdi.

paras.en: Miss Bingley's attention was quite as much engaged in watching Mr. Darcy's progress through his book, as in reading her own; and she was perpetually either making some inquiry, or looking at his page. She could not win him, however, to any conversation; he merely answered her question, and read on. At length, quite exhausted by the attempt to be amused with her own book, which she had only chosen because it was the second volume of his, she gave a great yawn and said, “How pleasant it is to spend an evening in this way! I declare after all there is no enjoyment like reading! How much sooner one tires of anything than of a book! When I have a house of my own, I shall be miserable if I have not an excellent library.”
paras.uz: Miss Binglining e'tibori o'z kitobini o'qishdan ko'ra janob Darsining kitobida qanchalik ilgarilaganini kuzatishga ko'proq qaratilgan edi; u tinimsiz yo biror narsa so'rar, yo uning sahifasiga qarardi. Biroq u uni biror suhbatga torta olmadi; u faqat savoliga javob berib, o'qishda davom etardi. Nihoyat, faqat uning kitobining ikkinchi jildi bo'lgani uchun tanlagan o'z kitobi bilan ko'ngil ochishga urinishdan butunlay holdan toyib, u katta esnadi va dedi: «Oqshomni shu tarzda o'tkazish qanday yoqimli! Ochig'ini aytaman, oxir-oqibat o'qishga teng keladigan zavq yo'q! Odam har qanday narsadan kitobdan ko'ra ancha tez charchaydi! O'z uyim bo'lganda, ajoyib kutubxonam bo'lmasa, baxtsiz bo'laman».

paras.en: No one made any reply. She then yawned again, threw aside her book, and cast her eyes round the room in quest for some amusement; when hearing her brother mentioning a ball to Miss Bennet, she turned suddenly towards him and said:
paras.uz: Hech kim javob bermadi. Shunda u yana esnadi, kitobini chetga uloqtirdi va biror ermak izlab xona bo'ylab ko'z yugurtirdi; akasining miss Bennetga bal haqida gapirayotganini eshitib, birdan unga o'girildi va dedi:

paras.en: “By the bye, Charles, are you really serious in meditating a dance at Netherfield? I would advise you, before you determine on it, to consult the wishes of the present party; I am much mistaken if there are not some among us to whom a ball would be rather a punishment than a pleasure.”
paras.uz: «Aytgancha, Charlz, Nezerfildda raqs kechasi o'tkazishni rostdan ham jiddiy o'ylayapsanmi? Qaror qilishdan oldin hozirgi davradagilarning xohishini so'rashingni maslahat bergan bo'lardim; agar oramizda bal zavqdan ko'ra jazo bo'ladigan ba'zilar bo'lmasa, qattiq adashgan bo'laman».

paras.en: “If you mean Darcy,” cried her brother, “he may go to bed, if he chooses, before it begins--but as for the ball, it is quite a settled thing; and as soon as Nicholls has made white soup enough, I shall send round my cards.”
paras.uz: «Agar Darsini nazarda tutsang, — deb xitob qildi akasi, — xohlasa, bal boshlanmasdan oldin uxlashga yotishi mumkin — balga kelsak, bu butunlay hal bo'lgan ish; Nikolls yetarlicha oq sho'rva tayyorlagach, taklifnomalarimni tarqataman».

paras.en: “I should like balls infinitely better,” she replied, “if they were carried on in a different manner; but there is something insufferably tedious in the usual process of such a meeting. It would surely be much more rational if conversation instead of dancing were made the order of the day.”
paras.uz: «Agar ballar boshqacha tarzda o'tkazilganida, — dedi u, — ularni cheksiz ko'proq yoqtirgan bo'lardim; lekin bunday yig'inlarning odatiy tartibida chidab bo'lmas zerikarli narsa bor. Agar kun tartibiga raqs o'rniga suhbat qo'yilganida, albatta, ancha oqilonaroq bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Much more rational, my dear Caroline, I dare say, but it would not be near so much like a ball.”
paras.uz: «Ancha oqilonaroq, aziz Karolayn, shubham yo'q, lekin bu balga unchalik o'xshamasdi».

paras.en: Miss Bingley made no answer, and soon afterwards she got up and walked about the room. Her figure was elegant, and she walked well; but Darcy, at whom it was all aimed, was still inflexibly studious. In the desperation of her feelings, she resolved on one effort more, and, turning to Elizabeth, said:
paras.uz: Miss Bingli javob bermadi va ko'p o'tmay o'rnidan turib, xona bo'ylab yura boshladi. Uning qomati nafis edi va u chiroyli yurardi; lekin bularning hammasi qaratilgan Darsi hamon qat'iyat bilan mutolaaga berilgan edi. Tuyg'ularining umidsizligida u yana bir urinishga qaror qildi va Elizabetga o'girilib dedi:

paras.en: “Miss Eliza Bennet, let me persuade you to follow my example, and take a turn about the room. I assure you it is very refreshing after sitting so long in one attitude.”
paras.uz: «Miss Eliza Bennet, ruxsat bering, sizni mening o'rnagimga ergashib, xona bo'ylab bir aylanishga ko'ndiray. Sizni ishontiraman, bir holatda uzoq o'tirgandan keyin bu juda tetiklashtiradi».

paras.en: Elizabeth was surprised, but agreed to it immediately. Miss Bingley succeeded no less in the real object of her civility; Mr. Darcy looked up. He was as much awake to the novelty of attention in that quarter as Elizabeth herself could be, and unconsciously closed his book. He was directly invited to join their party, but he declined it, observing that he could imagine but two motives for their choosing to walk up and down the room together, with either of which motives his joining them would interfere. “What could he mean? She was dying to know what could be his meaning?”--and asked Elizabeth whether she could at all understand him?
paras.uz: Elizabet hayron bo'ldi, lekin darhol rozi bo'ldi. Miss Bingli o'z xushmuomalaligining haqiqiy maqsadiga ham kam muvaffaq bo'lmadi: janob Darsi boshini ko'tardi. U o'sha tomondan ko'rsatilgan bu yangi e'tiborni Elizabetning o'zi qanchalik sezgan bo'lsa, shunchalik sezdi va beixtiyor kitobini yopdi. Uni darhol ularga qo'shilishga taklif qilishdi, lekin u rad etdi va ularning xona bo'ylab birga yurishni tanlashiga faqat ikki sabab bo'lishi mumkinligini tasavvur qila olishini, ulardan har biriga uning qo'shilishi xalaqit berishini aytdi. «U nima demoqchi? U uning nima demoqchi ekanini bilishga o'layotgan edi!» — va u Elizabetdan uni umuman tushuna oladimi, deb so'radi.

paras.en: “Not at all,” was her answer; “but depend upon it, he means to be severe on us, and our surest way of disappointing him will be to ask nothing about it.”
paras.uz: «Aslo, — deb javob berdi u, — lekin ishonavering, u bizni qattiq tanqid qilmoqchi va uning hafsalasini pir qilishning eng ishonchli yo'li bu haqda hech narsa so'ramaslik bo'ladi».

paras.en: Miss Bingley, however, was incapable of disappointing Mr. Darcy in anything, and persevered therefore in requiring an explanation of his two motives.
paras.uz: Biroq miss Bingli janob Darsining hafsalasini biror narsada pir qilishga qodir emasdi va shuning uchun uning ikki sababini tushuntirishni talab qilishda davom etdi.

paras.en: “I have not the smallest objection to explaining them,” said he, as soon as she allowed him to speak. “You either choose this method of passing the evening because you are in each other's confidence, and have secret affairs to discuss, or because you are conscious that your figures appear to the greatest advantage in walking; if the first, I would be completely in your way, and if the second, I can admire you much better as I sit by the fire.”
paras.uz: «Ularni tushuntirishga zarracha qarshiligim yo'q, — dedi u, u gapirishga ruxsat berishi bilanoq. — Siz oqshomni shu tarzda o'tkazishni yo bir-biringizga sirdosh bo'lib, muhokama qiladigan maxfiy ishlaringiz bo'lgani uchun tanlaysiz, yo yurganda qomatingiz eng yaxshi ko'rinishini bilganingiz uchun; agar birinchisi bo'lsa, men sizga butunlay xalaqit bergan bo'lardim, agar ikkinchisi bo'lsa, kamin yonida o'tirib sizga ancha yaxshiroq mahliyo bo'la olaman».

paras.en: “Oh! shocking!” cried Miss Bingley. “I never heard anything so abominable. How shall we punish him for such a speech?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Dahshat! — deb qichqirdi miss Bingli. — Hech qachon bunchalik jirkanch gap eshitmaganman. Bunday gap uchun uni qanday jazolaymiz?»

paras.en: “Nothing so easy, if you have but the inclination,” said Elizabeth. “We can all plague and punish one another. Tease him--laugh at him. Intimate as you are, you must know how it is to be done.”
paras.uz: «Xohishingiz bo'lsa, bundan oson narsa yo'q, — dedi Elizabet. — Hammamiz bir-birimizni qiynab, jazolay olamiz. Uni masxara qiling — ustidan kuling. Shunchalik yaqin bo'lganingizdan keyin, buni qanday qilishni bilishingiz kerak».

paras.en: “But upon my honour, I do not. I do assure you that my intimacy has not yet taught me that. Tease calmness of manner and presence of mind! No, no; I feel he may defy us there. And as to laughter, we will not expose ourselves, if you please, by attempting to laugh without a subject. Mr. Darcy may hug himself.”
paras.uz: «Lekin or-nomusim haqqi, bilmayman. Sizni ishontiraman, yaqinligim hali buni menga o'rgatmagan. Vazmin muomala va hozirjavoblikni masxara qilish! Yo'q, yo'q; his qilyapmanki, bu borada u bizga bas keladi. Kulgiga kelsak, xohlasangiz, sababsiz kulishga urinib o'zimizni sharmanda qilmaymiz. Janob Darsi o'zidan mamnun bo'lishi mumkin».

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy is not to be laughed at!” cried Elizabeth. “That is an uncommon advantage, and uncommon I hope it will continue, for it would be a great loss to me to have many such acquaintances. I dearly love a laugh.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi ustidan kulib bo'lmas ekan! — deb xitob qildi Elizabet. — Bu g'ayrioddiy afzallik, umid qilamanki, g'ayrioddiyligicha qoladi, chunki bunday tanishlarim ko'p bo'lsa, men uchun katta yo'qotish bo'lardi. Men kulishni juda yaxshi ko'raman».

paras.en: “Miss Bingley,” said he, “has given me more credit than can be. The wisest and the best of men--nay, the wisest and best of their actions--may be rendered ridiculous by a person whose first object in life is a joke.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bingli, — dedi u, — menga loyiq bo'lganimdan ko'proq baho berdi. Eng dono va eng yaxshi odamlarni — yo'q, ularning eng dono va eng yaxshi ishlarini ham — hayotidagi birinchi maqsadi hazil bo'lgan odam kulgili qilib ko'rsatishi mumkin».

paras.en: “Certainly,” replied Elizabeth--“there are such people, but I hope I am not one of them. I hope I never ridicule what is wise and good. Follies and nonsense, whims and inconsistencies, do divert me, I own, and I laugh at them whenever I can. But these, I suppose, are precisely what you are without.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, — dedi Elizabet, — bunday odamlar bor, lekin umid qilamanki, men ulardan emasman. Umid qilamanki, men hech qachon dono va yaxshi narsani masxara qilmayman. Ahmoqlik va bema'nilik, injiqlik va nomuvofiqliklar meni chindan ham ovutadi, tan olaman, va imkon bo'lganda ularning ustidan kulaman. Lekin menimcha, aynan bular sizda yo'q».

paras.en: “Perhaps that is not possible for anyone. But it has been the study of my life to avoid those weaknesses which often expose a strong understanding to ridicule.”
paras.uz: «Balki bu hech kimga mumkin emasdir. Lekin kuchli aqlni ko'pincha masxaraga qo'yadigan zaifliklardan qochish butun umrim davomida o'rganib kelgan ishim bo'ldi».

paras.en: “Such as vanity and pride.”
paras.uz: «Masalan, manmanlik va g'urur».

paras.en: “Yes, vanity is a weakness indeed. But pride--where there is a real superiority of mind, pride will be always under good regulation.”
paras.uz: «Ha, manmanlik chindan ham zaiflik. Lekin g'urur — aqlning haqiqiy ustunligi bor joyda g'urur doim yaxshi nazorat ostida bo'ladi».

paras.en: Elizabeth turned away to hide a smile.
paras.uz: Elizabet tabassumini yashirish uchun yuzini burdi.

paras.en: “Your examination of Mr. Darcy is over, I presume,” said Miss Bingley; “and pray what is the result?”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsini tekshirishingiz tugadi shekilli, — dedi miss Bingli, — ayting-chi, natija qanday?»

paras.en: “I am perfectly convinced by it that Mr. Darcy has no defect. He owns it himself without disguise.”
paras.uz: «Men janob Darsida hech qanday nuqson yo'qligiga to'liq ishonch hosil qildim. U buni o'zi yashirmasdan tan oladi».

paras.en: “No,” said Darcy, “I have made no such pretension. I have faults enough, but they are not, I hope, of understanding. My temper I dare not vouch for. It is, I believe, too little yielding--certainly too little for the convenience of the world. I cannot forget the follies and vices of others so soon as I ought, nor their offenses against myself. My feelings are not puffed about with every attempt to move them. My temper would perhaps be called resentful. My good opinion once lost, is lost forever.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — dedi Darsi, — men bunday da'vo qilmadim. Kamchiliklarim yetarli, lekin, umid qilamanki, ular aql-idrokka tegishli emas. Fe'lim uchun kafolat bera olmayman. Menimcha, u juda kam yon beradi — albatta, dunyoning qulayligi uchun juda kam. Men boshqalarning ahmoqliklari va illatlarini, shuningdek, ularning menga qilgan haqoratlarini kerakli darajada tez unuta olmayman. Tuyg'ularim ularni qo'zg'atishga bo'lgan har bir urinishdan qo'zg'alib ketmaydi. Fe'limni, ehtimol, kek saqlovchi deyishar. Bir marta yo'qotilgan yaxshi fikrim abadiy yo'qoladi».

paras.en: “That is a failing indeed!” cried Elizabeth. “Implacable resentment is a shade in a character. But you have chosen your fault well. I really cannot laugh at it. You are safe from me.”
paras.uz: «Bu chindan ham kamchilik! — deb xitob qildi Elizabet. — Murosasiz kek — xarakterdagi soya. Lekin siz kamchiligingizni yaxshi tanlagansiz. Rostdan ham uning ustidan kula olmayman. Mendan xavfsizsiz».

paras.en: “There is, I believe, in every disposition a tendency to some particular evil--a natural defect, which not even the best education can overcome.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, har bir tabiatda qandaydir muayyan yomonlikka moyillik — hatto eng yaxshi tarbiya ham yenga olmaydigan tabiiy nuqson bor».

paras.en: “And your defect is to hate everybody.”
paras.uz: «Sizning nuqsoningiz esa — hammani yomon ko'rish».

paras.en: “And yours,” he replied with a smile, “is willfully to misunderstand them.”
paras.uz: «Sizniki esa, — dedi u jilmayib, — ularni ataylab noto'g'ri tushunish».

paras.en: “Do let us have a little music,” cried Miss Bingley, tired of a conversation in which she had no share. “Louisa, you will not mind my waking Mr. Hurst?”
paras.uz: «Keling, biroz musiqa tinglaylik, — deb qichqirdi o'zi qatnashmagan suhbatdan zerikkan miss Bingli. — Luiza, janob Xerstni uyg'otsam, qarshi emasmisan?»

paras.en: Her sister had not the smallest objection, and the pianoforte was opened; and Darcy, after a few moments' recollection, was not sorry for it. He began to feel the danger of paying Elizabeth too much attention.
paras.uz: Singlisining zarracha ham qarshiligi yo'q edi, fortepiano ochildi; Darsi esa bir necha lahza o'ylab, bundan afsuslanmadi. U Elizabetga haddan tashqari ko'p e'tibor berish xavfini his qila boshlagan edi.

gloss.ex: My temper would perhaps be called resentful.
Darcy has no defect.
At length, quite exhausted by the attempt to be amused with her own book, which she had only chosen because it was the second volume of his, she gave a…
The wisest and the best of men--nay, the wisest and best of their actions--may be rendered ridiculous by a person whose first object in life is a joke.”
But it has been the study of my life to avoid those weaknesses which often expose a strong understanding to ridicule.”
They could describe an entertainment with accuracy, relate an anecdote with humour, and laugh at their acquaintance with spirit.
When the ladies removed after dinner, Elizabeth ran up to her sister, and seeing her well guarded from cold, attended her into the drawing-room, where she was welcomed by her…

quiz.why_uz: Bu xususiyat keyinroq Uikhem bilan bog'liq voqeada muhim bo'ladi.

chapters.title: Leaving Netherfield
chapters.recap_uz: Opa-singillar uyga qaytadi. Darsi Elizabetga haddan ortiq qiziqib qolganini sezib, undan uzoqlashishga harakat qiladi.

paras.en: In consequence of an agreement between the sisters, Elizabeth wrote the next morning to their mother, to beg that the carriage might be sent for them in the course of the day. But Mrs. Bennet, who had calculated on her daughters remaining at Netherfield till the following Tuesday, which would exactly finish Jane's week, could not bring herself to receive them with pleasure before. Her answer, therefore, was not propitious, at least not to Elizabeth's wishes, for she was impatient to get home. Mrs. Bennet sent them word that they could not possibly have the carriage before Tuesday; and in her postscript it was added, that if Mr. Bingley and his sister pressed them to stay longer, she could spare them very well. Against staying longer, however, Elizabeth was positively resolved--nor did she much expect it would be asked; and fearful, on the contrary, as being considered as intruding themselves needlessly long, she urged Jane to borrow Mr. Bingley's carriage immediately, and at length it was settled that their original design of leaving Netherfield that morning should be mentioned, and the request made.
paras.uz: Opa-singil o'rtasidagi kelishuvga ko'ra, Elizabet ertasi kuni ertalab onasiga xat yozib, kun davomida ular uchun arava yuborishni iltimos qildi. Lekin qizlari Nezerfildda keyingi seshanbagacha — Jeynning bir haftasi aynan tugaydigan kungacha qolishini hisoblab qo'ygan missis Bennet ularni bundan oldin xursandchilik bilan kutib olishga o'zini majbur qila olmadi. Shuning uchun uning javobi — hech bo'lmasa uyga qaytishga oshiqayotgan Elizabetning istaklariga — qulay bo'lmadi. Missis Bennet ularga seshanbadan oldin aravani olishning iloji yo'qligini aytib yubordi; xatining oxiridagi qo'shimchada esa, agar janob Bingli va uning singlisi ularni uzoqroq qolishga qistasa, u ularsiz bemalol tura olishini qo'shgan edi. Biroq Elizabet uzoqroq qolishga qat'iyan qarshi edi — buni so'rashlarini ham unchalik kutmasdi; aksincha, keraksiz uzoq vaqt o'zlarini tiqishtirib turishgan deb hisoblanishdan qo'rqib, Jeynni darhol janob Binglining aravasini so'rashga undadi va oxiri ularning o'sha kuni ertalab Nezerfildni tark etish haqidagi dastlabki niyatini aytib, iltimos qilishga kelishildi.

paras.en: The communication excited many professions of concern; and enough was said of wishing them to stay at least till the following day to work on Jane; and till the morrow their going was deferred. Miss Bingley was then sorry that she had proposed the delay, for her jealousy and dislike of one sister much exceeded her affection for the other.
paras.uz: Bu xabar ko'p xavotir izhorlariga sabab bo'ldi; ularning hech bo'lmasa ertasi kungacha qolishini istash haqida Jeynga ta'sir qiladigan darajada yetarli gaplar aytildi; ketish ertangi kunga qoldirildi. Shunda miss Bingli kechiktirishni taklif qilganidan afsuslandi, chunki uning bir opa-singilga bo'lgan rashki va yoqtirmasligi ikkinchisiga bo'lgan mehridan ancha ortiq edi.

paras.en: The master of the house heard with real sorrow that they were to go so soon, and repeatedly tried to persuade Miss Bennet that it would not be safe for her--that she was not enough recovered; but Jane was firm where she felt herself to be right.
paras.uz: Uy egasi ular shunchalik tez ketishlarini chin dildan qayg'u bilan eshitdi va miss Bennetni bu uning uchun xavfsiz emasligiga — u hali yetarlicha tuzalmaganiga qayta-qayta ishontirishga urindi; lekin Jeyn o'zini haq deb his qilgan joyda qat'iy edi.

paras.en: To Mr. Darcy it was welcome intelligence--Elizabeth had been at Netherfield long enough. She attracted him more than he liked--and Miss Bingley was uncivil to her, and more teasing than usual to himself. He wisely resolved to be particularly careful that no sign of admiration should now escape him, nothing that could elevate her with the hope of influencing his felicity; sensible that if such an idea had been suggested, his behaviour during the last day must have material weight in confirming or crushing it. Steady to his purpose, he scarcely spoke ten words to her through the whole of Saturday, and though they were at one time left by themselves for half-an-hour, he adhered most conscientiously to his book, and would not even look at her.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi uchun bu yoqimli xabar edi — Elizabet Nezerfildda yetarlicha uzoq qoldi. U uni o'zi istaganidan ko'proq o'ziga tortardi — miss Bingli esa unga qo'pollik qilar va Darsining o'zini odatdagidan ko'proq jig'iga tegardi. U endi undan hech qanday mahliyolik belgisi chiqib ketmasligiga, uni o'zining baxtiga ta'sir qilish umidi bilan ko'taradigan hech narsa bo'lmasligiga alohida ehtiyot bo'lishga oqilona qaror qildi; agar bunday fikr paydo bo'lgan bo'lsa, oxirgi kundagi xatti-harakati uni tasdiqlash yoki yo'q qilishda katta ahamiyatga ega bo'lishini anglardi. O'z maqsadiga sodiq qolib, u butun shanba kuni unga o'nta so'z ham arang aytdi; bir vaqt ular yarim soat yolg'iz qolishganda ham, u juda vijdonan kitobiga yopishib oldi va unga qaramadi ham.

paras.en: On Sunday, after morning service, the separation, so agreeable to almost all, took place. Miss Bingley's civility to Elizabeth increased at last very rapidly, as well as her affection for Jane; and when they parted, after assuring the latter of the pleasure it would always give her to see her either at Longbourn or Netherfield, and embracing her most tenderly, she even shook hands with the former. Elizabeth took leave of the whole party in the liveliest of spirits.
paras.uz: Yakshanba kuni ertalabki ibodatdan keyin deyarli hamma uchun yoqimli bo'lgan ajralish sodir bo'ldi. Oxiri miss Binglining Elizabetga xushmuomalaligi, Jeynga bo'lgan mehri kabi, juda tez ortdi; xayrlashayotganda u Jeynni Longbornda ham, Nezerfildda ham ko'rish unga doim zavq bag'ishlashiga ishontirib, uni juda mehr bilan quchoqlagach, hatto Elizabetning qo'lini ham siqdi. Elizabet butun davra bilan eng quvnoq kayfiyatda xayrlashdi.

paras.en: They were not welcomed home very cordially by their mother. Mrs. Bennet wondered at their coming, and thought them very wrong to give so much trouble, and was sure Jane would have caught cold again. But their father, though very laconic in his expressions of pleasure, was really glad to see them; he had felt their importance in the family circle. The evening conversation, when they were all assembled, had lost much of its animation, and almost all its sense by the absence of Jane and Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Uyda onasi ularni unchalik samimiy kutib olmadi. Missis Bennet ularning kelganidan hayron bo'ldi, shuncha tashvish tug'dirganlari uchun ularni juda noto'g'ri ish qilgan deb hisobladi va Jeyn yana shamollab qolgan bo'lishiga ishonchi komil edi. Lekin otalari, xursandchiligini juda qisqa ifoda etsa ham, ularni ko'rganidan chindan ham xursand edi; u oila davrasida ularning ahamiyatini his qilgan edi. Hammasi yig'ilgandagi kechki suhbat Jeyn va Elizabet yo'qligida jonliligining ko'p qismini va deyarli butun ma'nosini yo'qotgan edi.

paras.en: They found Mary, as usual, deep in the study of thorough-bass and human nature; and had some extracts to admire, and some new observations of threadbare morality to listen to. Catherine and Lydia had information for them of a different sort. Much had been done and much had been said in the regiment since the preceding Wednesday; several of the officers had dined lately with their uncle, a private had been flogged, and it had actually been hinted that Colonel Forster was going to be married.
paras.uz: Ular Merini odatdagidek bas-generalni va inson tabiatini o'rganishga sho'ng'igan holda topishdi; hayratlanish uchun bir nechta ko'chirmalar va tinglash uchun eskirib ketgan axloq haqida bir nechta yangi mulohazalar tayyor edi. Ketrin va Lidiyada ular uchun boshqa turdagi xabarlar bor edi. O'tgan chorshanbadan beri polkda ko'p narsa qilingan va ko'p gap bo'lgan edi; bir nechta ofitser yaqinda amakilarinikida tushlik qilgan, bir oddiy askar qamchilangan va hatto polkovnik Forster uylanmoqchi ekani haqida shama qilingan edi.
