chapters.title: Mr. Collins's Letter
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Bennet kelayotgan mehmon — mulk merosxo'ri, ruhoniy janob Kollinz haqida xabar beradi. Kollinzning xati dabdabali va kulgili; u o'z homiysi ledi Ketrin de Burni maqtaydi.

paras.en: “I hope, my dear,” said Mr. Bennet to his wife, as they were at breakfast the next morning, “that you have ordered a good dinner to-day, because I have reason to expect an addition to our family party.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, azizim, — dedi janob Bennet ertasi kuni ertalab nonushta paytida xotiniga, — bugun yaxshi tushlik buyurgansiz, chunki oilaviy davramizga yana bir kishi qo'shilishini kutishga asosim bor».

paras.en: “Who do you mean, my dear? I know of nobody that is coming, I am sure, unless Charlotte Lucas should happen to call in--and I hope my dinners are good enough for her. I do not believe she often sees such at home.”
paras.uz: «Kimni aytyapsiz, azizim? Kelayotgan hech kimni bilmayman, ishonchim komil, faqat Sharlotta Lukas kirib qolmasa — umid qilamanki, mening tushliklarim uning uchun yetarlicha yaxshi. Uyda bunaqasini tez-tez ko'radi deb o'ylamayman».

paras.en: “The person of whom I speak is a gentleman, and a stranger.”
paras.uz: «Men gapirayotgan odam — janob va notanish».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet's eyes sparkled. “A gentleman and a stranger! It is Mr. Bingley, I am sure! Well, I am sure I shall be extremely glad to see Mr. Bingley. But--good Lord! how unlucky! There is not a bit of fish to be got to-day. Lydia, my love, ring the bell--I must speak to Hill this moment.”
paras.uz: Missis Bennetning ko'zlari chaqnadi. «Janob va notanish! Bu janob Bingli, ishonchim komil! Xo'sh, janob Binglini ko'rganimdan nihoyatda xursand bo'laman. Lekin — yo Xudo! Qanday omadsizlik! Bugun bir parcha ham baliq topib bo'lmaydi. Lidiya, jonim, qo'ng'iroqni chal — Xill bilan hozir gaplashishim kerak».

paras.en: “It is not Mr. Bingley,” said her husband; “it is a person whom I never saw in the whole course of my life.”
paras.uz: «Bu janob Bingli emas, — dedi eri, — bu umrim bo'yi hech qachon ko'rmagan odam».

paras.en: This roused a general astonishment; and he had the pleasure of being eagerly questioned by his wife and his five daughters at once.
paras.uz: Bu umumiy hayrat uyg'otdi va u xotini va besh qizi tomonidan bir vaqtda ishtiyoq bilan so'roqqa tutilish zavqiga muyassar bo'ldi.

paras.en: After amusing himself some time with their curiosity, he thus explained:
paras.uz: Ularning qiziqishi bilan bir muddat ermak qilgach, u shunday tushuntirdi:

paras.en: “About a month ago I received this letter; and about a fortnight ago I answered it, for I thought it a case of some delicacy, and requiring early attention. It is from my cousin, Mr. Collins, who, when I am dead, may turn you all out of this house as soon as he pleases.”
paras.uz: «Taxminan bir oy oldin men mana bu xatni oldim, ikki haftacha oldin esa unga javob berdim, chunki bu ancha nozik va tezroq e'tibor talab qiladigan ish deb o'yladim. Xat amakivachcham janob Kollinzdan; men o'lgach, u xohlagan paytida hammangizni bu uydan haydab chiqarishi mumkin».

paras.en: “Oh! my dear,” cried his wife, “I cannot bear to hear that mentioned. Pray do not talk of that odious man. I do think it is the hardest thing in the world, that your estate should be entailed away from your own children; and I am sure, if I had been you, I should have tried long ago to do something or other about it.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Azizim, — deb qichqirdi xotini, — bu haqda eshitishga chiday olmayman. Iltimos, o'sha jirkanch odam haqida gapirmang. Menimcha, mulkingiz o'z farzandlaringizdan tortib olinib, boshqaga o'tishi dunyodagi eng og'ir narsa; ishonchim komilki, men sizning o'rningizda bo'lganimda, bu haqda allaqachon biror chora ko'rishga urinardim».

paras.en: Jane and Elizabeth tried to explain to her the nature of an entail. They had often attempted to do it before, but it was a subject on which Mrs. Bennet was beyond the reach of reason, and she continued to rail bitterly against the cruelty of settling an estate away from a family of five daughters, in favour of a man whom nobody cared anything about.
paras.uz: Jeyn va Elizabet unga meros cheklovining mohiyatini tushuntirishga urinishdi. Ular buni avval ham ko'p marta qilishga uringan edilar, lekin bu missis Bennetga aql bilan yetib bo'lmaydigan mavzu edi va u besh qizli oiladan mulkni tortib olib, hech kim e'tibor bermaydigan odamga berishning shafqatsizligi haqida achchiq-achchiq gapirishda davom etdi.

paras.en: “It certainly is a most iniquitous affair,” said Mr. Bennet, “and nothing can clear Mr. Collins from the guilt of inheriting Longbourn. But if you will listen to his letter, you may perhaps be a little softened by his manner of expressing himself.”
paras.uz: «Bu, albatta, o'ta nohaq ish, — dedi janob Bennet, — va hech narsa janob Kollinzni Longbornni meros qilib olish aybidan oqlay olmaydi. Lekin agar uning xatini tinglasangiz, uning o'zini ifoda etish tarzi sizni biroz yumshatishi mumkin».

paras.en: “No, that I am sure I shall not; and I think it is very impertinent of him to write to you at all, and very hypocritical. I hate such false friends. Why could he not keep on quarreling with you, as his father did before him?”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, buni aniq bilaman, yumshatmaydi; menimcha, u sizga umuman xat yozgani juda surbetlik va juda ikkiyuzlamachilik. Men bunday soxta do'stlarni yomon ko'raman. Nega u otasi singari siz bilan janjallashishda davom eta olmadi?»

paras.en: “Why, indeed; he does seem to have had some filial scruples on that head, as you will hear.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan ham, nega; eshitasiz, u bu masalada farzandlik vijdoni bilan ikkilanganga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Hunsford, near Westerham, Kent, 15th October.
paras.uz: «Xansford, Uesterem yaqinida, Kent, 15-oktabr.

paras.en: “Dear Sir,--
paras.uz: Hurmatli ser,

paras.en: “The disagreement subsisting between yourself and my late honoured father always gave me much uneasiness, and since I have had the misfortune to lose him, I have frequently wished to heal the breach; but for some time I was kept back by my own doubts, fearing lest it might seem disrespectful to his memory for me to be on good terms with anyone with whom it had always pleased him to be at variance.--'There, Mrs. Bennet.'--My mind, however, is now made up on the subject, for having received ordination at Easter, I have been so fortunate as to be distinguished by the patronage of the Right Honourable Lady Catherine de Bourgh, widow of Sir Lewis de Bourgh, whose bounty and beneficence has preferred me to the valuable rectory of this parish, where it shall be my earnest endeavour to demean myself with grateful respect towards her ladyship, and be ever ready to perform those rites and ceremonies which are instituted by the Church of England.
paras.uz: Siz bilan marhum muhtaram otam o'rtasidagi kelishmovchilik doim meni ancha bezovta qilgan; uni yo'qotish baxtsizligiga uchraganimdan beri, ko'pincha bu yoriqni bitkazishni istadim; lekin bir muddat o'z shubhalarim meni to'xtatib turdi: u doim kelishmay yurishni ma'qul ko'rgan biror kishi bilan yaxshi munosabatda bo'lishim uning xotirasiga hurmatsizlik bo'lib tuyulishidan qo'rqdim. — „Mana, missis Bennet“. — Biroq endi bu masalada qarorim qat'iy, chunki Pasxada ruhoniylikka tayinlanib, marhum ser Lyuis de Burgning bevasi, oliy martabali ledi Ketrin de Burgning homiyligiga sazovor bo'lish baxtiga muyassar bo'ldim; uning saxovati va olijanobligi meni shu cherkov qavmining qimmatli ruhoniylik lavozimiga tayinladi; u yerda janoblariga nisbatan minnatdor hurmat bilan o'zimni tutishga va Angliya cherkovi tomonidan belgilangan marosim va udumlarni bajarishga doim tayyor bo'lishga astoydil intilaman.

paras.en: As a clergyman, moreover, I feel it my duty to promote and establish the blessing of peace in all families within the reach of my influence; and on these grounds I flatter myself that my present overtures are highly commendable, and that the circumstance of my being next in the entail of Longbourn estate will be kindly overlooked on your side, and not lead you to reject the offered olive-branch. I cannot be otherwise than concerned at being the means of injuring your amiable daughters, and beg leave to apologise for it, as well as to assure you of my readiness to make them every possible amends--but of this hereafter.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, ruhoniy sifatida, ta'sirim yetadigan barcha oilalarda tinchlik ne'matini qaror toptirish va mustahkamlashni o'z burchim deb bilaman; shu asosda hozirgi takliflarimni juda maqtovga loyiq deb hisoblayman va Longborn mulkining navbatdagi merosxo'ri ekanligim sizning tomoningizdan mehribonlik bilan e'tiborsiz qoldiriladi va taklif qilingan zaytun novdasini rad etishingizga sabab bo'lmaydi deb umid qilaman. Sizning yoqimli qizlaringizga zarar yetkazishga vosita bo'layotganimdan tashvishlanmay ilojim yo'q va buning uchun uzr so'rashga, shuningdek, ularga har qanday mumkin bo'lgan tovonni berishga tayyorligimni bildirishga ruxsat so'rayman — lekin bu haqda keyinroq.

paras.en: If you should have no objection to receive me into your house, I propose myself the satisfaction of waiting on you and your family, Monday, November 18th, by four o'clock, and shall probably trespass on your hospitality till the Saturday se'ennight following, which I can do without any inconvenience, as Lady Catherine is far from objecting to my occasional absence on a Sunday, provided that some other clergyman is engaged to do the duty of the day.--I remain, dear sir, with respectful compliments to your lady and daughters, your well-wisher and friend,
paras.uz: Agar meni uyingizda qabul qilishga e'tirozingiz bo'lmasa, 18-noyabr dushanba kuni soat to'rtgacha sizga va oilangizga tashrif buyurish mamnuniyatini o'zimga ravo ko'raman va, ehtimol, keyingi haftaning shanbasigacha mehmondo'stligingizni suiiste'mol qilaman; buni hech qanday noqulayliksiz qila olaman, chunki ledi Ketrin, kun xizmatini boshqa ruhoniy bajarishi sharti bilan, yakshanba kunlari vaqti-vaqti bilan yo'q bo'lishimga aslo qarshi emas. Xonimingiz va qizlaringizga hurmatli salomlar bilan, sizga xayrixoh va do'stingiz bo'lib qolaman,

paras.en: “WILLIAM COLLINS”
paras.uz: UILYAM KOLLINZ»

paras.en: “At four o'clock, therefore, we may expect this peace-making gentleman,” said Mr. Bennet, as he folded up the letter. “He seems to be a most conscientious and polite young man, upon my word, and I doubt not will prove a valuable acquaintance, especially if Lady Catherine should be so indulgent as to let him come to us again.”
paras.uz: «Demak, bu tinchlik o'rnatuvchi janobni soat to'rtda kutishimiz mumkin, — dedi janob Bennet xatni buklab. — Or-nomusim haqqi, u juda vijdonli va xushmuomala yosh yigitga o'xshaydi va, shubham yo'q, qimmatli tanish bo'lib chiqadi, ayniqsa agar ledi Ketrin uni yana bizning oldimizga kelishiga ruxsat beradigan darajada iltifotli bo'lsa».

paras.en: “There is some sense in what he says about the girls, however, and if he is disposed to make them any amends, I shall not be the person to discourage him.”
paras.uz: «Biroq uning qizlar haqida aytganlarida qandaydir ma'no bor; agar u ularga biror tovon berishga moyil bo'lsa, men uni bundan qaytaradigan odam bo'lmayman».

paras.en: “Though it is difficult,” said Jane, “to guess in what way he can mean to make us the atonement he thinks our due, the wish is certainly to his credit.”
paras.uz: «Garchi u bizga munosib deb bilgan tovonni qanday yo'l bilan bermoqchi ekanini taxmin qilish qiyin bo'lsa ham, — dedi Jeyn, — bu istak, albatta, unga sharaf keltiradi».

paras.en: Elizabeth was chiefly struck by his extraordinary deference for Lady Catherine, and his kind intention of christening, marrying, and burying his parishioners whenever it were required.
paras.uz: Elizabetni asosan uning ledi Ketringa bo'lgan g'ayrioddiy hurmati va kerak bo'lganda qavmini cho'qintirish, nikohlash va dafn qilish haqidagi mehribon niyati hayratga soldi.

paras.en: “He must be an oddity, I think,” said she. “I cannot make him out.--There is something very pompous in his style.--And what can he mean by apologising for being next in the entail?--We cannot suppose he would help it if he could.--Could he be a sensible man, sir?”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, u g'alati odam bo'lsa kerak, — dedi u. — Uni tushuna olmayapman. Uslubida juda dabdabali nimadir bor. Navbatdagi merosxo'r bo'lgani uchun uzr so'rashi bilan nima demoqchi? Iloji bo'lsa, buni o'zgartirardi deb o'ylay olmaymiz-ku. U aqlli odam bo'lishi mumkinmi, ser?»

paras.en: “No, my dear, I think not. I have great hopes of finding him quite the reverse. There is a mixture of servility and self-importance in his letter, which promises well. I am impatient to see him.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, azizim, menimcha, yo'q. Uni butunlay buning aksi deb topishga katta umidim bor. Xatida yaltoqlik va o'zini muhim sanash aralashmasi bor — bu yaxshi va'da beradi. Uni ko'rishga sabrsizlik bilan intiqman».

paras.en: “In point of composition,” said Mary, “the letter does not seem defective. The idea of the olive-branch perhaps is not wholly new, yet I think it is well expressed.”
paras.uz: «Yozilish jihatidan, — dedi Meri, — xat nuqsonli ko'rinmaydi. Zaytun novdasi haqidagi fikr, balki, butunlay yangi emasdir, lekin menimcha, yaxshi ifodalangan».

paras.en: To Catherine and Lydia, neither the letter nor its writer were in any degree interesting. It was next to impossible that their cousin should come in a scarlet coat, and it was now some weeks since they had received pleasure from the society of a man in any other colour. As for their mother, Mr. Collins's letter had done away much of her ill-will, and she was preparing to see him with a degree of composure which astonished her husband and daughters.
paras.uz: Ketrin va Lidiya uchun na xat, na uning muallifi zarracha ham qiziq emasdi. Amakivachchalarining qizil kamzulda kelishi deyarli mumkin emasdi, ular esa boshqa rangdagi kiyimdagi erkakning davrasidan zavq olmaganlariga bir necha hafta bo'lgan edi. Onalariga kelsak, janob Kollinzning xati uning g'azabining ko'p qismini yo'qotgan edi va u erini va qizlarini hayratga soladigan darajada xotirjamlik bilan uni ko'rishga tayyorlanardi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins was punctual to his time, and was received with great politeness by the whole family. Mr. Bennet indeed said little; but the ladies were ready enough to talk, and Mr. Collins seemed neither in need of encouragement, nor inclined to be silent himself. He was a tall, heavy-looking young man of five-and-twenty. His air was grave and stately, and his manners were very formal. He had not been long seated before he complimented Mrs. Bennet on having so fine a family of daughters; said he had heard much of their beauty, but that in this instance fame had fallen short of the truth; and added, that he did not doubt her seeing them all in due time disposed of in marriage. This gallantry was not much to the taste of some of his hearers; but Mrs. Bennet, who quarreled with no compliments, answered most readily.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz aytilgan vaqtda keldi va butun oila tomonidan katta xushmuomalalik bilan kutib olindi. Janob Bennet, to'g'ri, kam gapirdi; lekin xonimlar gapirishga yetarlicha tayyor edilar, janob Kollinz esa na dalda talab qilardi, na o'zi jim turishga moyil edi. U yigirma besh yoshli, baland bo'yli, og'ir-vazmin ko'rinishli yigit edi. Qiyofasi jiddiy va salobatli, muomalasi juda rasmiy edi. O'tirganidan ko'p o'tmay u missis Bennetni shunday ajoyib qizlari borligi bilan maqtadi; ularning go'zalligi haqida ko'p eshitganini, lekin bu holatda shon-shuhrat haqiqatdan orqada qolganini aytdi va vaqti kelib ularning hammasini erga berganini ko'rishiga shubha qilmasligini qo'shib qo'ydi. Bu iltifot ba'zi tinglovchilarning didiga unchalik to'g'ri kelmadi; lekin hech qanday maqtov bilan janjallashmaydigan missis Bennet darhol javob berdi.

paras.en: “You are very kind, I am sure; and I wish with all my heart it may prove so, for else they will be destitute enough. Things are settled so oddly.”
paras.uz: «Siz juda mehribonsiz, ishonchim komil; chin dildan shunday bo'lishini istayman, aks holda ular ancha qashshoq qoladi. Ishlar juda g'alati tartibga solingan».

paras.en: “You allude, perhaps, to the entail of this estate.”
paras.uz: «Siz, ehtimol, bu mulkning meros cheklovini nazarda tutyapsiz».

paras.en: “Ah! sir, I do indeed. It is a grievous affair to my poor girls, you must confess. Not that I mean to find fault with you, for such things I know are all chance in this world. There is no knowing how estates will go when once they come to be entailed.”
paras.uz: «Ah! Ser, xuddi shuni. Tan olishingiz kerak, bu mening bechora qizlarim uchun og'ir ish. Sizni ayblamoqchi emasman, chunki bilamanki, bu dunyoda bunday narsalar tasodif. Mulklar bir marta cheklovga tushgach, qanday ketishini bilib bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: “I am very sensible, madam, of the hardship to my fair cousins, and could say much on the subject, but that I am cautious of appearing forward and precipitate. But I can assure the young ladies that I come prepared to admire them. At present I will not say more; but, perhaps, when we are better acquainted--”
paras.uz: «Xonim, men go'zal amakivachchalarimning qiyinchiligini juda yaxshi tushunaman va bu mavzuda ko'p gapirishim mumkin edi, lekin dadil va shoshqaloq ko'rinishdan ehtiyot bo'laman. Biroq yosh xonimlarni ishontirib aytamanki, men ularga mahliyo bo'lishga tayyor holda keldim. Hozircha boshqa gap aytmayman; lekin, balki, yaqinroq tanishganimizdan keyin...»

paras.en: He was interrupted by a summons to dinner; and the girls smiled on each other. They were not the only objects of Mr. Collins's admiration. The hall, the dining-room, and all its furniture, were examined and praised; and his commendation of everything would have touched Mrs. Bennet's heart, but for the mortifying supposition of his viewing it all as his own future property. The dinner too in its turn was highly admired; and he begged to know to which of his fair cousins the excellency of its cooking was owing. But he was set right there by Mrs. Bennet, who assured him with some asperity that they were very well able to keep a good cook, and that her daughters had nothing to do in the kitchen. He begged pardon for having displeased her. In a softened tone she declared herself not at all offended; but he continued to apologise for about a quarter of an hour.
paras.uz: Uning gapini tushlikka chaqiriq bo'ldi; qizlar bir-biriga jilmayib qo'yishdi. Ular janob Kollinzning hayratidagi yagona obyekt emasdi. Dahliz, ovqat xonasi va uning barcha mebellari ko'zdan kechirilib, maqtaldi; uning hamma narsani maqtashi missis Bennetning yuragiga ta'sir qilgan bo'lardi, agar u bularning hammasiga o'zining kelajakdagi mulki sifatida qarayapti degan izza qiluvchi taxmin bo'lmaganida. O'z navbatida tushlik ham juda maqtaldi; u taomning a'lo darajada pishirilganini go'zal amakivachchalaridan qaysi biriga qarzdor ekanini bilishni so'radi. Lekin missis Bennet bu borada uni tuzatdi va biroz keskinlik bilan ular yaxshi oshpaz saqlashga bemalol qodir ekanliklarini va qizlarining oshxonada hech qanday ishi yo'qligini ta'kidladi. U uning ko'nglini og'ritgani uchun kechirim so'radi. U yumshoqroq ohangda umuman ranjimaganini aytdi; lekin u chorak soatcha uzr so'rashda davom etdi.

quiz.q: Who is Mr. Collins?
o: The clergyman who will inherit Longbourn
quiz.why_uz: Mulk qonun bo'yicha Bennetlardan keyin unga o'tadi.

quiz.q: What is special about his letter?
o: It is pompous and full of self-importance
quiz.why_uz: Janob Bennet uni o'qib, zavqlanadi — uning ahmoqligidan kuladi.

chapters.title: Mr. Collins Reads
chapters.recap_uz: Kollinz ledi Ketrinni cheksiz maqtaydi. Kechqurun u qizlarga diniy kitob o'qib beradi, Lidiya esa uni bo'lib yuboradi.

paras.en: During dinner, Mr. Bennet scarcely spoke at all; but when the servants were withdrawn, he thought it time to have some conversation with his guest, and therefore started a subject in which he expected him to shine, by observing that he seemed very fortunate in his patroness. Lady Catherine de Bourgh's attention to his wishes, and consideration for his comfort, appeared very remarkable. Mr. Bennet could not have chosen better. Mr. Collins was eloquent in her praise. The subject elevated him to more than usual solemnity of manner, and with a most important aspect he protested that “he had never in his life witnessed such behaviour in a person of rank--such affability and condescension, as he had himself experienced from Lady Catherine. She had been graciously pleased to approve of both of the discourses which he had already had the honour of preaching before her.
paras.uz: Tushlik paytida janob Bennet deyarli umuman gapirmadi; lekin xizmatkorlar chiqib ketgach, mehmoni bilan biroz suhbatlashish vaqti keldi deb o'yladi va shuning uchun uning porlashini kutgan mavzuni boshladi: uning homiysi bilan juda omadi kelganga o'xshashini aytdi. Ledi Ketrin de Burgning uning istaklariga e'tibori va qulayligi haqida g'amxo'rligi juda diqqatga sazovor ko'rinardi. Janob Bennet bundan yaxshiroq mavzuni tanlay olmasdi. Janob Kollinz uni maqtashda notiqlik qildi. Mavzu uni odatdagidan ham salobatliroq qildi va eng muhim qiyofada u «umrida hech qachon yuqori martabali odamda bunday xulqni — ledi Ketrindan o'zi ko'rgandek xushmuomalalik va yuqoridan mehribonlikni ko'rmaganini» ta'kidladi. «U oldida va'z o'qish sharafiga muyassar bo'lgan ikkala va'zini ham marhamat bilan ma'qullagan edi.

paras.en: She had also asked him twice to dine at Rosings, and had sent for him only the Saturday before, to make up her pool of quadrille in the evening. Lady Catherine was reckoned proud by many people he knew, but he had never seen anything but affability in her. She had always spoken to him as she would to any other gentleman; she made not the smallest objection to his joining in the society of the neighbourhood nor to his leaving the parish occasionally for a week or two, to visit his relations. She had even condescended to advise him to marry as soon as he could, provided he chose with discretion; and had once paid him a visit in his humble parsonage, where she had perfectly approved all the alterations he had been making, and had even vouchsafed to suggest some herself--some shelves in the closet up stairs.”
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, u uni ikki marta Rozingsga tushlikka taklif qilgan va o'tgan shanbagina kechqurun kadril o'yinida sheriklarini to'ldirish uchun uni chaqirtirgan edi. U bilgan ko'p odamlar ledi Ketrinni mag'rur deb hisoblardi, lekin u undan xushmuomalalikdan boshqa narsa ko'rmagan edi. U u bilan doim boshqa har qanday janob bilan gaplashgandek gaplashgan; uning mahalla davrasiga qo'shilishiga ham, qarindoshlarini ko'rish uchun vaqti-vaqti bilan bir-ikki haftaga cherkov qavmini tark etishiga ham zarracha e'tiroz bildirmagan. U hatto unga iloji boricha tezroq uylanishni maslahat berishga ham iltifot ko'rsatgan, faqat aql bilan tanlash sharti bilan; bir marta esa uning kamtarona ruhoniy uyiga tashrif buyurib, u qilgan barcha o'zgarishlarni to'liq ma'qullagan va hatto o'zi ham ba'zilarini taklif qilish iltifotini ko'rsatgan — yuqori qavatdagi shkafga bir nechta tokcha».

paras.en: “That is all very proper and civil, I am sure,” said Mrs. Bennet, “and I dare say she is a very agreeable woman. It is a pity that great ladies in general are not more like her. Does she live near you, sir?”
paras.uz: «Bularning hammasi juda o'rinli va xushmuomala, ishonaman, — dedi missis Bennet, — u juda yoqimli ayol bo'lsa kerak. Afsuski, umuman olganda katta xonimlar unga ko'proq o'xshamaydi. U sizga yaqin yashaydimi, ser?»

paras.en: “The garden in which stands my humble abode is separated only by a lane from Rosings Park, her ladyship's residence.”
paras.uz: «Mening kamtarona maskanim turgan bog' janoblarining qarorgohi Rozings Parkdan faqat bir tor ko'cha bilan ajratilgan».

paras.en: “I think you said she was a widow, sir? Has she any family?”
paras.uz: «U beva dedingiz shekilli, ser? Oilasi bormi?»

paras.en: “She has only one daughter, the heiress of Rosings, and of very extensive property.”
paras.uz: «Uning faqat bitta qizi bor — Rozingsning va juda katta mulkning merosxo'ri».

paras.en: “Ah!” said Mrs. Bennet, shaking her head, “then she is better off than many girls. And what sort of young lady is she? Is she handsome?”
paras.uz: «Ah! — dedi missis Bennet boshini chayqab. — Unda u ko'p qizlardan ahvoli yaxshiroq. U qanday yosh xonim? Chiroylimi?»

paras.en: “She is a most charming young lady indeed. Lady Catherine herself says that, in point of true beauty, Miss de Bourgh is far superior to the handsomest of her sex, because there is that in her features which marks the young lady of distinguished birth. She is unfortunately of a sickly constitution, which has prevented her from making that progress in many accomplishments which she could not have otherwise failed of, as I am informed by the lady who superintended her education, and who still resides with them. But she is perfectly amiable, and often condescends to drive by my humble abode in her little phaeton and ponies.”
paras.uz: «U haqiqatan ham juda maftunkor yosh xonim. Ledi Ketrinning o'zi aytadiki, haqiqiy go'zallik jihatidan miss de Burg o'z jinsining eng chiroylilaridan ham ancha ustun, chunki uning chehrasida mumtoz nasldan bo'lgan yosh xonimni ko'rsatib turadigan narsa bor. Afsuski, uning sog'lig'i nozik, bu esa uni ko'plab hunarlarda, aks holda albatta erishadigan muvaffaqiyatlarga erishishdan to'sib qo'ygan — buni menga uning tarbiyasi bilan shug'ullangan va hali ham ular bilan yashayotgan xonim aytdi. Lekin u mutlaqo yoqimli va ko'pincha ponilar qo'shilgan kichkina faetonida mening kamtarona maskanim yonidan o'tish iltifotini ko'rsatadi».

paras.en: “Has she been presented? I do not remember her name among the ladies at court.”
paras.uz: «U saroyda tanishtirilganmi? Saroydagi xonimlar orasida uning ismini eslay olmayman».

paras.en: “Her indifferent state of health unhappily prevents her being in town; and by that means, as I told Lady Catherine one day, has deprived the British court of its brightest ornament. Her ladyship seemed pleased with the idea; and you may imagine that I am happy on every occasion to offer those little delicate compliments which are always acceptable to ladies. I have more than once observed to Lady Catherine, that her charming daughter seemed born to be a duchess, and that the most elevated rank, instead of giving her consequence, would be adorned by her. These are the kind of little things which please her ladyship, and it is a sort of attention which I conceive myself peculiarly bound to pay.”
paras.uz: «Uning sog'lig'i yaxshi emasligi afsuski uni Londonda bo'lishdan to'sadi; shu bilan, bir kuni ledi Ketringa aytganimdek, Britaniya saroyini eng yorqin bezagidan mahrum qilgan. Janoblari bu fikrdan mamnun bo'lganday ko'rindi; tasavvur qilishingiz mumkinki, men har qanday imkoniyatda xonimlarga doim yoqadigan o'sha kichkina nozik iltifotlarni aytishdan xursandman. Ledi Ketringa bir necha marta uning maftunkor qizi gertsoginya bo'lish uchun tug'ilganga o'xshashini va eng yuksak martaba unga obro' bag'ishlash o'rniga, aksincha, uning o'zi bilan bezanishini aytganman. Janoblariga mana shunday kichik narsalar yoqadi va bu men o'zimni alohida burchli deb biladigan e'tibor turi».

paras.en: “You judge very properly,” said Mr. Bennet, “and it is happy for you that you possess the talent of flattering with delicacy. May I ask whether these pleasing attentions proceed from the impulse of the moment, or are the result of previous study?”
paras.uz: «Juda to'g'ri hukm qilyapsiz, — dedi janob Bennet, — xushomadni nozik qila olish iste'dodiga ega ekaningiz siz uchun baxt. So'rasam bo'ladimi, bu yoqimli e'tiborlar lahzaning turtkisi bilan paydo bo'ladimi yoki oldindan o'rganishning natijasimi?»

paras.en: “They arise chiefly from what is passing at the time, and though I sometimes amuse myself with suggesting and arranging such little elegant compliments as may be adapted to ordinary occasions, I always wish to give them as unstudied an air as possible.”
paras.uz: «Ular asosan o'sha paytda bo'layotgan narsadan kelib chiqadi; garchi ba'zan oddiy vaziyatlarga mos keladigan bunday kichik nafis iltifotlarni o'ylab topish va tartibga solish bilan ko'ngil ochsam ham, doim ularga iloji boricha o'rganilmagan tus berishni istayman».

paras.en: Mr. Bennet's expectations were fully answered. His cousin was as absurd as he had hoped, and he listened to him with the keenest enjoyment, maintaining at the same time the most resolute composure of countenance, and, except in an occasional glance at Elizabeth, requiring no partner in his pleasure.
paras.uz: Janob Bennetning kutganlari to'liq oqlandi. Amakivachchasi u umid qilganidek bema'ni edi va u uni eng o'tkir zavq bilan tingladi, shu bilan birga yuzida eng qat'iy xotirjamlikni saqlab, vaqti-vaqti bilan Elizabetga bir qarab qo'yishdan tashqari, zavqiga hech qanday sherik talab qilmadi.

paras.en: By tea-time, however, the dose had been enough, and Mr. Bennet was glad to take his guest into the drawing-room again, and, when tea was over, glad to invite him to read aloud to the ladies. Mr. Collins readily assented, and a book was produced; but, on beholding it (for everything announced it to be from a circulating library), he started back, and begging pardon, protested that he never read novels. Kitty stared at him, and Lydia exclaimed. Other books were produced, and after some deliberation he chose Fordyce's Sermons. Lydia gaped as he opened the volume, and before he had, with very monotonous solemnity, read three pages, she interrupted him with:
paras.uz: Biroq choy vaqtiga kelib, doza yetarli bo'ldi va janob Bennet mehmonini yana mehmonxonaga olib borishdan, choy tugagach esa uni xonimlarga ovoz chiqarib kitob o'qib berishga taklif qilishdan xursand bo'ldi. Janob Kollinz darhol rozi bo'ldi va kitob olib kelindi; lekin uni ko'rib (chunki hamma narsa uning pullik kutubxonadan ekanini ko'rsatib turardi), u orqaga tisarildi va kechirim so'rab, hech qachon roman o'qimasligini ta'kidladi. Ketti unga tikilib qoldi, Lidiya esa xitob qildi. Boshqa kitoblar olib kelindi va biroz o'ylagach, u Fordaysning «Va'zlar»ini tanladi. U jildni ochganda Lidiya esnadi va u juda bir xil salobat bilan uch sahifani o'qib bo'lmasidan, uning gapini bo'ldi:

paras.en: “Do you know, mamma, that my uncle Phillips talks of turning away Richard; and if he does, Colonel Forster will hire him. My aunt told me so herself on Saturday. I shall walk to Meryton to-morrow to hear more about it, and to ask when Mr. Denny comes back from town.”
paras.uz: «Bilasizmi, oyijon, Fillips amakim Richardni ishdan bo'shatish haqida gapiryapti; agar bo'shatsa, polkovnik Forster uni yollaydi. Xolam buni shanba kuni menga o'zi aytdi. Ertaga bu haqda ko'proq bilish va janob Denni Londondan qachon qaytishini so'rash uchun Meritonga piyoda boraman».

paras.en: Lydia was bid by her two eldest sisters to hold her tongue; but Mr. Collins, much offended, laid aside his book, and said:
paras.uz: Ikki katta opasi Lidiyaga tilini tiyishni buyurishdi; lekin qattiq ranjigan janob Kollinz kitobini chetga qo'ydi va dedi:

paras.en: “I have often observed how little young ladies are interested by books of a serious stamp, though written solely for their benefit. It amazes me, I confess; for, certainly, there can be nothing so advantageous to them as instruction. But I will no longer importune my young cousin.”
paras.uz: «Men ko'pincha yosh xonimlar faqat o'z foydasi uchun yozilgan jiddiy kitoblarga qanchalik kam qiziqishini kuzatganman. Tan olaman, bu meni hayratga soladi; chunki, albatta, ular uchun ta'limdan foydaliroq narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas. Lekin yosh amakivachchamni boshqa bezovta qilmayman».

paras.en: Then turning to Mr. Bennet, he offered himself as his antagonist at backgammon. Mr. Bennet accepted the challenge, observing that he acted very wisely in leaving the girls to their own trifling amusements. Mrs. Bennet and her daughters apologised most civilly for Lydia's interruption, and promised that it should not occur again, if he would resume his book; but Mr. Collins, after assuring them that he bore his young cousin no ill-will, and should never resent her behaviour as any affront, seated himself at another table with Mr. Bennet, and prepared for backgammon.
paras.uz: So'ng janob Bennetga o'girilib, unga nard o'yinida raqib bo'lishni taklif qildi. Janob Bennet qizlarni o'zlarining arzimas ermaklariga qoldirib, juda oqilona ish qilayotganini aytib, chaqiriqni qabul qildi. Missis Bennet va qizlari Lidiyaning gapni bo'lgani uchun juda xushmuomalalik bilan uzr so'rashdi va agar u kitobini davom ettirsa, bu boshqa takrorlanmasligiga va'da berishdi; lekin janob Kollinz yosh amakivachchasiga hech qanday g'arazi yo'qligini va uning xatti-harakatini hech qachon haqorat deb qabul qilmasligini aytib, janob Bennet bilan boshqa stolga o'tirdi va nard o'ynashga tayyorlandi.

gloss.ex: The subject elevated him to more than usual solemnity of manner, and with a most important aspect he protested that “he had never in his life witnessed such behaviour in…

Other books were produced, and after some deliberation he chose Fordyce's Sermons.
His cousin was as absurd as he had hoped, and he listened to him with the keenest enjoyment, maintaining at the same time the most resolute composure of countenance, and,…
Her ladyship seemed pleased with the idea; and you may imagine that I am happy on every occasion to offer those little delicate compliments which are always acceptable to ladies.
She had always spoken to him as she would to any other gentleman; she made not the smallest objection to his joining in the society of the neighbourhood nor to…
Bennet was glad to take his guest into the drawing-room again, and, when tea was over, glad to invite him to read aloud to the ladies.

quiz.q: How does Mr. Collins describe Lady Catherine?
quiz.why_uz: Uning maqtovlari Kollinzning yaltoqligini ko'rsatadi.

quiz.q: Who interrupts his reading?
quiz.why_uz: Lidiyaning beparvoligi bu yerda ham ko'rinadi.

chapters.title: Meeting Mr. Wickham
chapters.recap_uz: Kollinz Bennet qizlaridan biriga uylanmoqchi. Meritonda qizlar kelishgan ofitser janob Uikhem bilan tanishadi. Darsi va Uikhem uchrashib qolishadi: biri oqarib, biri qizarib ketadi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins was not a sensible man, and the deficiency of nature had been but little assisted by education or society; the greatest part of his life having been spent under the guidance of an illiterate and miserly father; and though he belonged to one of the universities, he had merely kept the necessary terms, without forming at it any useful acquaintance. The subjection in which his father had brought him up had given him originally great humility of manner; but it was now a good deal counteracted by the self-conceit of a weak head, living in retirement, and the consequential feelings of early and unexpected prosperity. A fortunate chance had recommended him to Lady Catherine de Bourgh when the living of Hunsford was vacant; and the respect which he felt for her high rank, and his veneration for her as his patroness, mingling with a very good opinion of himself, of his authority as a clergyman, and his right as a rector, made him altogether a mixture of pride and obsequiousness, self-importance and humility.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz aqlli odam emasdi, tabiatdagi bu kamchilikka esa ta'lim ham, jamiyat ham juda oz yordam bergan edi: hayotining katta qismi savodsiz va xasis otaning nazoratida o'tgan edi; garchi u universitetlardan biriga tegishli bo'lsa ham, u yerda faqat kerakli muddatlarni o'tkazgan, birorta ham foydali tanish orttirmagan edi. Otasi uni tarbiyalagan itoatkorlik dastlab unga katta kamtarlik bergan edi; lekin endi bu xilvatda yashaydigan zaif aqlning o'ziga bino qo'yishi va erta hamda kutilmagan farovonlikning o'zini muhim sanash tuyg'ulari bilan ancha muvozanatlashgan edi. Xansforddagi lavozim bo'shab qolganda, omadli tasodif uni ledi Ketrin de Burgga tavsiya qilgan edi; uning yuksak martabasiga bo'lgan hurmati va homiysi sifatida unga bo'lgan ehtiromi o'zi haqidagi, ruhoniy sifatidagi obro'yi va cherkov boshlig'i sifatidagi huquqlari haqidagi juda yuqori fikr bilan qo'shilib, uni butunlay g'urur va yaltoqlik, o'zini muhim sanash va kamtarlik aralashmasiga aylantirgan edi.

paras.en: Having now a good house and a very sufficient income, he intended to marry; and in seeking a reconciliation with the Longbourn family he had a wife in view, as he meant to choose one of the daughters, if he found them as handsome and amiable as they were represented by common report. This was his plan of amends--of atonement--for inheriting their father's estate; and he thought it an excellent one, full of eligibility and suitableness, and excessively generous and disinterested on his own part.
paras.uz: Endi yaxshi uyi va yetarlicha daromadi bo'lgani uchun u uylanmoqchi edi; Longborn oilasi bilan yarashishga intilganida u xotinni ko'zda tutgan edi, chunki agar qizlarni umumiy mish-mishlarda tasvirlanganidek chiroyli va yoqimli deb topsa, ulardan birini tanlamoqchi edi. Bu uning ularning otasining mulkini meros qilib olgani uchun tovon — gunohini yuvish rejasi edi; u buni ajoyib, har jihatdan munosib va o'z tomonidan nihoyatda saxiy va beg'araz reja deb hisoblardi.

paras.en: His plan did not vary on seeing them. Miss Bennet's lovely face confirmed his views, and established all his strictest notions of what was due to seniority; and for the first evening she was his settled choice. The next morning, however, made an alteration; for in a quarter of an hour's tete-a-tete with Mrs. Bennet before breakfast, a conversation beginning with his parsonage-house, and leading naturally to the avowal of his hopes, that a mistress might be found for it at Longbourn, produced from her, amid very complaisant smiles and general encouragement, a caution against the very Jane he had fixed on. “As to her younger daughters, she could not take upon her to say--she could not positively answer--but she did not know of any prepossession; her eldest daughter, she must just mention--she felt it incumbent on her to hint, was likely to be very soon engaged.”
paras.uz: Ularni ko'rgach, rejasi o'zgarmadi. Miss Bennetning go'zal yuzi uning qarashlarini tasdiqladi va yoshi kattalikka nima tegishli ekani haqidagi eng qat'iy tushunchalarini mustahkamladi; birinchi oqshom davomida u uning qat'iy tanlovi edi. Biroq ertasi tong o'zgarish olib keldi; chunki nonushtadan oldin missis Bennet bilan chorak soatlik yuzma-yuz suhbatda — uning ruhoniy uyi haqida boshlanib, tabiiy ravishda uning uchun bekani Longborndan topish umidlarini izhor qilishga olib kelgan suhbatda — u juda muloyim tabassumlar va umumiy dalda orasida aynan u tanlagan Jeyn haqida ogohlantirish oldi: «Kichik qizlariga kelsak, u hech narsa deya olmaydi — aniq javob bera olmaydi — lekin hech qanday moyillikni bilmaydi; to'ng'ich qizi haqida esa aytib o'tishi kerak — ishora qilishni o'z burchi deb biladi — u, ehtimol, juda tez orada unashtiriladi».

paras.en: Mr. Collins had only to change from Jane to Elizabeth--and it was soon done--done while Mrs. Bennet was stirring the fire. Elizabeth, equally next to Jane in birth and beauty, succeeded her of course.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinzga faqat Jeyndan Elizabetga o'tish qolgan edi — va bu tez orada amalga oshdi — missis Bennet o'choqdagi olovni kovlayotgan paytdayoq. Tug'ilishi va go'zalligi bo'yicha Jeyndan keyin turadigan Elizabet, tabiiyki, uning o'rnini egalladi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet treasured up the hint, and trusted that she might soon have two daughters married; and the man whom she could not bear to speak of the day before was now high in her good graces.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet bu ishorani qalbiga tugib qo'ydi va tez orada ikki qizini erga berishiga ishondi; kecha nomini tilga olishga ham chiday olmagan odam endi uning nazarida yuqori o'rinda edi.

paras.en: Lydia's intention of walking to Meryton was not forgotten; every sister except Mary agreed to go with her; and Mr. Collins was to attend them, at the request of Mr. Bennet, who was most anxious to get rid of him, and have his library to himself; for thither Mr. Collins had followed him after breakfast; and there he would continue, nominally engaged with one of the largest folios in the collection, but really talking to Mr. Bennet, with little cessation, of his house and garden at Hunsford. Such doings discomposed Mr. Bennet exceedingly. In his library he had been always sure of leisure and tranquillity; and though prepared, as he told Elizabeth, to meet with folly and conceit in every other room of the house, he was used to be free from them there; his civility, therefore, was most prompt in inviting Mr. Collins to join his daughters in their walk; and Mr. Collins, being in fact much better fitted for a walker than a reader, was extremely pleased to close his large book, and go.
paras.uz: Lidiyaning Meritonga piyoda borish niyati unutilmadi; Meridan boshqa barcha opa-singillar u bilan borishga rozi bo'lishdi; janob Kollinz esa ularni kuzatib borishi kerak edi — buni undan qutulib, kutubxonasini o'ziga qoldirishni juda istagan janob Bennet so'radi; chunki janob Kollinz nonushtadan keyin uning ortidan u yerga kelgan edi va u yerda, go'yo to'plamdagi eng katta foliantlardan biri bilan band bo'lib, aslida janob Bennet bilan Xansforddagi uyi va bog'i haqida deyarli to'xtovsiz gaplashib o'tirishda davom etardi. Bunday ishlar janob Bennetni nihoyatda bezovta qilardi. Kutubxonasida u doim bo'sh vaqt va osoyishtalikka ishonardi; garchi Elizabetga aytganidek, uyning boshqa har bir xonasida ahmoqlik va manmanlikka duch kelishga tayyor bo'lsa ham, u yerda ulardan xoli bo'lishga odatlangan edi; shuning uchun u janob Kollinzni qizlari bilan sayrga qo'shilishga taklif qilishda nihoyatda tez xushmuomalalik ko'rsatdi; aslida kitobxondan ko'ra sayr qiluvchiga ancha mosroq bo'lgan janob Kollinz esa katta kitobini yopib, borishdan nihoyatda xursand bo'ldi.

paras.en: In pompous nothings on his side, and civil assents on that of his cousins, their time passed till they entered Meryton. The attention of the younger ones was then no longer to be gained by him. Their eyes were immediately wandering up in the street in quest of the officers, and nothing less than a very smart bonnet indeed, or a really new muslin in a shop window, could recall them.
paras.uz: Uning tomonidan dabdabali bo'sh gaplar va amakivachchalari tomonidan xushmuomala tasdiqlar bilan vaqt Meritonga kirgunlaricha o'tdi. Shundan keyin kichiklarning e'tiborini u endi jalb qila olmadi. Ularning ko'zlari darhol ofitserlarni izlab ko'cha bo'ylab kezardi va faqat haqiqatan ham juda chiroyli shlyapa yoki do'kon vitrinasidagi chinakam yangi muslingina ularni qaytara olardi.

paras.en: But the attention of every lady was soon caught by a young man, whom they had never seen before, of most gentlemanlike appearance, walking with another officer on the other side of the way. The officer was the very Mr. Denny concerning whose return from London Lydia came to inquire, and he bowed as they passed. All were struck with the stranger's air, all wondered who he could be; and Kitty and Lydia, determined if possible to find out, led the way across the street, under pretense of wanting something in an opposite shop, and fortunately had just gained the pavement when the two gentlemen, turning back, had reached the same spot. Mr. Denny addressed them directly, and entreated permission to introduce his friend, Mr. Wickham, who had returned with him the day before from town, and he was happy to say had accepted a commission in their corps.
paras.uz: Lekin tez orada barcha xonimlarning e'tiborini ilgari hech qachon ko'rmagan, ko'chaning narigi tomonida boshqa bir ofitser bilan ketayotgan juda janoblarga xos qiyofali bir yosh yigit tortdi. Ofitser Lidiya Londondan qaytishini so'rash uchun kelgan o'sha janob Denni edi va ular o'tib ketayotganda u ta'zim qildi. Notanishning qiyofasi hammani hayratga soldi, hamma u kim bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida o'yladi; iloji bo'lsa buni aniqlashga qaror qilgan Ketti va Lidiya ro'paradagi do'konda biror narsa kerakday bahona qilib, ko'chani kesib o'tishdi va baxtiga, ikki janob ortga burilib aynan o'sha joyga yetib kelganda, ular endigina yo'lakka chiqqan edilar. Janob Denni darhol ularga murojaat qildi va kecha u bilan Londondan qaytgan va, aytishdan xursandki, ularning polkida ofitserlik lavozimini qabul qilgan do'sti janob Uikhemni tanishtirishga ruxsat so'radi.

paras.en: This was exactly as it should be; for the young man wanted only regimentals to make him completely charming. His appearance was greatly in his favour; he had all the best part of beauty, a fine countenance, a good figure, and very pleasing address. The introduction was followed up on his side by a happy readiness of conversation--a readiness at the same time perfectly correct and unassuming; and the whole party were still standing and talking together very agreeably, when the sound of horses drew their notice, and Darcy and Bingley were seen riding down the street. On distinguishing the ladies of the group, the two gentlemen came directly towards them, and began the usual civilities. Bingley was the principal spokesman, and Miss Bennet the principal object. He was then, he said, on his way to Longbourn on purpose to inquire after her.
paras.uz: Bu aynan shunday bo'lishi kerak edi; chunki yigitni butunlay maftunkor qilish uchun unga faqat forma yetishmasdi. Uning tashqi ko'rinishi uning foydasiga katta ta'sir ko'rsatardi; unda go'zallikning eng yaxshi tomonlari — chiroyli chehra, kelishgan qomat va juda yoqimli muomala bor edi. Tanishuvdan keyin u suhbatga baxtli tayyorlik ko'rsatdi — shu bilan birga mutlaqo to'g'ri va kamtarona tayyorlik; butun davra hali birga turib, juda yoqimli suhbatlashayotgan ediki, otlar tovushi ularning e'tiborini tortdi va ko'cha bo'ylab otda kelayotgan Darsi va Bingli ko'rindi. Guruhdagi xonimlarni tanib, ikki janob to'g'ri ular tomon kelishdi va odatiy xushmuomalaliklarni boshlashdi. Asosiy so'zlovchi Bingli, asosiy e'tibor obyekti esa miss Bennet edi. U, o'zining aytishicha, aynan uning ahvolini so'rash uchun Longbornga ketayotgan ekan.

paras.en: Mr. Darcy corroborated it with a bow, and was beginning to determine not to fix his eyes on Elizabeth, when they were suddenly arrested by the sight of the stranger, and Elizabeth happening to see the countenance of both as they looked at each other, was all astonishment at the effect of the meeting. Both changed colour, one looked white, the other red. Mr. Wickham, after a few moments, touched his hat--a salutation which Mr. Darcy just deigned to return. What could be the meaning of it? It was impossible to imagine; it was impossible not to long to know.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi buni ta'zim bilan tasdiqladi va Elizabetga ko'z tikmaslikka qaror qila boshlagan ediki, ko'zlari to'satdan notanishni ko'rib to'xtab qoldi; Elizabet esa ular bir-biriga qaraganda ikkalasining yuzini tasodifan ko'rib, bu uchrashuvning ta'siridan butunlay hayratda qoldi. Ikkalasining ham rangi o'zgardi: biri oqarib, biri qizarib ketdi. Bir necha lahzadan keyin janob Uikhem shlyapasiga qo'l tekkizdi — janob Darsi bu salomga zo'rg'a javob berishni o'ziga ep ko'rdi. Bu nimani anglatishi mumkin? Tasavvur qilish imkonsiz edi; bilishni istamaslik ham imkonsiz edi.

paras.en: In another minute, Mr. Bingley, but without seeming to have noticed what passed, took leave and rode on with his friend.
paras.uz: Yana bir daqiqadan keyin janob Bingli, bo'lib o'tgan narsani sezmaganday, xayrlashdi va do'sti bilan otda yo'lida davom etdi.

paras.en: Mr. Denny and Mr. Wickham walked with the young ladies to the door of Mr. Phillip's house, and then made their bows, in spite of Miss Lydia's pressing entreaties that they should come in, and even in spite of Mrs. Phillips's throwing up the parlour window and loudly seconding the invitation.
paras.uz: Janob Denni va janob Uikhem yosh xonimlar bilan janob Fillipsning uyi eshigigacha yurib borishdi va keyin, miss Lidiyaning ichkariga kirish haqidagi qattiq iltimoslariga qaramay, hatto missis Fillips mehmonxona derazasini ochib, taklifni baland ovozda qo'llab-quvvatlaganiga qaramay, ta'zim qilib xayrlashishdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Phillips was always glad to see her nieces; and the two eldest, from their recent absence, were particularly welcome, and she was eagerly expressing her surprise at their sudden return home, which, as their own carriage had not fetched them, she should have known nothing about, if she had not happened to see Mr. Jones's shop-boy in the street, who had told her that they were not to send any more draughts to Netherfield because the Miss Bennets were come away, when her civility was claimed towards Mr. Collins by Jane's introduction of him. She received him with her very best politeness, which he returned with as much more, apologising for his intrusion, without any previous acquaintance with her, which he could not help flattering himself, however, might be justified by his relationship to the young ladies who introduced him to her notice.
paras.uz: Missis Fillips jiyanlarini ko'rishdan doim xursand bo'lardi; ikki kattasi yaqinda yo'q bo'lgani uchun ayniqsa xush kelgan edi va u ularning to'satdan uyga qaytganidan hayratini qizg'in bildirayotgan edi — o'z aravalari ularni olib kelmagani uchun, agar ko'chada tasodifan janob Jonsning do'kon bolasini ko'rib qolmaganida, bundan hech narsa bilmagan bo'lardi; bola unga miss Bennetlar ketib qolgani uchun Nezerfildga boshqa dori yubormasliklari kerakligini aytgan edi — shunda Jeyn janob Kollinzni tanishtirdi va xushmuomalaligi unga qaratilishi kerak bo'ldi. U uni eng zo'r xushmuomalaligi bilan qabul qildi, u esa bunga yanada ko'proq xushmuomalalik bilan javob berdi va u bilan oldindan tanish bo'lmay turib kirib kelgani uchun uzr so'radi; biroq u buni uni u bilan tanishtirgan yosh xonimlarga qarindoshligi oqlashi mumkin, deb o'zini ovutmay qololmadi.

paras.en: Mrs. Phillips was quite awed by such an excess of good breeding; but her contemplation of one stranger was soon put to an end by exclamations and inquiries about the other; of whom, however, she could only tell her nieces what they already knew, that Mr. Denny had brought him from London, and that he was to have a lieutenant's commission in the ----shire. She had been watching him the last hour, she said, as he walked up and down the street, and had Mr. Wickham appeared, Kitty and Lydia would certainly have continued the occupation, but unluckily no one passed windows now except a few of the officers, who, in comparison with the stranger, were become “stupid, disagreeable fellows.”
paras.uz: Missis Fillips bunday ortiqcha yaxshi tarbiyadan butunlay hayratga tushdi; lekin uning bir notanishni kuzatishi tez orada ikkinchisi haqidagi xitoblar va so'roqlar bilan to'xtadi; biroq u haqida u jiyanlariga ular allaqachon bilgan narsalarnigina — janob Denni uni Londondan olib kelganini va u ----shir polkida leytenant lavozimini olishini aytib bera oldi. U oxirgi bir soat davomida uning ko'chada u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurganini kuzatib turganini aytdi va agar janob Uikhem ko'ringanida, Ketti va Lidiya bu mashg'ulotni albatta davom ettirgan bo'lardi, lekin afsuski, endi derazalar yonidan bir nechta ofitserdan boshqa hech kim o'tmasdi, ular esa notanish bilan solishtirganda «ahmoq, yoqimsiz yigitlar»ga aylanib qolgan edi.

paras.en: Some of them were to dine with the Phillipses the next day, and their aunt promised to make her husband call on Mr. Wickham, and give him an invitation also, if the family from Longbourn would come in the evening. This was agreed to, and Mrs. Phillips protested that they would have a nice comfortable noisy game of lottery tickets, and a little bit of hot supper afterwards. The prospect of such delights was very cheering, and they parted in mutual good spirits. Mr. Collins repeated his apologies in quitting the room, and was assured with unwearying civility that they were perfectly needless.
paras.uz: Ulardan ba'zilari ertasi kuni Fillipslarnikida tushlik qilishlari kerak edi va xolalari, agar Longborn oilasi kechqurun kelsa, erini janob Uikhemning oldiga borib, uni ham taklif qilishga majbur qilishga va'da berdi. Bunga kelishildi va missis Fillips ular yoqimli, qulay va shovqinli lotereya chiptalari o'yinini o'ynashlarini, keyin esa ozgina issiq kechki ovqat bo'lishini ta'kidladi. Bunday zavqlar istiqboli juda quvontirdi va ular o'zaro yaxshi kayfiyatda ajralishdi. Janob Kollinz xonadan chiqayotib uzrlarini takrorladi va unga charchamas xushmuomalalik bilan ular mutlaqo keraksiz ekaniga ishontirildi.

paras.en: As they walked home, Elizabeth related to Jane what she had seen pass between the two gentlemen; but though Jane would have defended either or both, had they appeared to be in the wrong, she could no more explain such behaviour than her sister.
paras.uz: Uyga qaytishayotganda Elizabet Jeynga ikki janob o'rtasida ko'rganlarini aytib berdi; lekin Jeyn, agar ular aybdor ko'rinsa, ikkalasini ham yoki har birini himoya qilgan bo'lsa ham, bunday xatti-harakatni singlisidan ortiq tushuntira olmadi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins on his return highly gratified Mrs. Bennet by admiring Mrs. Phillips's manners and politeness. He protested that, except Lady Catherine and her daughter, he had never seen a more elegant woman; for she had not only received him with the utmost civility, but even pointedly included him in her invitation for the next evening, although utterly unknown to her before. Something, he supposed, might be attributed to his connection with them, but yet he had never met with so much attention in the whole course of his life.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz qaytgach, missis Fillipsning muomalasi va xushmuomalaligiga mahliyo bo'lib, missis Bennetni juda mamnun qildi. U ledi Ketrin va uning qizini hisobga olmaganda, hech qachon bundan nafisroq ayolni ko'rmaganini ta'kidladi; chunki u uni nafaqat eng katta xushmuomalalik bilan qabul qilgan, balki ilgari unga mutlaqo notanish bo'lsa ham, uni ertangi oqshomga taklifiga alohida qo'shgan edi. Uning fikricha, nimanidir u bilan qarindoshligiga bog'lash mumkin edi, lekin baribir u butun umri davomida bunchalik ko'p e'tibor ko'rmagan edi.
