chapters.title: Wickham's Story
chapters.recap_uz: Uikhem Elizabetga Darsining otasi unga ruhoniylik lavozimini va'da qilganini, lekin Darsi bu va'dani bajarmay, uni kambag'al qoldirganini aytadi. Elizabet unga ishonadi.

paras.en: As no objection was made to the young people's engagement with their aunt, and all Mr. Collins's scruples of leaving Mr. and Mrs. Bennet for a single evening during his visit were most steadily resisted, the coach conveyed him and his five cousins at a suitable hour to Meryton; and the girls had the pleasure of hearing, as they entered the drawing-room, that Mr. Wickham had accepted their uncle's invitation, and was then in the house.
paras.uz: Yoshlarning xolalari bilan kelishuviga hech qanday e'tiroz bildirilmagani va janob Kollinzning tashrifi davomida janob va missis Bennetni birorta oqshom yolg'iz qoldirish haqidagi barcha ikkilanishlari qat'iyat bilan rad etilgani sababli, kareta uni va besh amakivachchasini munosib soatda Meritonga olib bordi; qizlar esa mehmonxonaga kirisharkan, janob Uikhem amakilarining taklifini qabul qilgani va hozir uyda ekanini eshitib xursand bo'lishdi.

paras.en: When this information was given, and they had all taken their seats, Mr. Collins was at leisure to look around him and admire, and he was so much struck with the size and furniture of the apartment, that he declared he might almost have supposed himself in the small summer breakfast parlour at Rosings; a comparison that did not at first convey much gratification; but when Mrs. Phillips understood from him what Rosings was, and who was its proprietor--when she had listened to the description of only one of Lady Catherine's drawing-rooms, and found that the chimney-piece alone had cost eight hundred pounds, she felt all the force of the compliment, and would hardly have resented a comparison with the housekeeper's room.
paras.uz: Bu xabar aytilib, hammalari joylashib olgach, janob Kollinz atrofga qarab, zavqlanishga fursat topdi; xonaning kattaligi va jihozlari uni shunchalik hayratga soldiki, u o'zini deyarli Rozingsdagi kichkina yozgi nonushta xonasida turgandek his qilishi mumkinligini aytdi; bu taqqoslash dastlab unchalik mamnuniyat bag'ishlamadi; lekin missis Fillips undan Rozings nima ekanini va uning egasi kimligini tushunib olgach — ledi Ketrinning faqat bitta mehmonxonasi tasvirini tinglab, birgina kamin sakkiz yuz funt turganini bilib olgach — iltifotning butun kuchini his qildi va hatto uy bekasi xonasi bilan taqqoslashdan ham ranjimagan bo'lardi.

paras.en: In describing to her all the grandeur of Lady Catherine and her mansion, with occasional digressions in praise of his own humble abode, and the improvements it was receiving, he was happily employed until the gentlemen joined them; and he found in Mrs. Phillips a very attentive listener, whose opinion of his consequence increased with what she heard, and who was resolving to retail it all among her neighbours as soon as she could. To the girls, who could not listen to their cousin, and who had nothing to do but to wish for an instrument, and examine their own indifferent imitations of china on the mantelpiece, the interval of waiting appeared very long. It was over at last, however.
paras.uz: Unga ledi Ketrin va uning saroyining butun ulug'vorligini tasvirlab, vaqti-vaqti bilan o'zining kamtarona maskanini va unda qilinayotgan yaxshilanishlarni maqtashga chalg'ib, u janoblar ularga qo'shilgunicha baxtli band bo'ldi; missis Fillipsda esa juda diqqatli tinglovchini topdi — eshitganlari bilan uning obro'si haqidagi fikri oshib bordi va u imkon topishi bilan bularning hammasini qo'shnilari orasida tarqatishga qaror qildi. Amakivachchalarini tinglay olmagan, cholg'u asbobini orzu qilish va kamin tokchasidagi o'zlarining chinniga o'xshatib qilingan o'rtacha buyumlarini ko'zdan kechirishdan boshqa qiladigan ishi bo'lmagan qizlarga kutish vaqti juda uzoq tuyuldi. Biroq nihoyat u ham tugadi.

paras.en: The gentlemen did approach, and when Mr. Wickham walked into the room, Elizabeth felt that she had neither been seeing him before, nor thinking of him since, with the smallest degree of unreasonable admiration. The officers of the ----shire were in general a very creditable, gentlemanlike set, and the best of them were of the present party; but Mr. Wickham was as far beyond them all in person, countenance, air, and walk, as they were superior to the broad-faced, stuffy uncle Phillips, breathing port wine, who followed them into the room.
paras.uz: Janoblar kirib kelishdi va janob Uikhem xonaga kirganida Elizabet uni avval ko'rganida ham, shundan beri o'ylaganida ham zarracha asossiz hayratlanmaganini his qildi. ----shir polkining ofitserlari umuman olganda juda hurmatli, janoblarga xos jamoa edi va ularning eng yaxshilari shu davrada edi; lekin janob Uikhem qomati, chehrasi, qiyofasi va yurishi bilan ularning hammasidan ular ortlaridan xonaga kirib kelgan, keng yuzli, portveyn hidi anqib turgan dimiqqan Fillips amakidan qanchalik ustun bo'lsa, shunchalik ustun edi.

paras.en: Mr. Wickham was the happy man towards whom almost every female eye was turned, and Elizabeth was the happy woman by whom he finally seated himself; and the agreeable manner in which he immediately fell into conversation, though it was only on its being a wet night, made her feel that the commonest, dullest, most threadbare topic might be rendered interesting by the skill of the speaker.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhem deyarli barcha ayollarning nigohi qaratilgan baxtli erkak edi, Elizabet esa u nihoyat yoniga o'tirgan baxtli ayol edi; u darhol suhbatga kirishgan yoqimli tarz — garchi gap faqat kechaning yomg'irli ekani haqida bo'lsa ham — unga eng oddiy, eng zerikarli, eng siyqa mavzuni ham so'zlovchining mahorati qiziqarli qila olishini his qildirdi.

paras.en: With such rivals for the notice of the fair as Mr. Wickham and the officers, Mr. Collins seemed to sink into insignificance; to the young ladies he certainly was nothing; but he had still at intervals a kind listener in Mrs. Phillips, and was by her watchfulness, most abundantly supplied with coffee and muffin. When the card-tables were placed, he had the opportunity of obliging her in turn, by sitting down to whist.
paras.uz: Go'zallarning e'tibori uchun janob Uikhem va ofitserlardek raqiblar bo'lganda, janob Kollinz arzimas narsaga aylanib qolganday ko'rindi; yosh xonimlar uchun u, albatta, hech kim emasdi; lekin vaqti-vaqti bilan missis Fillips hali ham uning mehribon tinglovchisi edi va uning hushyorligi tufayli u qahva va bulochka bilan mo'l-ko'l ta'minlandi. Karta stollari qo'yilganda, u vist o'yiniga o'tirib, navbatda uning iltifotiga javob berish imkoniyatiga ega bo'ldi.

paras.en: “I know little of the game at present,” said he, “but I shall be glad to improve myself, for in my situation in life--” Mrs. Phillips was very glad for his compliance, but could not wait for his reason.
paras.uz: «Hozircha bu o'yinni yaxshi bilmayman, — dedi u, — lekin o'zimni takomillashtirishdan xursand bo'laman, chunki hayotdagi mavqeimda...» Missis Fillips uning rozi bo'lganidan juda xursand bo'ldi, lekin sababini eshitishni kuta olmadi.

paras.en: Mr. Wickham did not play at whist, and with ready delight was he received at the other table between Elizabeth and Lydia. At first there seemed danger of Lydia's engrossing him entirely, for she was a most determined talker; but being likewise extremely fond of lottery tickets, she soon grew too much interested in the game, too eager in making bets and exclaiming after prizes to have attention for anyone in particular. Allowing for the common demands of the game, Mr. Wickham was therefore at leisure to talk to Elizabeth, and she was very willing to hear him, though what she chiefly wished to hear she could not hope to be told--the history of his acquaintance with Mr. Darcy. She dared not even mention that gentleman. Her curiosity, however, was unexpectedly relieved. Mr. Wickham began the subject himself. He inquired how far Netherfield was from Meryton; and, after receiving her answer, asked in a hesitating manner how long Mr. Darcy had been staying there.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhem vist o'ynamasdi va uni boshqa stolda Elizabet bilan Lidiya o'rtasida mamnuniyat bilan qabul qilishdi. Avvaliga Lidiya uni butunlay egallab oladigandek xavf bor edi, chunki u juda qat'iyatli gapdon edi; lekin lotereya chiptalarini ham nihoyatda yaxshi ko'rgani uchun u tez orada o'yinga shunchalik berilib ketdiki, garov tikishga va yutuqlar ortidan qichqirishga shunchalik ishtiyoqmand bo'ldiki, birorta odamga alohida e'tibor berishga vaqti qolmadi. Shunday qilib, o'yinning odatiy talablarini hisobga olmaganda, janob Uikhem Elizabet bilan gaplashishga bo'sh edi, u ham uni tinglashga juda tayyor edi, garchi asosan eshitishni istagan narsasini — uning janob Darsi bilan tanishligi tarixini — aytib berishlariga umid qila olmasa ham. U hatto o'sha janobni tilga olishga ham jur'at eta olmadi. Biroq uning qiziqishi kutilmaganda qondirildi. Janob Uikhem mavzuni o'zi boshladi. U Nezerfild Meritondan qancha uzoqligini so'radi va javobini olgach, ikkilangan holda janob Darsi u yerda qancha vaqtdan beri turganini so'radi.

paras.en: “About a month,” said Elizabeth; and then, unwilling to let the subject drop, added, “He is a man of very large property in Derbyshire, I understand.”
paras.uz: «Bir oyga yaqin», — dedi Elizabet; keyin mavzuni to'xtatishni istamay, qo'shib qo'ydi: «Bilishimcha, u Derbishirda juda katta mulkka ega».

paras.en: “Yes,” replied Mr. Wickham; “his estate there is a noble one. A clear ten thousand per annum. You could not have met with a person more capable of giving you certain information on that head than myself, for I have been connected with his family in a particular manner from my infancy.”
paras.uz: «Ha, — javob berdi janob Uikhem, — u yerdagi mulki ajoyib. Yiliga sof o'n ming. Bu haqda sizga mendan ko'ra aniqroq ma'lumot bera oladigan odamni uchrata olmasdingiz, chunki men go'dakligimdan uning oilasi bilan alohida tarzda bog'langanman».

paras.en: Elizabeth could not but look surprised.
paras.uz: Elizabet hayratlanmay qololmadi.

paras.en: “You may well be surprised, Miss Bennet, at such an assertion, after seeing, as you probably might, the very cold manner of our meeting yesterday. Are you much acquainted with Mr. Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Bunday gapdan hayratlanishingiz tabiiy, miss Bennet, ayniqsa kecha uchrashuvimizning juda sovuq tarzini ko'rgan bo'lsangiz. Siz janob Darsi bilan yaqindan tanishmisiz?»

paras.en: “As much as I ever wish to be,” cried Elizabeth very warmly. “I have spent four days in the same house with him, and I think him very disagreeable.”
paras.uz: «Hech qachon istaganimdan ortiq emas, — qizg'in xitob qildi Elizabet. — U bilan bir uyda to'rt kun o'tkazdim va uni juda yoqimsiz odam deb hisoblayman».

paras.en: “I have no right to give my opinion,” said Wickham, “as to his being agreeable or otherwise. I am not qualified to form one. I have known him too long and too well to be a fair judge. It is impossible for me to be impartial. But I believe your opinion of him would in general astonish--and perhaps you would not express it quite so strongly anywhere else. Here you are in your own family.”
paras.uz: «Uning yoqimli yoki aksincha ekani haqida fikr bildirishga haqqim yo'q, — dedi Uikhem. — Bunday fikr chiqarishga loyiq emasman. Uni haddan tashqari uzoq va haddan tashqari yaxshi bilaman, shuning uchun adolatli hakam bo'la olmayman. Men uchun xolis bo'lish imkonsiz. Lekin o'ylaymanki, uning haqidagi fikringiz umuman olganda ko'pchilikni hayratga solardi — va ehtimol, boshqa joyda buni bunchalik keskin aytmagan bo'lardingiz. Bu yerda siz o'z oilangiz davrasidasiz».

paras.en: “Upon my word, I say no more here than I might say in any house in the neighbourhood, except Netherfield. He is not at all liked in Hertfordshire. Everybody is disgusted with his pride. You will not find him more favourably spoken of by anyone.”
paras.uz: «Ochig'ini aytsam, bu yerda Nezerfilddan tashqari mahalladagi har qanday uyda aytishim mumkin bo'lgan gapdan ortiq hech narsa demayapman. Uni Xertfordshirda umuman yoqtirishmaydi. Hamma uning g'ururidan nafratlanadi. Hech kimdan u haqida yaxshiroq gap eshitmaysiz».

paras.en: “I cannot pretend to be sorry,” said Wickham, after a short interruption, “that he or that any man should not be estimated beyond their deserts; but with him I believe it does not often happen. The world is blinded by his fortune and consequence, or frightened by his high and imposing manners, and sees him only as he chooses to be seen.”
paras.uz: «Men u yoki boshqa har qanday odam munosib bo'lganidan ortiq baholanmasligidan afsusdaman, deb da'vo qila olmayman, — dedi Uikhem, qisqa sukutdan keyin, — lekin u bilan bu kamdan-kam bo'ladi, deb o'ylayman. Dunyo uning boyligi va mavqeidan ko'r bo'lib qolgan yoki uning yuqoridan qaraydigan salobatli muomalasidan qo'rqadi va uni faqat u o'zi ko'rinishni istagandek ko'radi».

paras.en: “I should take him, even on my slight acquaintance, to be an ill-tempered man.” Wickham only shook his head.
paras.uz: «Hatto qisqa tanishligimga qaramay, men uni jizzaki odam deb bilaman». Uikhem faqat boshini chayqadi.

paras.en: “I wonder,” said he, at the next opportunity of speaking, “whether he is likely to be in this country much longer.”
paras.uz: «Qiziq, — dedi u gapirish uchun keyingi imkoniyatda, — u bu yerlarda yana uzoq qolarmikin?»

paras.en: “I do not at all know; but I heard nothing of his going away when I was at Netherfield. I hope your plans in favour of the ----shire will not be affected by his being in the neighbourhood.”
paras.uz: «Umuman bilmayman; lekin Nezerfildda bo'lganimda uning ketishi haqida hech narsa eshitmadim. Umid qilamanki, uning mahallada ekani ----shir polkiga oid rejalaringizga ta'sir qilmaydi».

paras.en: “Oh! no--it is not for me to be driven away by Mr. Darcy. If he wishes to avoid seeing me, he must go. We are not on friendly terms, and it always gives me pain to meet him, but I have no reason for avoiding him but what I might proclaim before all the world, a sense of very great ill-usage, and most painful regrets at his being what he is. His father, Miss Bennet, the late Mr. Darcy, was one of the best men that ever breathed, and the truest friend I ever had; and I can never be in company with this Mr. Darcy without being grieved to the soul by a thousand tender recollections. His behaviour to myself has been scandalous; but I verily believe I could forgive him anything and everything, rather than his disappointing the hopes and disgracing the memory of his father.”
paras.uz: «Oh, yo'q! Meni janob Darsi quvib chiqara olmaydi. Agar u meni ko'rishdan qochmoqchi bo'lsa, o'zi ketsin. Biz do'stona munosabatda emasmiz va u bilan uchrashish menga doim og'riq beradi, lekin undan qochish uchun butun dunyo oldida e'lon qila oladigan sababdan boshqa sababim yo'q — juda katta adolatsizlik ko'rganim hissi va uning shunday odam ekanidan eng og'riqli afsus. Uning otasi, miss Bennet, marhum janob Darsi, dunyodagi eng yaxshi odamlardan biri va menda bo'lgan eng sodiq do'st edi; bu janob Darsi bilan bir davrada bo'lganimda ming bir mehrli xotiradan qalbim qayg'uga to'lmasdan iloji yo'q. Uning menga nisbatan xatti-harakati sharmandali bo'lgan; lekin chin dildan ishonamanki, uning otasining umidlarini puchga chiqarib, xotirasini badnom qilganidan ko'ra, unga har narsani va hamma narsani kechira olardim».

paras.en: Elizabeth found the interest of the subject increase, and listened with all her heart; but the delicacy of it prevented further inquiry.
paras.uz: Elizabet mavzuga qiziqishi ortib borayotganini sezdi va butun qalbi bilan tingladi; lekin uning nozikligi boshqa so'rashga yo'l qo'ymadi.

paras.en: Mr. Wickham began to speak on more general topics, Meryton, the neighbourhood, the society, appearing highly pleased with all that he had yet seen, and speaking of the latter with gentle but very intelligible gallantry.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhem umumiyroq mavzularda — Meriton, mahalla, jamiyat haqida gapira boshladi, hozirgacha ko'rganlarining hammasidan juda mamnun ko'rindi va jamiyat haqida yumshoq, lekin juda tushunarli xushomad bilan gapirdi.

paras.en: “It was the prospect of constant society, and good society,” he added, “which was my chief inducement to enter the ----shire. I knew it to be a most respectable, agreeable corps, and my friend Denny tempted me further by his account of their present quarters, and the very great attentions and excellent acquaintances Meryton had procured them. Society, I own, is necessary to me. I have been a disappointed man, and my spirits will not bear solitude. I must have employment and society. A military life is not what I was intended for, but circumstances have now made it eligible. The church ought to have been my profession--I was brought up for the church, and I should at this time have been in possession of a most valuable living, had it pleased the gentleman we were speaking of just now.”
paras.uz: «Doimiy jamiyat, yaxshi jamiyat istiqboli, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — ----shir polkiga kirishimning asosiy sababi bo'ldi. Men uni juda hurmatli, yoqimli polk deb bilardim, do'stim Denni esa ularning hozirgi qarorgohi va Meriton ularga ko'rsatgan juda katta e'tibor hamda ajoyib tanishlar haqidagi hikoyasi bilan meni yanada vasvasaga soldi. Tan olaman, jamiyat men uchun zarur. Men umidlari puchga chiqqan odamman va ruhim yolg'izlikka bardosh berolmaydi. Menga mashg'ulot va jamiyat kerak. Harbiy hayot men uchun mo'ljallangan narsa emasdi, lekin vaziyat endi uni maqbul qilib qo'ydi. Mening kasbim cherkov bo'lishi kerak edi — meni cherkov uchun tarbiyalashgan va agar biz hozir gaplashgan janobga ma'qul kelganida, hozir juda qimmatli ruhoniylik lavozimiga ega bo'lgan bo'lardim».

paras.en: “Indeed!”
paras.uz: «Rostdanmi!»

paras.en: “Yes--the late Mr. Darcy bequeathed me the next presentation of the best living in his gift. He was my godfather, and excessively attached to me. I cannot do justice to his kindness. He meant to provide for me amply, and thought he had done it; but when the living fell, it was given elsewhere.”
paras.uz: «Ha — marhum janob Darsi menga o'z ixtiyoridagi eng yaxshi lavozimga keyingi tayinlovni vasiyat qilgan edi. U mening cho'qintirgan otam edi va menga nihoyatda bog'langan edi. Uning mehribonligini munosib ta'riflay olmayman. U meni yetarlicha ta'minlamoqchi edi va shunday qildim deb o'ylagan edi; lekin lavozim bo'shaganda, u boshqa birovga berildi».

paras.en: “Good heavens!” cried Elizabeth; “but how could that be? How could his will be disregarded? Why did you not seek legal redress?”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Lekin bu qanday bo'lishi mumkin? Uning vasiyatini qanday e'tiborsiz qoldirish mumkin? Nega qonuniy yo'l bilan haqqingizni talab qilmadingiz?»

paras.en: “There was just such an informality in the terms of the bequest as to give me no hope from law. A man of honour could not have doubted the intention, but Mr. Darcy chose to doubt it--or to treat it as a merely conditional recommendation, and to assert that I had forfeited all claim to it by extravagance, imprudence--in short anything or nothing. Certain it is, that the living became vacant two years ago, exactly as I was of an age to hold it, and that it was given to another man; and no less certain is it, that I cannot accuse myself of having really done anything to deserve to lose it. I have a warm, unguarded temper, and I may have spoken my opinion of him, and to him, too freely. I can recall nothing worse. But the fact is, that we are very different sort of men, and that he hates me.”
paras.uz: «Vasiyat shartlarida shunday rasmiy noaniqlik bor ediki, qonundan hech qanday umid qilolmasdim. Sharafli odam niyatga shubha qilmagan bo'lardi, lekin janob Darsi shubha qilishni tanladi — yoki uni shunchaki shartli tavsiya deb hisoblashni va men isrofgarchilik, ehtiyotsizlik — qisqasi, har narsa yoki hech narsa bilan unga bo'lgan barcha haqqimni yo'qotganimni da'vo qilishni tanladi. Aniq shuki, lavozim ikki yil oldin, aynan men uni egallashga yetarli yoshga yetganimda bo'shab qoldi va u boshqa odamga berildi; xuddi shunday aniqki, men o'zimni uni yo'qotishga loyiq biror ish qilganlikda ayblay olmayman. Mening qizg'in, ehtiyotsiz fe'lim bor va ehtimol u haqida, unga ham, fikrimni haddan tashqari erkin aytgandirman. Bundan yomonroq hech narsani eslay olmayman. Lekin gap shundaki, biz juda boshqa-boshqa toifadagi odamlarmiz va u mendan nafratlanadi».

paras.en: “This is quite shocking! He deserves to be publicly disgraced.”
paras.uz: «Bu juda dahshatli! U ochiqchasiga sharmanda qilinishga loyiq».

paras.en: “Some time or other he will be--but it shall not be by me. Till I can forget his father, I can never defy or expose him.”
paras.uz: «Qachondir shunday bo'ladi — lekin men tomonidan emas. Otasini unutmagunimcha, men unga hech qachon qarshi chiqa olmayman yoki uni fosh qila olmayman».

paras.en: Elizabeth honoured him for such feelings, and thought him handsomer than ever as he expressed them.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunday tuyg'ulari uchun uni hurmat qildi va ularni ifodalayotganida uni har qachongidan ham chiroyliroq deb o'yladi.

paras.en: “But what,” said she, after a pause, “can have been his motive? What can have induced him to behave so cruelly?”
paras.uz: «Lekin, — dedi u bir oz sukutdan keyin, — uning sababi nima bo'lishi mumkin? Uni bunchalik shafqatsiz harakat qilishga nima undagan bo'lishi mumkin?»

paras.en: “A thorough, determined dislike of me--a dislike which I cannot but attribute in some measure to jealousy. Had the late Mr. Darcy liked me less, his son might have borne with me better; but his father's uncommon attachment to me irritated him, I believe, very early in life. He had not a temper to bear the sort of competition in which we stood--the sort of preference which was often given me.”
paras.uz: «Menga nisbatan to'liq, qat'iy yoqtirmaslik — men buni ma'lum darajada hasaddan deb bilmay ilojim yo'q. Agar marhum janob Darsi meni kamroq yaxshi ko'rganida, o'g'li menga yaxshiroq toqat qilgan bo'lardi; lekin otasining menga g'ayrioddiy bog'liqligi, menimcha, uni hayotining juda erta davridayoq g'ashini keltirgan. Uning fe'li biz o'rtasidagi raqobatga — menga tez-tez ko'rsatiladigan afzallikka bardosh beradigan emasdi».

paras.en: “I had not thought Mr. Darcy so bad as this--though I have never liked him. I had not thought so very ill of him. I had supposed him to be despising his fellow-creatures in general, but did not suspect him of descending to such malicious revenge, such injustice, such inhumanity as this.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsini bunchalik yomon deb o'ylamagan edim — garchi uni hech qachon yoqtirmagan bo'lsam ham. U haqida bunchalik yomon o'ylamagan edim. U umuman o'z hamjinslarini mensimaydi deb o'ylagan edim, lekin bunday g'arazli o'chakishishga, bunday adolatsizlikka, bunday shafqatsizlikka tushadi deb gumon qilmagan edim».

paras.en: After a few minutes' reflection, however, she continued, “I do remember his boasting one day, at Netherfield, of the implacability of his resentments, of his having an unforgiving temper. His disposition must be dreadful.”
paras.uz: Biroq bir necha daqiqa o'ylab, u davom etdi: «Esimda, bir kuni Nezerfildda u o'zining kekini hech qachon unutmasligi, kechirimsiz fe'li bilan maqtangan edi. Uning tabiati dahshatli bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “I will not trust myself on the subject,” replied Wickham; “I can hardly be just to him.”
paras.uz: «Bu mavzuda o'zimga ishonmayman, — javob berdi Uikhem, — unga nisbatan adolatli bo'lishim qiyin».

paras.en: Elizabeth was again deep in thought, and after a time exclaimed, “To treat in such a manner the godson, the friend, the favourite of his father!” She could have added, “A young man, too, like you, whose very countenance may vouch for your being amiable”--but she contented herself with, “and one, too, who had probably been his companion from childhood, connected together, as I think you said, in the closest manner!”
paras.uz: Elizabet yana chuqur o'yga botdi va biroz vaqtdan keyin xitob qildi: «Otasining cho'qintirgan o'g'liga, do'stiga, sevimlisiga bunday munosabatda bo'lish!» U yana «Buning ustiga sizdek yosh yigitga, yuzining o'zi yoqimli ekaningizga kafolat bo'ladigan odamga» deb qo'shishi mumkin edi — lekin «va buning ustiga, ehtimol, bolaligidan uning hamrohi bo'lgan, siz aytganingizdek, eng yaqin tarzda bog'langan odamga!» deyish bilan cheklandi.

paras.en: “We were born in the same parish, within the same park; the greatest part of our youth was passed together; inmates of the same house, sharing the same amusements, objects of the same parental care. My father began life in the profession which your uncle, Mr. Phillips, appears to do so much credit to--but he gave up everything to be of use to the late Mr. Darcy and devoted all his time to the care of the Pemberley property. He was most highly esteemed by Mr. Darcy, a most intimate, confidential friend. Mr. Darcy often acknowledged himself to be under the greatest obligations to my father's active superintendence, and when, immediately before my father's death, Mr. Darcy gave him a voluntary promise of providing for me, I am convinced that he felt it to be as much a debt of gratitude to him, as of his affection to myself.”
paras.uz: «Biz bir qavmda, bir park ichida tug'ilganmiz; yoshligimizning katta qismi birga o'tgan; bir uyda yashaganmiz, bir xil ermaklarni baham ko'rganmiz, bir xil ota-onalik g'amxo'rligida bo'lganmiz. Otam hayotini amakingiz janob Fillips shunchalik sharaf keltirayotgan kasbda boshlagan edi — lekin u marhum janob Darsiga foydali bo'lish uchun hamma narsadan voz kechdi va butun vaqtini Pemberli mulkini boshqarishga bag'ishladi. Janob Darsi uni juda qadrlardi, u eng yaqin, ishonchli do'sti edi. Janob Darsi ko'pincha otamning faol nazoratidan juda qarzdor ekanini tan olardi va otam vafotidan biroz oldin janob Darsi unga o'z ixtiyori bilan meni ta'minlashga va'da berganida, ishonamanki, u buni menga bo'lgan mehri kabi, otamga ham minnatdorlik qarzi deb his qilgan».

paras.en: “How strange!” cried Elizabeth. “How abominable! I wonder that the very pride of this Mr. Darcy has not made him just to you! If from no better motive, that he should not have been too proud to be dishonest--for dishonesty I must call it.”
paras.uz: «Qanday g'alati! — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Qanday jirkanch! Hayronmanki, bu janob Darsining g'ururining o'zi uni sizga nisbatan adolatli qilmagan! Yaxshiroq sabab bo'lmasa ham, u insofsizlikka tushish uchun haddan tashqari mag'rur bo'lishi kerak edi — chunki buni insofsizlik demasdan ilojim yo'q».

paras.en: “It is wonderful,” replied Wickham, “for almost all his actions may be traced to pride; and pride had often been his best friend. It has connected him nearer with virtue than with any other feeling. But we are none of us consistent, and in his behaviour to me there were stronger impulses even than pride.”
paras.uz: «Bu ajablanarli, — javob berdi Uikhem, — chunki uning deyarli barcha harakatlarining ildizi g'ururda; g'urur esa ko'pincha uning eng yaxshi do'sti bo'lgan. U uni boshqa har qanday tuyg'udan ko'ra fazilatga yaqinroq qilgan. Lekin hech birimiz izchil emasmiz va uning menga nisbatan xatti-harakatida hatto g'ururdan ham kuchliroq turtkilar bor edi».

paras.en: “Can such abominable pride as his have ever done him good?”
paras.uz: «Uning shunday jirkanch g'ururi qachondir unga yaxshilik qilganmi?»

paras.en: “Yes. It has often led him to be liberal and generous, to give his money freely, to display hospitality, to assist his tenants, and relieve the poor. Family pride, and filial pride--for he is very proud of what his father was--have done this. Not to appear to disgrace his family, to degenerate from the popular qualities, or lose the influence of the Pemberley House, is a powerful motive. He has also brotherly pride, which, with some brotherly affection, makes him a very kind and careful guardian of his sister, and you will hear him generally cried up as the most attentive and best of brothers.”
paras.uz: «Ha. U ko'pincha uni saxiy va qo'li ochiq bo'lishga, pulini ayamay berishga, mehmondo'stlik ko'rsatishga, ijarachilariga yordam berishga va kambag'allarga ko'mak berishga undagan. Buni oilaviy g'urur va farzandlik g'ururi qilgan — chunki u otasining qanday odam bo'lganidan juda faxrlanadi. Oilasini sharmanda qilganday ko'rinmaslik, xalq sevgan fazilatlardan tanazzulga uchramaslik yoki Pemberli xonadonining ta'sirini yo'qotmaslik kuchli sababdir. Unda akalik g'ururi ham bor, u biroz akalik mehri bilan birga uni singlisining juda mehribon va g'amxo'r vasiysiga aylantiradi va uni odatda eng e'tiborli va eng yaxshi aka deb maqtashlarini eshitasiz».

paras.en: “What sort of girl is Miss Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Miss Darsi qanday qiz?»

paras.en: He shook his head. “I wish I could call her amiable. It gives me pain to speak ill of a Darcy. But she is too much like her brother--very, very proud. As a child, she was affectionate and pleasing, and extremely fond of me; and I have devoted hours and hours to her amusement. But she is nothing to me now. She is a handsome girl, about fifteen or sixteen, and, I understand, highly accomplished. Since her father's death, her home has been London, where a lady lives with her, and superintends her education.”
paras.uz: U boshini chayqadi. «Uni yoqimli deb atay olganimda edi. Darsilar haqida yomon gapirish menga og'riq beradi. Lekin u akasiga haddan tashqari o'xshaydi — juda, juda mag'rur. Bolaligida u mehribon va yoqimli edi, meni nihoyatda yaxshi ko'rardi; men uni ovutishga soatlab vaqt bag'ishlaganman. Lekin endi u men uchun hech kim emas. U o'n besh-o'n olti yoshlardagi chiroyli qiz va, bilishimcha, juda ko'p hunarlarni egallagan. Otasi vafotidan beri uning uyi London, u yerda u bilan bir xonim yashaydi va uning ta'limini nazorat qiladi».

paras.en: After many pauses and many trials of other subjects, Elizabeth could not help reverting once more to the first, and saying:
paras.uz: Ko'p sukutlar va boshqa mavzularga ko'p urinishlardan keyin Elizabet yana bir bor birinchi mavzuga qaytmay va shunday demay qololmadi:

paras.en: “I am astonished at his intimacy with Mr. Bingley! How can Mr. Bingley, who seems good humour itself, and is, I really believe, truly amiable, be in friendship with such a man? How can they suit each other? Do you know Mr. Bingley?”
paras.uz: «Uning janob Bingli bilan yaqinligidan hayratdaman! O'zi xushfe'llikning timsoli bo'lgan va, chin dildan ishonamanki, haqiqatan ham yoqimli janob Bingli qanday qilib bunday odam bilan do'st bo'lishi mumkin? Ular bir-biriga qanday mos kelishi mumkin? Siz janob Binglini bilasizmi?»

paras.en: “Not at all.”
paras.uz: «Umuman yo'q».

paras.en: “He is a sweet-tempered, amiable, charming man. He cannot know what Mr. Darcy is.”
paras.uz: «U shirin fe'lli, yoqimli, maftunkor odam. U janob Darsining qanday ekanini bilmasa kerak».

paras.en: “Probably not; but Mr. Darcy can please where he chooses. He does not want abilities. He can be a conversible companion if he thinks it worth his while. Among those who are at all his equals in consequence, he is a very different man from what he is to the less prosperous. His pride never deserts him; but with the rich he is liberal-minded, just, sincere, rational, honourable, and perhaps agreeable--allowing something for fortune and figure.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, bilmas; lekin janob Darsi xohlagan joyida yoqa oladi. Unda qobiliyat yetishmaydi emas. Agar arziydi deb hisoblasa, u gapga chechan hamroh bo'la oladi. Mavqei bo'yicha unga teng bo'lganlar orasida u kamroq boy odamlar bilan bo'lganidan butunlay boshqacha odam. G'ururi uni hech qachon tark etmaydi; lekin boylar bilan u keng fikrli, adolatli, samimiy, oqilona, sharafli va, ehtimol, yoqimli — boylik va qiyofaga biroz chegirma qilinsa».

paras.en: The whist party soon afterwards breaking up, the players gathered round the other table and Mr. Collins took his station between his cousin Elizabeth and Mrs. Phillips. The usual inquiries as to his success were made by the latter. It had not been very great; he had lost every point; but when Mrs. Phillips began to express her concern thereupon, he assured her with much earnest gravity that it was not of the least importance, that he considered the money as a mere trifle, and begged that she would not make herself uneasy.
paras.uz: Tez orada vist o'yini tugagach, o'yinchilar boshqa stol atrofiga to'planishdi va janob Kollinz amakivachchasi Elizabet bilan missis Fillips o'rtasiga joylashdi. Missis Fillips odatiy tarzda uning muvaffaqiyati haqida so'radi. U unchalik katta bo'lmagan edi; u har bir ochkoni yutqazgan edi; lekin missis Fillips bundan tashvishini bildira boshlaganida, u unga jiddiy salobat bilan bu zarracha ahamiyatga ega emasligini, pulni shunchaki arzimas narsa deb bilishini aytib ishontirdi va xavotirlanmasligini iltimos qildi.

paras.en: “I know very well, madam,” said he, “that when persons sit down to a card-table, they must take their chances of these things, and happily I am not in such circumstances as to make five shillings any object. There are undoubtedly many who could not say the same, but thanks to Lady Catherine de Bourgh, I am removed far beyond the necessity of regarding little matters.”
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi bilaman, xonim, — dedi u, — odamlar karta stoliga o'tirganda, bunday narsalarda omadni sinashlari kerak; baxtimga, men besh shilling biror narsa anglatadigan ahvolda emasman. Shubhasiz, buni ayta olmaydiganlar ko'p, lekin ledi Ketrin de Burgga rahmat, men mayda-chuyda narsalarni hisobga olish zaruratidan ancha yuqoridaman».

paras.en: Mr. Wickham's attention was caught; and after observing Mr. Collins for a few moments, he asked Elizabeth in a low voice whether her relation was very intimately acquainted with the family of de Bourgh.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhemning e'tibori tortildi; bir necha lahza janob Kollinzni kuzatgach, u Elizabetdan past ovozda qarindoshi de Burglar oilasi bilan juda yaqin tanishmi, deb so'radi.

paras.en: “Lady Catherine de Bourgh,” she replied, “has very lately given him a living. I hardly know how Mr. Collins was first introduced to her notice, but he certainly has not known her long.”
paras.uz: «Ledi Ketrin de Burg, — javob berdi u, — unga yaqinda ruhoniylik lavozimini bergan. Janob Kollinz uning e'tiboriga dastlab qanday tushganini deyarli bilmayman, lekin u bilan uzoq vaqtdan beri tanish emasligi aniq».

paras.en: “You know of course that Lady Catherine de Bourgh and Lady Anne Darcy were sisters; consequently that she is aunt to the present Mr. Darcy.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, ledi Ketrin de Burg va ledi Enn Darsi opa-singil bo'lganini bilasiz; demak, u hozirgi janob Darsining xolasi».

paras.en: “No, indeed, I did not. I knew nothing at all of Lady Catherine's connections. I never heard of her existence till the day before yesterday.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, rostdan ham bilmasdim. Ledi Ketrinning qarindoshlari haqida umuman hech narsa bilmasdim. Uning mavjudligini o'tgan kungacha eshitmagan edim».

paras.en: “Her daughter, Miss de Bourgh, will have a very large fortune, and it is believed that she and her cousin will unite the two estates.”
paras.uz: «Uning qizi, miss de Burg, juda katta boylikka ega bo'ladi va u amakivachchasi bilan ikki mulkni birlashtiradi, deb ishonishadi».

paras.en: This information made Elizabeth smile, as she thought of poor Miss Bingley. Vain indeed must be all her attentions, vain and useless her affection for his sister and her praise of himself, if he were already self-destined for another.
paras.uz: Bu ma'lumot bechora miss Binglini o'ylab, Elizabetni jilmaytirdi. Agar u allaqachon boshqasiga mo'ljallangan bo'lsa, uning barcha e'tiborlari, singlisiga bo'lgan mehri va uni maqtashlari haqiqatan ham bekor, behuda va foydasiz edi.

paras.en: “Mr. Collins,” said she, “speaks highly both of Lady Catherine and her daughter; but from some particulars that he has related of her ladyship, I suspect his gratitude misleads him, and that in spite of her being his patroness, she is an arrogant, conceited woman.”
paras.uz: «Janob Kollinz, — dedi u, — ledi Ketrin haqida ham, uning qizi haqida ham yuqori fikrda gapiradi; lekin janoblari haqida aytib bergan ba'zi tafsilotlardan gumon qilamanki, minnatdorligi uni chalg'itmoqda va homiysi bo'lishiga qaramay, u kibrli, manman ayol».

paras.en: “I believe her to be both in a great degree,” replied Wickham; “I have not seen her for many years, but I very well remember that I never liked her, and that her manners were dictatorial and insolent. She has the reputation of being remarkably sensible and clever; but I rather believe she derives part of her abilities from her rank and fortune, part from her authoritative manner, and the rest from the pride for her nephew, who chooses that everyone connected with him should have an understanding of the first class.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, u ikkalasi ham katta darajada, — javob berdi Uikhem. — Uni ko'p yillardan beri ko'rmaganman, lekin uni hech qachon yoqtirmaganimni va muomalasi buyruqbozlarcha va surbet bo'lganini juda yaxshi eslayman. Uning nihoyatda aqlli va zukko degan shuhrati bor; lekin men u qobiliyatlarining bir qismini martabasi va boyligidan, bir qismini hukmron muomalasidan, qolganini esa o'zi bilan bog'liq har bir kishi birinchi darajali aqlga ega bo'lishini istaydigan jiyanidan faxrlanishidan oladi, deb o'ylayman».

paras.en: Elizabeth allowed that he had given a very rational account of it, and they continued talking together, with mutual satisfaction till supper put an end to cards, and gave the rest of the ladies their share of Mr. Wickham's attentions. There could be no conversation in the noise of Mrs. Phillips's supper party, but his manners recommended him to everybody. Whatever he said, was said well; and whatever he did, done gracefully. Elizabeth went away with her head full of him. She could think of nothing but of Mr. Wickham, and of what he had told her, all the way home; but there was not time for her even to mention his name as they went, for neither Lydia nor Mr. Collins were once silent. Lydia talked incessantly of lottery tickets, of the fish she had lost and the fish she had won; and Mr. Collins in describing the civility of Mr. and Mrs. Phillips, protesting that he did not in the least regard his losses at whist, enumerating all the dishes at supper, and repeatedly fearing that he crowded his cousins, had more to say than he could well manage before the carriage stopped at Longbourn House.
paras.uz: Elizabet u buni juda oqilona tushuntirib berganini tan oldi va ular o'zaro mamnuniyat bilan suhbatni davom ettirishdi, toki kechki ovqat kartani tugatib, qolgan xonimlarga ham janob Uikhemning e'tiboridan ulush berdi. Missis Fillipsning kechki ovqatidagi shovqinda hech qanday suhbat bo'lishi mumkin emasdi, lekin uning muomalasi uni hammaga yoqtirdi. Nima desa, yaxshi aytilardi; nima qilsa, nafis qilinardi. Elizabet boshi u bilan to'la holda ketdi. U butun yo'l davomida janob Uikhemdan va u aytib bergan narsalardan boshqa hech narsani o'ylay olmadi; lekin yo'lda uning ismini tilga olishga ham vaqt bo'lmadi, chunki Lidiya ham, janob Kollinz ham bir lahza ham jim turmadi. Lidiya to'xtovsiz lotereya chiptalari, yutqazgan va yutgan fishkalari haqida gapirdi; janob Kollinz esa janob va missis Fillipsning xushmuomalaligini tasvirlab, vistdagi yutqazig'ini zarracha ham hisobga olmasligini ta'kidlab, kechki ovqatdagi barcha taomlarni sanab va amakivachchalarini siqib qo'yayotganidan qayta-qayta xavotirlanib, kareta Longborn uyi oldida to'xtagunicha ulgurishi mumkin bo'lganidan ko'proq gapirishga ega edi.

gloss.ex: The church ought to have been my profession--I was brought up for the church, and I should at this time have been in possession of a most valuable living, had…
I had supposed him to be despising his fellow-creatures in general, but did not suspect him of descending to such malicious revenge, such injustice, such inhumanity as this.”
Elizabeth was again deep in thought, and after a time exclaimed, “To treat in such a manner the godson, the friend, the favourite of his father!”
“Upon my word, I say no more here than I might say in any house in the neighbourhood, except Netherfield.
A military life is not what I was intended for, but circumstances have now made it eligible.
Wickham was therefore at leisure to talk to Elizabeth, and she was very willing to hear him, though what she chiefly wished to hear she could not hope to be…
“I have spent four days in the same house with him, and I think him very disagreeable.”

quiz.q: What does Wickham claim Darcy did?
o: Refused to give him the living promised by Darcy's father
quiz.why_uz: Keyinroq bu hikoya yolg'on ekani ma'lum bo'ladi.

quiz.q: Why does Elizabeth believe Wickham so easily?
o: He is charming and she already dislikes Darcy
quiz.why_uz: Bu — romandagi «xurofot»ning asosiy namunasi.

chapters.title: Jane Doubts
chapters.recap_uz: Jeyn ikkalasini ham ayblashni istamaydi. Bingley Netherfieldda bal e'lon qiladi. Kollinz Elizabetni birinchi ikki raqsga taklif qiladi.

paras.en: Elizabeth related to Jane the next day what had passed between Mr. Wickham and herself. Jane listened with astonishment and concern; she knew not how to believe that Mr. Darcy could be so unworthy of Mr. Bingley's regard; and yet, it was not in her nature to question the veracity of a young man of such amiable appearance as Wickham. The possibility of his having endured such unkindness, was enough to interest all her tender feelings; and nothing remained therefore to be done, but to think well of them both, to defend the conduct of each, and throw into the account of accident or mistake whatever could not be otherwise explained.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni Elizabet Jeynga janob Uikhem bilan o'rtalarida bo'lib o'tgan gaplarni aytib berdi. Jeyn hayrat va tashvish bilan tingladi; u janob Darsi janob Binglining hurmatiga bunchalik nomunosib bo'lishi mumkinligiga qanday ishonishni bilmadi; shu bilan birga, Uikhemdek yoqimli qiyofali yosh yigitning rostgo'yligiga shubha qilish uning tabiatida yo'q edi. Uning bunday shafqatsizlikka duch kelgan bo'lishi ehtimoli uning barcha nozik tuyg'ularini qo'zg'atishga yetarli edi; shuning uchun ikkalasi haqida ham yaxshi o'ylash, har birining xatti-harakatini oqlash va boshqacha tushuntirib bo'lmaydigan hamma narsani tasodif yoki xato hisobiga qo'yishdan boshqa ish qolmadi.

paras.en: “They have both,” said she, “been deceived, I dare say, in some way or other, of which we can form no idea. Interested people have perhaps misrepresented each to the other. It is, in short, impossible for us to conjecture the causes or circumstances which may have alienated them, without actual blame on either side.”
paras.uz: «Ikkalasi ham, — dedi u, — qandaydir biz tasavvur ham qila olmaydigan yo'l bilan aldangan bo'lsa kerak. Ehtimol, manfaatdor odamlar har birini ikkinchisiga noto'g'ri ko'rsatgandir. Qisqasi, ikkala tomonda haqiqiy ayb bo'lmagan holda ularni bir-biridan uzoqlashtirgan sabablar yoki vaziyatlarni taxmin qilishimiz imkonsiz».

paras.en: “Very true, indeed; and now, my dear Jane, what have you got to say on behalf of the interested people who have probably been concerned in the business? Do clear them too, or we shall be obliged to think ill of somebody.”
paras.uz: «Juda to'g'ri, albatta; xo'sh, azizim Jeyn, endi bu ishga aralashgan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan manfaatdor odamlar foydasiga nima deya olasan? Ularni ham oqla, aks holda kimdir haqida yomon o'ylashga majbur bo'lamiz».

paras.en: “Laugh as much as you choose, but you will not laugh me out of my opinion. My dearest Lizzy, do but consider in what a disgraceful light it places Mr. Darcy, to be treating his father's favourite in such a manner, one whom his father had promised to provide for. It is impossible. No man of common humanity, no man who had any value for his character, could be capable of it. Can his most intimate friends be so excessively deceived in him? Oh! no.”
paras.uz: «Xohlaganingcha kul, lekin kulib meni fikrimdan qaytara olmaysan. Eng azizim Lizzi, o'ylab ko'r-chi, otasining sevimlisiga, otasi ta'minlashga va'da bergan odamga bunday munosabatda bo'lish janob Darsini qanday sharmandali holatga qo'yadi. Bu imkonsiz. Oddiy insoniylikka ega bo'lgan hech bir odam, o'z obro'sini qadrlaydigan hech bir odam bunga qodir bo'lmasdi. Uning eng yaqin do'stlari u haqida shunchalik qattiq aldanishi mumkinmi? Oh! Yo'q».

paras.en: “I can much more easily believe Mr. Bingley's being imposed on, than that Mr. Wickham should invent such a history of himself as he gave me last night; names, facts, everything mentioned without ceremony. If it be not so, let Mr. Darcy contradict it. Besides, there was truth in his looks.”
paras.uz: «Janob Uikhem kecha menga aytib bergan o'zi haqidagi bunday tarixni — ismlar, faktlar, hammasi tortinmay aytilgan — to'qib chiqargan bo'lishiga ishonishdan ko'ra, janob Binglini aldashganiga ishonish menga ancha oson. Agar bu shunday bo'lmasa, janob Darsi uni rad etsin. Bundan tashqari, uning qarashlarida haqiqat bor edi».

paras.en: “It is difficult indeed--it is distressing. One does not know what to think.”
paras.uz: «Bu haqiqatan ham qiyin — bu tashvishli. Nima deb o'ylashni bilmaysan».

paras.en: “I beg your pardon; one knows exactly what to think.”
paras.uz: «Kechirasan; nima deb o'ylashni aniq bilasan».

paras.en: But Jane could think with certainty on only one point--that Mr. Bingley, if he had been imposed on, would have much to suffer when the affair became public.
paras.uz: Lekin Jeyn faqat bitta narsa haqida aniq o'ylay olardi — agar janob Binglini aldashgan bo'lsa, ish oshkor bo'lganda u ko'p azob chekishi kerak bo'ladi.

paras.en: The two young ladies were summoned from the shrubbery, where this conversation passed, by the arrival of the very persons of whom they had been speaking; Mr. Bingley and his sisters came to give their personal invitation for the long-expected ball at Netherfield, which was fixed for the following Tuesday. The two ladies were delighted to see their dear friend again, called it an age since they had met, and repeatedly asked what she had been doing with herself since their separation. To the rest of the family they paid little attention; avoiding Mrs. Bennet as much as possible, saying not much to Elizabeth, and nothing at all to the others. They were soon gone again, rising from their seats with an activity which took their brother by surprise, and hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet's civilities.
paras.uz: Ikki yosh xonimni bu suhbat bo'lib o'tgan butazordan aynan ular gaplashayotgan odamlarning kelishi chaqirib oldi; janob Bingli va uning opa-singillari kelasi seshanbaga belgilangan, uzoq kutilgan Nezerfild baliga shaxsan taklif qilish uchun kelishgan edi. Ikki xonim aziz do'stlarini yana ko'rganidan xursand bo'lishdi, uchrashmaganlariga bir asr bo'ldi deyishdi va ajralganlaridan beri u nima qilganini qayta-qayta so'rashdi. Oilaning qolganlariga ular kam e'tibor berishdi; iloji boricha missis Bennetdan qochishdi, Elizabetga ko'p gapirishmadi, boshqalarga esa umuman hech narsa deyishmadi. Ular tez orada yana ketishdi, akalarini hayron qoldirgan chaqqonlik bilan o'rinlaridan turib, go'yo missis Bennetning xushmuomalaligidan qochishga oshiqqandek shoshilib chiqib ketishdi.

paras.en: The prospect of the Netherfield ball was extremely agreeable to every female of the family. Mrs. Bennet chose to consider it as given in compliment to her eldest daughter, and was particularly flattered by receiving the invitation from Mr. Bingley himself, instead of a ceremonious card. Jane pictured to herself a happy evening in the society of her two friends, and the attentions of their brother; and Elizabeth thought with pleasure of dancing a great deal with Mr. Wickham, and of seeing a confirmation of everything in Mr. Darcy's look and behaviour. The happiness anticipated by Catherine and Lydia depended less on any single event, or any particular person, for though they each, like Elizabeth, meant to dance half the evening with Mr. Wickham, he was by no means the only partner who could satisfy them, and a ball was, at any rate, a ball. And even Mary could assure her family that she had no disinclination for it.
paras.uz: Nezerfild bali istiqboli oiladagi har bir ayolga nihoyatda yoqdi. Missis Bennet uni to'ng'ich qiziga hurmat yuzasidan berilgan deb hisoblashni afzal ko'rdi va taklifni rasmiy kartochka o'rniga janob Binglining o'zidan olganidan ayniqsa g'ururlandi. Jeyn ikki dugonasi davrasida va ularning akasining e'tiborida baxtli oqshomni tasavvur qildi; Elizabet esa janob Uikhem bilan ko'p raqs tushishni va janob Darsining qarashi hamda xatti-harakatida hamma narsaning tasdig'ini ko'rishni mamnuniyat bilan o'yladi. Ketrin va Lidiya kutgan baxt birorta voqeaga yoki birorta odamga kamroq bog'liq edi, chunki ularning har biri, Elizabet kabi, oqshomning yarmini janob Uikhem bilan raqs tushishni mo'ljallagan bo'lsa ham, u ularni qanoatlantira oladigan yagona sherik emasdi, bal esa, har holda, bal edi. Hatto Meri ham oilasini bunga hech qanday qarshiligi yo'qligiga ishontira oldi.

paras.en: “While I can have my mornings to myself,” said she, “it is enough--I think it is no sacrifice to join occasionally in evening engagements. Society has claims on us all; and I profess myself one of those who consider intervals of recreation and amusement as desirable for everybody.”
paras.uz: «Ertalablarim o'zimga qolsa, — dedi u, — shuning o'zi yetarli — vaqti-vaqti bilan kechki tadbirlarga qo'shilish qurbonlik emas deb o'ylayman. Jamiyatning barchamizga da'vosi bor; men dam olish va ko'ngil ochish oraliqlarini hamma uchun maqbul deb hisoblaydiganlardan biriman».

paras.en: Elizabeth's spirits were so high on this occasion, that though she did not often speak unnecessarily to Mr. Collins, she could not help asking him whether he intended to accept Mr. Bingley's invitation, and if he did, whether he would think it proper to join in the evening's amusement; and she was rather surprised to find that he entertained no scruple whatever on that head, and was very far from dreading a rebuke either from the Archbishop, or Lady Catherine de Bourgh, by venturing to dance.
paras.uz: Bu safar Elizabetning kayfiyati shunchalik baland ediki, garchi u janob Kollinz bilan keraksiz gaplashmasa ham, undan janob Binglining taklifini qabul qilmoqchimi va agar shunday bo'lsa, oqshom ko'ngilxushligiga qo'shilishni o'rinli deb biladimi, deb so'ramay qololmadi; va u bu borada hech qanday ikkilanmasligini, raqsga tushishga jur'at qilgani uchun arxiyepiskopdan ham, ledi Ketrin de Burgdan ham tanbeh olishdan qo'rqmasligini bilib, ancha hayron qoldi.

paras.en: “I am by no means of the opinion, I assure you,” said he, “that a ball of this kind, given by a young man of character, to respectable people, can have any evil tendency; and I am so far from objecting to dancing myself, that I shall hope to be honoured with the hands of all my fair cousins in the course of the evening; and I take this opportunity of soliciting yours, Miss Elizabeth, for the two first dances especially, a preference which I trust my cousin Jane will attribute to the right cause, and not to any disrespect for her.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, — dedi u, — hurmatli yosh yigit tomonidan hurmatli odamlar uchun berilgan bunday bal biror yomon moyillikka ega bo'lishi mumkin degan fikrda umuman emasman; o'zim raqs tushishga qarshi bo'lishdan shunchalik uzoqmanki, oqshom davomida barcha go'zal amakivachchalarim bilan raqs tushish sharafiga muyassar bo'lishga umid qilaman; va bu imkoniyatdan foydalanib, sizdan, miss Elizabet, ayniqsa birinchi ikki raqsni so'rayman — umid qilamanki, amakivachcham Jeyn bu afzallikni to'g'ri sababga bog'laydi, unga nisbatan biror hurmatsizlikka emas».

paras.en: Elizabeth felt herself completely taken in. She had fully proposed being engaged by Mr. Wickham for those very dances; and to have Mr. Collins instead! her liveliness had never been worse timed. There was no help for it, however. Mr. Wickham's happiness and her own were perforce delayed a little longer, and Mr. Collins's proposal accepted with as good a grace as she could. She was not the better pleased with his gallantry from the idea it suggested of something more. It now first struck her, that she was selected from among her sisters as worthy of being mistress of Hunsford Parsonage, and of assisting to form a quadrille table at Rosings, in the absence of more eligible visitors.
paras.uz: Elizabet o'zini butunlay tuzoqqa tushgandek his qildi. U aynan o'sha raqslarga janob Uikhem taklif qilishini to'liq mo'ljallagan edi; buning o'rniga esa janob Kollinz! Uning shodligi hech qachon bunchalik noo'rin paytga to'g'ri kelmagan edi. Biroq bunga hech qanday chora yo'q edi. Janob Uikhemning va o'zining baxti majburan yana biroz keyinga surildi va janob Kollinzning taklifi iloji boricha xushmuomalalik bilan qabul qilindi. Uning xushomadi undan ham ko'proq narsaga ishora qilgani uchun unga yoqmadi. Endi birinchi marta xayoliga keldiki, u opa-singillari orasidan Xansford ruhoniy uyining bekasi bo'lishga va munosibroq mehmonlar bo'lmaganda Rozingsda kadril stolini to'ldirishga yordam berishga loyiq deb tanlangan edi.

paras.en: The idea soon reached to conviction, as she observed his increasing civilities toward herself, and heard his frequent attempt at a compliment on her wit and vivacity; and though more astonished than gratified herself by this effect of her charms, it was not long before her mother gave her to understand that the probability of their marriage was extremely agreeable to her. Elizabeth, however, did not choose to take the hint, being well aware that a serious dispute must be the consequence of any reply. Mr. Collins might never make the offer, and till he did, it was useless to quarrel about him.
paras.uz: U uning o'ziga nisbatan ortib borayotgan xushmuomalaligini kuzatib, uning aqli va jo'shqinligi haqida tez-tez maqtov aytishga urinishlarini eshitgach, bu fikr tez orada ishonchga aylandi; garchi o'zi maftunkorligining bu ta'siridan mamnun bo'lishdan ko'ra ko'proq hayratlangan bo'lsa ham, ko'p o'tmay onasi unga ularning nikohi ehtimoli o'ziga nihoyatda yoqishini tushuntirdi. Biroq Elizabet ishorani tushunmaslikni afzal ko'rdi, chunki har qanday javob jiddiy janjalga olib kelishini yaxshi bilardi. Janob Kollinz hech qachon taklif qilmasligi mumkin edi va qilmaguncha u haqida janjallashish befoyda edi.

paras.en: If there had not been a Netherfield ball to prepare for and talk of, the younger Miss Bennets would have been in a very pitiable state at this time, for from the day of the invitation, to the day of the ball, there was such a succession of rain as prevented their walking to Meryton once. No aunt, no officers, no news could be sought after--the very shoe-roses for Netherfield were got by proxy. Even Elizabeth might have found some trial of her patience in weather which totally suspended the improvement of her acquaintance with Mr. Wickham; and nothing less than a dance on Tuesday, could have made such a Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday endurable to Kitty and Lydia.
paras.uz: Agar tayyorlanadigan va gaplashadigan Nezerfild bali bo'lmaganida, kichik miss Bennetlar bu paytda juda achinarli ahvolda bo'lardi, chunki taklif kunidan bal kunigacha shunday ketma-ket yomg'irlar yog'diki, ular Meritonga bir marta ham piyoda bora olishmadi. Na xola, na ofitserlar, na yangiliklar izlab bo'lardi — hatto Nezerfild uchun tufli gullarini ham boshqalar orqali olishdi. Hatto Elizabet ham janob Uikhem bilan tanishligini rivojlantirishni butunlay to'xtatib qo'ygan ob-havoda sabr-toqatini biroz sinovdan o'tkazgan bo'lishi mumkin edi; seshanba kungi raqsdan kamroq narsa Ketti va Lidiya uchun bunday juma, shanba, yakshanba va dushanbani chidab bo'ladigan qila olmasdi.
